episodes.label: Prison of Grammar or Spotlight of Words?: The Sapir–Whorf Hypothesis, Linguistic Relativity, and Universal Cognition on Trial — From Whorf's Hopi timelessness myth to modern psycholinguistics; Kay & Kempton's 1984 naming-strategy block & Winawer's 124 ms Russian siniy/goluboy cross-boundary speedup; Regier & Kay's 'Whorf Was Half Right' visual-hemifield synthesis & World Color Survey 110-language universal foci; Boroditsky's Mandarin vertical-time claim vs. January & Kako's 6 null replications; Majid & Levinson's Tzeltal cardinal space vs. Li, Abarbanell, Gleitman & Papafragou's pragmatic disambiguation; Bayesian cue-integration & crossed-random-effects power math plus spotting Whorfian tests in disguise
episodes.notes: Does the grammar and vocabulary of your native tongue quietly build the walls of what you can perceive, remember, and imagine—or do words merely act as transient, online verbal tags laid atop a universal human cognitive architecture? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Linguistic Relativity (the Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis) on full empirical trial across color psychophysics, spatial navigation, and temporal reasoning. Trace how Paul Kay and Willett Kempton rescued empirical Whorfian testing from Benjamin Lee Whorf's discredited Hopi timelessness claims via Tarahumara-versus-English blue-green triads, and audit the Neo-Whorfian surge led by Jonathan Winawer's Russian siniy/goluboy color-discrimination experiments, Terry Regier and Paul Kay's lateralized visual-hemifield synthesis ('Whorf Was Half Right'), Asifa Majid and Stephen Levinson's geocentric spatial rotation studies, and Lera Boroditsky's Mandarin vertical-time priming paradigm. Then examine the devastating universalist and methodological counterstrikes: Regier, Kay, and Richard Cook's World Color Survey proof across 110 unwritten languages that focal color prototypes cluster around universal perceptual optima, David January and Edward Kako's six consecutive failed replications of Mandarin-style vertical-time priming, and Peggy Li, Linda Abarbanell, Lila Gleitman, and Anna Papafragou's field experiments in Chiapas proving Tenejapan Mayan speakers solve egocentric left-right spatial tasks effortlessly once pragmatic ambiguity is removed. Pause twice for Python-verified Bayesian label-feedback cue-integration math and stimulus-sampling power audits, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a field guide for spotting Whorfian versus universalist claims in psycholinguistics and multimodal AI.

theory.canonical_title: Linguistic Relativity (Sapir–Whorf Hypothesis — Strong vs. Weak)
theory.core_claim: The structural categories of a speaker's native language—such as lexical color boundaries, spatial reference frames, grammatical tense, or gender—habitually channel or (in the strong determinist reading) constrain non-linguistic perception, memory, and conceptual thought.
theory.verdict_2026: Strong linguistic determinism (that language strictly imprisons what concepts humans can think) is decisively falsified, whereas a sharply circumscribed, online 'weak' or label-feedback relativity survives under rigorous revision. Replicable effects exist in categorical color discrimination across lexical boundaries (especially in the right visual field / left hemisphere; Regier & Kay 2009), spatial orientation habits (egocentric vs. geocentric frames; Majid et al. 2004), and verbal interference tasks (Lupyan 2020). By contrast, high-profile claims about Mandarin counterfactual reasoning, Piraha numeracy determinism, and pervasive grammatical-gender restructuring have repeatedly failed replication or proved task-artifactual.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Students and interdisciplinary papers habitually conflate 'thinking for speaking' (online verbal coding that vanishes under verbal shadowing) with deep restructuring of non-verbal conceptual architecture. Equally pervasive is citing Whorf's debunked 'Hopi timelessness' or 'Eskimo snow-words' tropes without noting that Berlin & Kay's universal perceptual anchors and Malotki's Hopi documentation refuted strong linguistic determinism decades ago.

historical_evolution.milestone: Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf articulate the principle of linguistic relativity, arguing habitual grammar shapes speakers' segmentation of reality.
Berlin & Kay demonstrate universal focal color constraints across languages, while cognitive universalists (Pinker, Pullum) demolish strong Whorfian determinism.
Neo-Whorfian empirical revival: Majid et al. document geocentric spatial cognition and Regier & Kay ('Whorf Was Half Right') show lateralized lexical color-boundary effects.

Label-feedback predictive processing (Lupyan) reframes effects as transient online top-down linguistic modulation, while large pre-registered replications prune overclaimed grammatical-gender and time effects.

theory.falsification_criteria: Strong linguistic relativity is falsified whenever speakers lacking a lexical/grammatical distinction easily learn or solve non-verbal tasks requiring that concept; weak online relativity is falsified for a given domain if cross-linguistic perceptual differences vanish even without articulatory suppression or fail cross-lab pre-registered replication.

pillars.name: Strong Linguistic Determinism (Language Imprisons Thought)
pillars.claim: Speakers lacking a specific lexical word or grammatical marker are fundamentally incapable of perceiving or reasoning about that underlying concept.

pillars.name: Online 'Label-Feedback' & Lexical Color/Spatial Modulation
pillars.claim: Habitual language labels transiently sharpen online perceptual discrimination across color boundaries (right visual field) and bias spatial coordinate habits (geocentric vs. egocentric).

pillars.name: Deep Non-Verbal Conceptual Restructuring Across Grammar

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree strong Whorfian determinism (Hopi timelessness, Eskimo snow-word myths) is dead, that humans share universal perceptual color anchors and non-verbal reasoning, and that verbal labels clearly influence online attention during speaking.
steelman.theory_a_case: Languages act as real-time top-down predictive cues: Russian speakers with separate words for light/dark blue discriminate across that boundary faster in the language-dominant left hemisphere (Winawer 2007), and geocentric-language speakers automatically maintain compass-aligned spatial memory in non-verbal rotation tasks.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Many headline grammatical-gender object-description and Mandarin-counterfactual Whorfian claims failed independent preregistered replications, and color-boundary speed boosts typically vanish under simple verbal interference (articulatory suppression)—showing transient online label-access rather…
steelman.rival_b_name: Language of Thought / Perceptual Universalism (Fodor-Pinker-Gibson-Kemp)
steelman.rival_b_case: Pre-linguistic infants and animals represent space, number, causation, and color categories before acquiring a single word; cross-linguistic color lexicons themselves optimize universal information-theoretic communicative efficiency over shared human visual physiology (Gibson et al. 2017 PNAS).
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Strict Mentalese encapsulation cannot explain why subtle top-down linguistic labels measurably modulate early visual ERP/V1 discrimination latencies and systematically shift spatial reference defaults across entire populations.

episodes.label: Two Tracks, One Genome — Dual Inheritance Theory, Gene–Culture Coevolution (Boyd, Richerson, Henrich & Laland), the Evershed 2022 Lactase-Persistence Reckoning, Cultural Attraction Theory & Pinker's Critique of Cultural Group Selection
episodes.notes: Why did 129 well-equipped Royal Navy sailors of the Franklin Expedition perish on the exact same frozen Arctic shoreline where Netsilik Inuit families thrived for centuries with the exact same human genome? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Dual Inheritance and Gene–Culture Coevolution Theory on full empirical trial. Trace the mathematical lineage from Cavalli-Sforza and Feldman through Boyd, Richerson, Henrich, McElreath, and Laland; examine the landmark molecular proofs of culturally driven evolution in Perry's AMY1 salivary amylase copy-number expansion and Tishkoff's four convergent African and European LCT enhancer sweeps; and then cross-examine the theory against its three sharpest challengers — Evershed, Davey Smith, and Thomas's 2022 Nature reckoning using 7,000 prehistoric pottery lipid residues and 500,000 UK Biobank genomes showing European dairying preceded the LCT sweep by millennia until famine and pathogen crises struck, Scott-Phillips, Blancke, and Heintz's Paris-school Cultural Attraction Theory challenging replicator-like copying fidelity, and Steven Pinker's evolutionary-psychology assault on Cultural Group Selection. Pause twice for worked quantitative calculations contrasting genetic selective-sweep velocity against cultural logistic diffusion and engineering exact ancient-DNA sample-size power across 500-year temporal bins, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a practical stealth field guide for spotting gene–culture and cognitive-attractor hypotheses hiding inside modern genomics, archaeology, and behavioral papers.

theory.canonical_title: Dual Inheritance & Gene–Culture Coevolution Theory
theory.core_claim: Human behavior and anatomy evolve via two coupled, interacting inheritance tracks: genetic transmission and high-fidelity, biased social learning (prestige, conformist, and payoff biases) that constructs cultural niches capable of altering selection pressures on the human genome.
theory.verdict_2026: Dual Inheritance Theory (DIT) is the dominant quantitative framework in evolutionary anthropology, backed by mathematical population-cultural models and genomic footprints of culturally mediated selection (e.g., AMY1 copy number, high-altitude hypoxia adaptations, and pathogen-response loci). Yet since 2022, ancient DNA combined with archaeological residue analyses has forced substantial mechanistic refinement: even the textbook lactase-persistence (LCT) sweep lagged millennia behind early European dairying and appears driven by episodic famine and enteric-disease mortality rather than milk consumption per se. Simultaneously, Paris-school Cultural Attraction Theory challenges DIT's reliance on replicator-like copying fidelity, prompting hybrid models combining reconstructive cognition with population dynamics.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Authors routinely invoke 'gene–culture coevolution' as a loose synonym for any plastic interaction between diet and physiology, overlooking that true coevolution requires demonstrable allele-frequency change driven by a culturally transmitted trait rather than ecological correlation. Conversely, textbook citations of lactase persistence still repeat the pre-2022 simple dairying-advantage narrative without addressing the multi-millennial lag between milk pottery lipids and the European LCT selective sweep.

historical_evolution.milestone: Cavalli-Sforza and Feldman formulate the first mathematical models of vertical, oblique, and horizontal cultural transmission analogous to population genetics.
Boyd and Richerson publish Culture and the Evolutionary Process, introducing conformist, prestige, and guided-variation transmission biases.
Genomic proofs of convergent LCT enhancer sweeps (Tishkoff) and dietary AMY1 expansion (Perry) anchor gene–culture coevolution in molecular evidence.
Ancient-DNA time series (Evershed 2022) decouple early milk use from LCT selection via famine/pathogen crises, while Cultural Attraction debates refine transmission-fidelity assumptions.

rivals: Narrow Evolutionary Psychology (Massive Modularity / Evoked Culture)
Cultural Attraction Theory (Sperber & Scott-Phillips)
Standard Human Behavioral Ecology (Phenotypic Gambit)
Strict Memetics (Dawkins / Blackmore Replicator Model)
theory.falsification_criteria: The framework would be falsified if ancient-DNA selective sweeps linked to culturally constructed niches (dairying, agriculture, boiling, pastoralism) consistently preceded or occurred independently of the cultural practice, or if human cumulative technologies proved reproducible by naive individuals via asocial trial-and-error without biased social copying.
theory.stealth_support: Your study finds genetic allele-frequency shifts (e.g., metabolic, immune, or digestive sweeps) driven by a socially learned practice, OR shows ecological survival depends on cumulative transmitted technology/norms rather than individual trial-and-error.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study shows the genetic sweep lagged the cultural practice by millennia and required an external ecological/pathogen shock (Evershed-style decoupling), OR shows cultural forms converge via universal cognitive attractors without high-fidelity copying.

head_to_head.theory_a_prediction: High-fidelity cultural practice (e.g., milk consumption, starch cooking) directly creates sustained directional genetic selection immediately following cultural adoption, and cultural phylogenies preserve arbitrary neutral markers via prestige/conformist copying.
head_to_head.rival_b_prediction: Genetic sweeps remain flat during benign cultural adoption and spike only during famine/pathogen mortality bottlenecks; cultural traits rapidly drift toward universal cognitive attractors even across noisy transmission chains.

pillars.name: High-Fidelity Biased Social Learning
pillars.claim: Human cumulative technology depends on prestige-, conformist-, and payoff-biased copying fidelity high enough to preserve opaque, multi-step adaptations across generations.

pillars.name: Direct Cultural-Niche Genetic Selection
pillars.claim: Socially learned subsistence innovations (dairying, starch cooking, agriculture) immediately generate sustained directional selection on the human genome.

pillars.name: Cultural Phylogeny & Group-Level Selection
pillars.claim: Divergent norms and institutions form heritable cultural lineages whose differential survival under intergroup competition drives ultra-social cooperation.

pillars.name: Counteractive Cultural Niche Construction
pillars.claim: Culturally transmitted practices actively reshape selective environments—sometimes buffering genetic selection (fermentation, medicine) and sometimes amplifying it.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree that human survival across extreme ecologies relies on accumulated cultural knowledge and that culturally shaped diets and pathogens have left genuine selective footprints on the human genome (such as AMY1 copy number, high-altitude EPAS1/EGLN1, and immune loci).
steelman.theory_a_case: No individual can independently reinvent kayak aerodynamics, cassava detoxification, or arctic tailoring in a single lifetime; mathematical population-cultural dynamics coupled with biased copying explains both explosive adaptive radiation and convergent genomic sweeps (multiple independent LCT mutations across Europe and East Africa).
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Time-stamped European ancient DNA paired with 6,899 pottery-lipid residues (Evershed et al. 2022) shows millennia of widespread dairying with flat LCT -13910*T frequencies—sweeping sharply only during Bronze Age famine and zoonotic enteric-pathogen crises rather than continuous milk consumption.
steelman.rival_b_name: Ecological-Shock Decoupling & Cultural Attraction Theory (Evershed / Sperber-Scott-Phillips)
steelman.rival_b_case: Human minds reconstruct rather than Xerox cultural traits toward stable cognitive attractors, and genomic sweeps often require acute demographic mortality shocks (famine, plague, migration) rather than gentle everyday dietary habits—explaining why fermented cheese buffered lactose exposure for 4,000 years.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Cognitive attractors alone cannot explain causally opaque, locally arbitrary multi-step technologies (poison-extraction recipes, complex maritime navigation, arbitrary ethnic badges) that naive individuals consistently fail to reinvent without faithful social copying.

flip_scenarios.next_experiment: Quantify interaction terms between raw-milk fermentation rates and Salmonella/pestis burden in structural Granger time-series models.

episodes.label: The Revolution That Wasn't — McBrearty & Brooks's African Middle Stone Age Mosaic, Marean's 164-ka Pinnacle Point Tides & Henshilwood's Blombos Ochre Workshops vs. Klein's 50-ka Neural-Mutation Saltation, Powell & Shennan's Demographic Ratchet & Hoffmann's 65-ka Iberian Neanderthal Cave Art
episodes.notes: Did the modern human mind switch on overnight around fifty thousand years ago through a freak genetic brain mutation that fueled Upper Paleolithic cave art across Ice Age Europe, or did symbolic thought, chemical engineering, and complex weaponry assemble piecemeal across Africa over a quarter-million years? This five-act adversarial deep dive places the Behavioral Modernity debate on full empirical trial. Trace how Richard Klein's saltationist 'Human Revolution' model collided with Sally McBrearty and Alison Brooks's landmark synthesis 'The Revolution That Wasn't,' then walk layer by layer through Curtis Marean's 164,000-year-old intertidal shellfish, pigment, and bladelet discoveries at Pinnacle Point and Christopher Henshilwood and Francesco d'Errico's 100,000-year-old abalone-shell ochre workshop, 77,000-year-old cross-hatched engravings, and 73,000-year-old silcrete drawing at Blombos Cave. Next, cross-examine the three fiercest rival paradigms reshaping paleoanthropology today: Klein's late neurogenetic sweep model, Adam Powell, Stephen Shennan, and Mark Thomas's demographic cultural-ratchet simulation explaining why Still Bay and Howiesons Poort technologies flickered in and out without brain mutations, and Dirk Hoffmann's controversial >64.8-ka uranium-thorium dates claiming Neanderthal authorship of Iberian cave art. Pause twice for Python-verified coalescent sweep math, Gumbel mentor-pool thresholds, and open-system uranium-leaching bias audits, concluding with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment.

theory.canonical_title: Behavioral Modernity "Upper Paleolithic Revolution" vs. Gradual African Mosaic
theory.core_claim: The classical Upper Paleolithic Revolution model claimed fully modern symbolic cognition appeared abruptly around 50–40 ka via a sudden neural mutation, whereas the Gradual African Mosaic model argues symbolic, technological, and social traits accumulated piecemeal across Africa over 300–50 ka and fluctuated with demographic connectedness.
theory.verdict_2026: The abrupt 50 ka Eurocentric 'Upper Paleolithic Revolution' / single-neural-mutation model has been decisively challenged and revised out of mainstream paleoanthropology. Over two decades of African Middle Stone Age excavations—73 ka ochre cross-hatching at Blombos Cave, 142 ka perforated shell beads at Bizmoune, 71 ka heat-treated microliths at Pinnacle Point, and 45–51 ka Indonesian figurative cave art (Sulawesi)—prove symbolic behavior vastly predates European Aurignacian art and was not triggered by a 50 ka genetic switch. Ongoing debate now focuses on whether Neanderthals shared comparable symbolic capacities and how demographic network density (Powell et al. 2009) vs. ecological risk drove the intermittent waxing and waning of complex material culture.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Textbooks and cognitive-science papers still lazily treat European cave art (~40 ka) as 'the dawn of human symbolism' and invoke Richard Klein's 50 ka neural-mutation hypothesis without recognizing that anatomically modern humans were already engraving ochre and manufacturing composite heat-treated tools in Africa >70–100 ka. Conversely, some revisionists equate isolated pigment use with full cumulative symbolic institutions without accounting for preservation bias and demographic ratcheting.

historical_evolution.milestone: Paul Mellars, Chris Stringer, and Richard Klein articulate the 'Human Revolution' model attributing the ~45 ka European Upper Paleolithic package to a late neural reorganization.
Sally McBrearty and Alison Brooks publish 'The Revolution That Wasn't,' cataloging deep African Middle Stone Age roots of blades, ochre, bone tools, and long-distance exchange.
Powell, Shennan & Thomas link cultural complexity bursts to demographic density; Blombos 73 ka drawing (Henshilwood) and 45+ ka Sulawesi art dismantle Eurocentrism.
U-Th dating of putative Neanderthal art (Hoffmann 2018, still debated) and pan-African MSA chronologies cement a non-linear, demographically modulated mosaic of cognitive modernity.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree that complex symbolic ornaments and heat-treated technologies existed in Africa >70–140 ka and figurative art existed in Indonesia by ~51 ka, decisively ending the Eurocentric 40 ka Upper Paleolithic Revolution story.
steelman.theory_a_case: Every hallmark once reserved for European 40 ka caves—pigment engraving, personal beads, bone harpoons, long-distance trade, microlithic blades—appears tens of thousands of years earlier across African MSA sites and fluctuates with paleodemographic population booms and crashes.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Testing whether regional effective population size (Ne) genuinely tracks technological complexity across the archaeological record remains statistically noisy, with some small hunter-gatherer groups keeping intricate toolkits while larger ones do not.
steelman.rival_b_name: Late Cognitive Saltation (Klein) vs. Pan-Hominin Symbolic Capacity (d'Errico-Zilhao)
steelman.rival_b_case: Revisionists like Zilhao and d'Errico point to Neanderthal eagle-talon jewelry, birch-tar adhesives, and Spanish cave pigments (>64 ka) to argue symbolic capacity was even older and shared across archaic hominins—whereas Klein counters that post-50 ka representational proliferation reflects a genuine neurocognitive threshold.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: A 50 ka genetic switch cannot explain 142 ka Moroccan shell beads or 73 ka Blombos cross-hatching, while pan-hominin equivalence struggles with the stark rarity of unambiguous Neanderthal figurative art compared to early Homo sapiens.

episodes.label: Braided Eden and Ghost Genomes — Cann, Stoneking & Wilson's Mitochondrial Eve, Stringer & Andrews's Replacement Synthesis, Green & Reich's Neanderthal & Denisovan Genomes, Hublin's 315-ka Jebel Irhoud Fossils & Ragsdale's Weakly Structured African Stem
episodes.notes: Did Homo sapiens burst out of a single East African valley sixty thousand years ago and wipe every archaic hominin cleanly off the Eurasian map, or did we evolve across a vast, braided African continent before interbreeding repeatedly with Neanderthals and Denisovans? This five-act adversarial deep dive traces the dramatic evolution of the Recent African Origin model from the fierce 1980s Replacement-versus-Multiregionalism wars to modern paleogenomics. Follow Rebecca Cann, Mark Stoneking, and Allan Wilson's 1987 Mitochondrial Eve coalescent tree and Chris Stringer and Peter Andrews's 1988 fossil-genetic synthesis as they overturned Milford Wolpoff's global Multiregional Continuity hypothesis. Then witness the double genomic and paleontological Plot Twist that shattered strict zero-admixture replacement and single-cradle myths alike: Richard Green, David Reich, Matthias Meyer, and Svante Paabo's ancient-DNA breakthroughs proving all non-Africans carry roughly two percent Neanderthal ancestry while Oceanians harbor four to six percent Denisovan DNA, alongside Jean-Jacques Hublin's 315,000-year-old Jebel Irhoud fossils in Morocco and Aaron Ragsdale's 2023 continuous-migration demographic proof of a weakly structured pan-African stem. Pause twice for Python-verified haploid-versus-autosomal coalescent scaling, serial founder bottleneck math, and ABBA-BABA plus recombination-tract dating calculations, then close with a pre-registered Paleolithic Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment and a scientist's field guide to archaic introgression.

theory.canonical_title: Recent African Origin (Out of Africa) with Archaic Admixture
theory.core_claim: All contemporary human populations derive the overwhelming majority of their ancestry from Homo sapiens populations that evolved in Africa and dispersed across Eurasia primarily 60–50 ka, subsequently absorbing minor but functionally consequential genomic introgression from archaic hominins (Neanderthals, Denisovans, and deep African 'ghost' lineages).
theory.verdict_2026: Recent African Origin with archaic admixture stands as the uncontested backbone of human origins, overwhelmingly corroborated by fossil chronologies and thousands of ancient and modern whole genomes. However, strict 'single-point Eden' replacement has been replaced by two major refinements: (1) a pan-African 'weakly structured stem' (African Multiregionalism, Scerri 2018; Ragsdale 2023) rather than one East African cradle, and (2) multiple pre-60 ka dispersals out of Africa plus repeated Neanderthal and Denisovan admixture pulses supplying adaptive immune, metabolic, and high-altitude (EPAS1) alleles.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Many papers still write as if a single homogeneous East African tribe replaced all archaic Eurasian hominins with zero gene flow, or conversely treat 2 percent Neanderthal ancestry as reviving classical global Multiregional Continuity. Equally common is equating the mitochondrial 'Eve' coalescent (~150–200 ka) with a single-couple bottleneck rather than a single gene-tree coalescence within a subdivided continental metapopulation.

historical_evolution.milestone: Cann, Stoneking, and Wilson ('Mitochondrial Eve') and Stringer & Andrews formalize the Recent African Origin replacement model against Multiregionalism.
Svante Paabo's team sequences the Neanderthal (Green et al.) and Denisovan (Reich et al.) genomes, refuting strict zero-admixture replacement.
Jebel Irhoud fossils (~315 ka, Hublin) and pan-African synthesis (Scerri) shift African origins from a single cradle to a braided, subdivided continental metapopulation.
Weakly structured stem demographic inference (Ragsdale 2023) and ultra-ancient Eurasian genomes refine multiple admixture waves and introgression deserts shaped by purifying selection.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree modern humans carry ~2 percent Neanderthal ancestry outside Africa and up to ~5 percent Denisovan ancestry in Oceania, while neutral genetic diversity peaks overwhelmingly in Africa.
steelman.theory_a_name: Recent African Origin With Archaic Admixture (Leaky Replacement)
steelman.theory_a_case: Thousands of ancient genomes prove an overwhelming recent African replacement (~95–98 percent ancestry) paired with targeted archaic gene flow supplying adaptive immune and hypoxia alleles across Eurasia.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Fossil dates outside Africa (Apidima 210 ka, Misliya 180 ka, Tam Pa Ling 80 ka) plus deep African 'ghost' admixture complicate any single tidy 55 ka migration pulse.
steelman.rival_b_name: Classical Multiregional Continuity vs. Strict Zero-Admixture Replacement
steelman.rival_b_case: Assimilation and African-multiregional models rightly foresaw that archaic hominins were not wholly sterile biological aliens and that Homo sapiens emerged across a subdivided continental web rather than one point.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Global Eurasian regional continuity (>50 percent local archaic ancestry) is decisively refuted by whole-genome coalescence showing all non-Africans nest deeply inside African genetic variation.

episodes.label: Slow Harvests & Tame Foxes on Trial — Stiner's Small-Game Pulses, Larson & Zeder's Protracted Niche Construction & Wilkins's Neural-Crest Hypothesis vs. Lord's Canadian Fur-Farm Fox Bombshell, Johnsson's QTL Uncoupling & Hayden's Feasting
episodes.notes: Why did human bands across at least a dozen independent centers abandon mobile hunting to spend millennia tending wild grasses and taming wary animals—and why do dogs, pigs, sheep, and laboratory foxes recurrently develop floppy ears, piebald coats, shorter snouts, and smaller brains? This five-act adversarial deep dive places the Broad-Spectrum Revolution and Mammalian Domestication Syndrome on full empirical trial. Trace how Kent Flannery's Broad-Spectrum Revolution and Mary Stiner's Mediterranean small-game turnover—from slow-reproducing tortoises to fast-rebounding partridges and hares—dismantled V. Gordon Childe's sudden Oasis Neolithic myth, while Greger Larson, Dolores Piperno, Robin Allaby, Michael Purugganan, and Melinda Zeder established protracted multi-millennial niche construction across commensal, prey, and directed pathways. Next, examine Adam Wilkins, Richard Wrangham, and Tecumseh Fitch's celebrated 2014 neural-crest-cell hypothesis claiming tameness selection alone pleiotropically generates the entire mammalian domestication syndrome—then confront the devastating 2020–2021 counterstrikes: Kathryn Lord, Greger Larson, Raymond Coppinger, and Elinor Karlsson's archival proof that Dmitry Belyaev's Siberian silver-fox founders already carried Canadian fur-farm spotting and ear traits before tameness breeding began, Martin Johnsson, Rie Henriksen, and Dominic Wright's quantitative-trait-locus evidence showing tameness and morphology segregate independently, and Brian Hayden's competitive feasting challenge. Pause twice for Python-verified rachis-selection and founder-genetics math, plus a pre-registered wild-founder Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment.

theory.canonical_title: Broad-Spectrum Revolution & Domestication Syndrome Theories of Agriculture
theory.core_claim: Transition to food production emerged via prolonged Late Pleistocene dietary broadening toward lower-ranked plants and fast-reproducing small game (Broad-Spectrum Revolution), followed by protracted human–species niche construction that selected recurrent morphological and behavioral shifts ('domestication syndrome') across crops and animals.
theory.verdict_2026: Protracted, multi-centric niche construction and broad-spectrum foraging form the dominant archaeological consensus for agricultural origins, decisively replacing abrupt 'Neolithic Revolution' single-invention stories. Conversely, the mechanistic 'neural crest cell' unified explanation of mammalian Domestication Syndrome (Wilkins et al. 2014) is actively challenged and narrowed in 2026: genomic scans across dogs, pigs, horses, and experimentally tamed foxes (Lord et al. 2020; Johnsson et al. 2021) show that floppy ears, piebald coats, and cranial gracilization rarely co-occur consistently under tameness selection alone and frequently stem from mosaic, trait-specific selection and drift.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Biology and archaeology papers still cite Belyaev's Siberian silver-fox experiment and Wilkins's neural-crest hypothesis as settled proof that selecting solely for tameness automatically produces the full mammalian domestication syndrome, overlooking Lord et al.'s (2020) historical demonstration that founder foxes already carried coat-color alleles from fur farms. In archaeology, papers still conflate 'domestication' (morphological/genetic change) with 'cultivation' (human management preceding fixation of non-shattering rachises by 2,000–3,000 years).

historical_evolution.milestone: Kent Flannery introduces the Broad-Spectrum Revolution hypothesis, linking Pleistocene demographic pressure to expanded plant and small-prey diets.
Mary Stiner quantifies Paleolithic small-prey turnover, while Melinda Zeder and Dorian Fuller document multi-millennial protracted domestication pathways across >12 global centers.
Wilkins, Wrangham, and Fitch propose mild neural-crest-cell deficits as the shared developmental mechanism underlying mammalian domestication syndrome.
Re-evaluations of the Russian fox archive (Lord 2020) and paleogenomic crop/livestock time series (Fuller, Frantz) replace monolithic domestication syndromes with polygenic, pathway-specific models.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree agriculture emerged slowly over 2,000–4,000 years across independent centers (Fertile Crescent, China, Mesoamerica, Andes, Africa) rather than overnight, and that domesticated mammals share some convergent behavioral reductions in fear and aggression.
steelman.theory_a_name: Broad-Spectrum Protracted Niche Construction & Unified Domestication Syndrome
steelman.theory_a_case: Archaeobotanical chaff sequences prove non-shattering cereals took millennia to fix while humans broadened diets early; meanwhile, shared neural-crest developmental origins offer an elegant hypothesis linking reduced adrenal stress reactivity to craniofacial and pigmentation shifts across mammals.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Lord et al. (2020 TREE) and Johnsson et al. (2021) proved Belyaev's farm-fox founders ALREADY carried Canadian fur-farm coat-color alleles prior to tameness selection, and genomic sweeps across dogs, pigs, and horses rarely show unified neural-crest pleiotropy.

steelman.rival_b_case: Cross-species comparative audits show floppy ears, curly tails, and spotted coats do NOT reliably co-occur across domesticates; instead, humans actively selected distinct aesthetic, meat, wool, and docility loci independently over centuries.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Purely independent trait selection must still explain why mild craniofacial gracilization and reduced brain-to-body ratios recur across so many evolutionarily distant domesticates (dogs, pigs, sheep, mink, guinea pigs) without deliberate human breeding for smaller brains.

episodes.label: Watching From Above — Big Gods & Moralizing Supernatural Punishment (Norenzayan, Shariff & Purzycki), Austronesian Human Sacrifice (Watts), the Retracted 2019 Seshat Nature Bombshell (Whitehouse vs. Beheim), Local Moralizing Spirits (Lightner) & the 2023 Historical Retake
episodes.notes: How did an ape built for face-to-face foraging bands of 50 relatives scale up into anonymous megasocieties of millions thousands of years before police forces or courts existed? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Ara Norenzayan's Big Gods and Moralizing Supernatural Punishment Hypothesis on full empirical trial. Examine the landmark behavioral proof in Purzycki and colleagues' eight-society Nature field experiment measuring 35,400 real-stakes coin allocations across Vanuatu, Fiji, Brazil, Mauritius, Siberia, and Tanzania; confront the dark coercive twin revealed by Watts and colleagues' Nature phylogenetic study of Austronesian ritual human sacrifice stabilizing hereditary inequality; and relive the most dramatic methodological courtroom clash in modern anthropology—Whitehouse and the Seshat consortium's 2019 Nature claim that megasocieties preceded Big Gods, Bret Beheim and colleagues' 2021 forensic audit exposing how recoding pre-literate missing values as zeros manufactured the jump and forced a Nature retraction, Lightner, Bendixen, and Purzycki's 2022 demonstration that small-scale societies already possess local moralizing spirits, and Whitehouse's 2023 corrected Seshat retake. Pause twice for worked quantitative calculations mapping secular gossip collapse across Holocene settlement scales and proving exact missing-data odds-ratio distortion plus Galton-adjusted regional transition power, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a practical field guide for recognizing Big Gods, doctrinal ritual, coercion, and affluence hypotheses hiding in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: Big Gods / Moralizing Supernatural Punishment Hypothesis
theory.core_claim: Belief in omniscient, interventionist, moralizing deities ('Big Gods') culturally coevolved with large-scale societies because supernatural monitoring and punishment suppressed free-riding among anonymous strangers, enabling cooperative polities to outcompete rivals.
theory.verdict_2026: The Big Gods hypothesis remains sharply contested in 2026. Cross-cultural behavioral experiments (Purzycki et al. 2016) reliably show that priming moralizing supernatural punishment increases impartial allocation to distant coreligionists, and Austronesian phylogenetic studies confirm broad supernatural punishment predicts political complexity. However, macro-historical temporal precedence is bitterly disputed: the Seshat Global History Databank initially reported that moralizing high gods appeared only after polities crossed 1 million inhabitants (Whitehouse 2019), prompting a major statistical dispute over missing-data imputation (Beheim 2021) and a retraction/re-analysis cycle that leaves causal priority unresolved.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Authors frequently conflate 'moralizing high gods' (Abrahamic-style supreme creators) with 'broad supernatural punishment' (ancestral spirits, karma, taboo-enforcing local deities), causing spurious falsifications when ancient Mesopotamia, Egypt, or Shang China lack a single omniscient creator yet possess pervasive oath-enforcing pantheons. Others ignore severe ethnographic missingness biases in historical databases when asserting clean causal ordering.

historical_evolution.milestone: Dominic Johnson and Ara Norenzayan & Azim Shariff formulate the Supernatural Punishment Hypothesis linking divine surveillance to human prosociality.
Norenzayan's Big Gods synthesis and Purzycki et al.'s 8-society Nature study show belief in punitive moralizing gods correlates with fairer coin allocations to distant strangers.
Whitehouse et al. analyze 414 societies in Seshat (Nature) and claim moralizing gods follow rather than precede megasocieties, sparking a methodological storm.
Beheim et al. expose coding-missingness artifacts leading to retraction of Whitehouse (2019) and revised Seshat models showing multi-pathway coevolution of ritual, moralizing gods, and statecraft.

theory.stealth_refute: Your study finds complex states (>1M population) emerged millennia before moralizing high gods appeared, or shows economic-game priming fails pre-registered cross-cultural replication.

(2021) proved Whitehouse's famous 2019 falsification rested on…
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Earliest mega-polities in Mesopotamia, Old Kingdom Egypt, Indus Valley, and Shang China achieved monumental urbanization, taxation, and armies centuries before universal moralizing Axial-Age religions appeared—suggesting secular bureaucracy and ritual coercion scaled societies first.

steelman.rival_b_hardest: Pure state-first models struggle to explain why early chiefdoms and trade networks across Polynesia, Silk Road caravans, and pre-state chiefdoms repeatedly harnessed supernatural oath enforcement and costly rituals to sustain cooperation far beyond state police reach.

episodes.label: Unilineal Cultural Evolution (Morgan / Tylor Stages of Savagery–Barbarism–Civilization) — Nineteenth-century cultural evolutionists (E. B. Tylor, Lewis Henry Morgan) posited that all human societies inevitably ascend a single, teleological ladder of universal developmental stages—Savagery, Barbarism, and Civilization—driven by 'psychic unity' and progressive technological mastery.
episodes.notes: Completely superseded and falsified as an empirical theory of human history, yet retained as a vital historical anchor because its covert teleological logic persists across modern social science. Franz Boas dismantled unilineal stage ladders via historical particularism and field ethnography, while contemporary archaeology (e.g., monumental hunter-gatherers at Gobekli Tepe and Poverty Point, seasonal institutional switching, and collapse/devolution cycles) proves human social organization is multilinear, reversible, and deeply contingent. Modern cultural evolution (DIT/cliodynamics) uses branching Darwinian phylogeny rather than Spencerian ladders of 'higher' and 'lower' cultures.

theory.canonical_title: Unilineal Cultural Evolution (Morgan / Tylor Stages of Savagery–Barbarism–Civilization)
theory.core_claim: Nineteenth-century cultural evolutionists (E. B. Tylor, Lewis Henry Morgan) posited that all human societies inevitably ascend a single, teleological ladder of universal developmental stages—Savagery, Barbarism, and Civilization—driven by 'psychic unity' and progressive technological mastery.
theory.verdict_2026: Completely superseded and falsified as an empirical theory of human history, yet retained as a vital historical anchor because its covert teleological logic persists across modern social science. Franz Boas dismantled unilineal stage ladders via historical particularism and field ethnography, while contemporary archaeology (e.g., monumental hunter-gatherers at Gobekli Tepe and Poverty Point, seasonal institutional switching, and collapse/devolution cycles) proves human social organization is multilinear, reversible, and deeply contingent. Modern cultural evolution (DIT/cliodynamics) uses branching Darwinian phylogeny rather than Spencerian ladders of 'higher' and 'lower' cultures.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Even scholars who explicitly reject Morgan and Tylor routinely smuggle unilineal teleology back into papers by treating Elman Service's 'band–tribe–chiefdom–state' typology as an inevitable one-way escalator, or by treating contemporary hunter-gatherers as 'living fossils' frozen at an ancestral Paleolithic stage rather than modern populations with tens of thousands of years of distinct historical adaptation.

historical_evolution.milestone: E. B. Tylor (Primitive Culture) and Lewis Henry Morgan (Ancient Society) codify the triadic Savagery–Barbarism–Civilization evolutionary ladder.
Franz Boas ('The Limitations of the Comparative Method of Anthropology') refutes unilineal convergence, demonstrating independent historical pathways and cultural diffusion.
Julian Steward replaces unilineal ladders with Multilinear Evolution and cultural ecology, though Service's band–tribe–chiefdom–state taxonomy partially revives stage thinking.
Archaeological discoveries of egalitarian monumentalism and branching phylogenetic cultural evolution permanently replace stage-teleology with multi-trajectory historical dynamics.

steelman.settled_ground: Both historical critics and modern cultural evolutionists agree Morgan and Tylor's racist 19th-century Savagery-Barbarism-Civilization ladder is completely false empirically, while recognizing that broad technological complexity has accumulated over the Holocene along branching, reversible paths.
steelman.theory_a_name: Unilineal Stage Evolution (Morgan-Tylor — Historical Superseded Anchor)
steelman.theory_a_case: In its 1870s context, Tylor and Morgan broke away from polygenic biological racism by invoking 'psychic unity of humankind'—arguing all populations share equal innate cognitive capacity and differ solely due to cultural-technological history.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Monumental pre-agricultural sites (Gobekli Tepe, Poverty Point), egalitarian urban megasites (Trypillia), seasonal monarchy-to-egalitarian switching, and documented reversions from farming back to foraging completely shatter any single one-way escalator.
steelman.rival_b_name: Boasian Particularism, Multilinear Ecology & Branching Cultural Phylogeny
steelman.rival_b_case: Human societies evolve like a Darwinian branching bush shaped by ecology, diffusion, political choice, and historical accident—never a Spencerian escalator—and modern phylogenetic methods capture real macro-patterns without teleology or ranking cultures 'higher/lower.'
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Extreme anti-comparative particularism that refuses all cross-cultural quantitative modeling misses genuine convergent regularities (e.g., independent rise of writing, cities, and numeracy across multiple Holocene agricultural cradles).

episodes.label: The Ghost in the Syntax — Universal Grammar & FLN Recursion (Hauser, Chomsky, Fitch & Berwick) vs. Pinker–Jackendoff Adaptationism, Everett's Pirahã Bombshell, Tomasello's Usage-Based Construction Grammar, Christiansen–Chater Brain-Shaped Evolution, Evans–Levinson Typological Diversity & Linzen–Baroni Deep Learning
episodes.notes: How does a three-year-old child who has never attended a grammar class instinctively skip the linearly first auxiliary verb and front the structurally highest main-clause auxiliary to ask 'Is the dog that is chasing the cat barking?' This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Chomskyan Universal Grammar and Usage-Based Construction Grammar on full scientific trial. Trace the dramatic minimalist contraction from rich Principles and Parameters to Hauser, Chomsky, and Fitch's 2002 Science manifesto isolating syntactic recursion (FLN/Merge), follow Steven Pinker and Ray Jackendoff's 2005 adaptationist friendly fire and Berwick, Pietroski, Yankama, and Chomsky's 2011 formal Poverty of the Stimulus defense, and then cross-examine the five-front empirical rebellion: Michael Tomasello's verb-island Usage-Based Construction Grammar, Daniel Everett's Amazonian Pirahã recursion challenge, Morten Christiansen and Nick Chater's evolutionary moving-target proof that cultural grammar shifts 25 to 100 times faster than genes can fix arbitrary parameters, Nicholas Evans and Stephen Levinson's 7,000-language demolition of substantive universals, and Tal Linzen and Marco Baroni's deep-learning reckoning showing neural models learn long-distance syntax without hardwired trees. Pause twice for Python-verified quantitative audits — calculating exact Poisson diagnostic token rarity across child-directed speech, the 340,000x to 515,000x frontier-LLM data-efficiency chasm, clustered child-versus-BabyLM experimental power, and typological universal-falsification sampling curves — then take away a pre-registered BabyLM-budget multimodal Head-to-Head Protocol and a stealth field guide for spotting Universal Grammar battles in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: Universal Grammar (Chomskyan Nativism) vs. Usage-Based Construction Grammar
theory.core_claim: Chomskyan nativism posits an innate, domain-specific biological faculty (Universal Grammar, narrowed in Minimalism to recursive Merge) required to overcome the 'poverty of the stimulus,' whereas Usage-Based Construction Grammar argues syntax emerges from domain-general statistical learning, intention-reading, and cultural-evolutionary adaptation to human memory constraints.
theory.verdict_2026: This foundational schism remains genuinely contested in 2026, though both camps have shifted dramatically from 1980s caricatures. Classical richly parameterized Universal Grammar (Principles and Parameters) has been largely abandoned in face of typological diversity (Evans & Levinson 2009) and Minimalist reduction to a minimal recursive operation (Merge). Meanwhile, developmentally realistic large language models trained on child-scale corpora (BabyLM benchmarks, ~10–100M words) demonstrate far greater acquisition of hierarchical island constraints and agreement than classic Poverty-of-the-Stimulus arguments predicted, sharpening the debate over what minimal innate inductive biases remain uniquely linguistic.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Critics routinely attack 1981 Principles-and-Parameters UG as if Minimalism had not shrunk the innate component to Merge plus interface conditions, while Chomskyan papers often dismiss neural-network and usage-based evidence by conflating massive web-scale LLMs with child-scale distributional learners and ignoring cross-linguistic fieldwork on non-configurational languages.

pillars.name: Poverty of the Stimulus for Hierarchical Syntax

episodes.label: Fire, Gut, and the 400-Calorie Engine — Aiello & Wheeler's Expensive-Tissue Hypothesis, Wrangham's Cooking Hypothesis, Carmody's Mouse Bioavailability Trials, Wonderwerk Cave's 1.0 Ma Ash, Navarrete's 100-Mammal Reckoning, Roebroeks & Villa's 400 ka Hearth Audit & Pontzer's 400 kcal/day Metabolic Acceleration
episodes.notes: How did a medium-sized savanna primate pay the relentless metabolic bill for a tripled brain burning nearly twenty percent of resting energy without starving during Pleistocene dry seasons? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts the Expensive-Tissue Hypothesis and the Cooking Hypothesis of hominin encephalization on full empirical trial. Walk through Leslie Aiello and Peter Wheeler's landmark 1995 sixty-five-kilogram organ ledger trading gastrointestinal tract mass for brain cortex under a fixed primate metabolic ceiling, alongside Richard Wrangham and NancyLou Conklin-Brittain's 2003 thesis casting habitual cooking at 1.9 million years ago as an obligate biological trait. Audit the strongest experimental and geoarchaeological corroborations—Rachel Carmody's controlled mouse feeding trials proving thermal processing unlocks far more net energy from both tubers and lean meat than mechanical pounding alone, and Francesco Berna's microstratigraphic and mFTIR discovery of 1.0-million-year-old in situ wood ash and heated bone deep inside Wonderwerk Cave—before facing three empirical counterstrikes: Wil Roebroeks and Paola Villa's European audit exposing a 1.5-million-year fire vacuum prior to 400,000 years ago, Ana Navarrete, Carel van Schaik, and Karin Isler's 100-mammal fat-free-mass dissection test falsifying the strict brain-versus-gut trade-off, and Herman Pontzer's doubly labeled water study proving humans evolved a 400-kilocalorie-per-day metabolic acceleration over chimpanzees and bonobos. Pause twice for worked quantitative calculations balancing organ wattage, cooking dividends, chewing hours, and taphonomic fire-detection power, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a practical stealth field guide for spotting encephalization and bioavailability tests hiding inside modern nutrition, respirometry, and geoarchaeology papers.

theory.canonical_title: Cooking & Expensive Tissue Hypothesis of Hominin Encephalization
theory.core_claim: Because brain tissue consumes ~20 percent of resting human metabolic energy, hominin encephalization required either an internal energetic trade-off with reduced gastrointestinal tract mass (Expensive Tissue Hypothesis) or a dramatic expansion of net caloric capture through thermal food processing (Cooking Hypothesis) and high-quality carnivory.
theory.verdict_2026: Bioenergetic release via dietary quality, food processing, and cooking remains a core pillar of hominin encephalization models, experimentally validated by murine and human energetic assays showing cooking increases net caloric yield from starch and meat. However, the original zero-sum Expensive Tissue Hypothesis (strict brain-versus-gut trade-off) was refuted as a general mammalian law by Navarrete et al. (2011) and supplanted by Pontzer's Metabolic Acceleration model showing humans evolved a higher total daily energy budget alongside lower locomotion costs and cooperative provisioning. Meanwhile, archaeological evidence of habitual controlled fire prior to ~1.0–0.4 Ma remains sparse relative to early Homo erectus brain expansion at ~1.9 Ma.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely cite Aiello & Wheeler (1995) as unchallenged fact that human brain growth was paid for solely by shrinking the gut while holding basal metabolic rate constant, ignoring both Navarrete's comparative falsification across 100 mammals and Pontzer's doubly labeled water proof that humans expend ~400 kcal/day more total energy than chimpanzees. Similarly, Wrangham's 1.9 Ma cooking timeline is often stated as archaeologically confirmed when secure hearths become abundant only after ~400 ka.

historical_evolution.milestone: Aiello and Wheeler propose the Expensive Tissue Hypothesis, arguing high-quality meat diets shrank the metabolically costly splanchnic gut to fund brain expansion.
Wrangham advances the Cooking Hypothesis (Catching Fire), arguing thermal gelatinization and protein denaturation drove Homo erectus tooth/gut reduction and encephalization.
Carmody et al. prove energetic gains of cooking experimentally, while Navarrete et al. falsify a universal mammal brain–gut trade-off in favor of adipose/locomotor trade-offs.

Pontzer et al. establish human metabolic acceleration (higher TEE than apes), while dental calculus, starch/lipid residues, and Wonderwerk/Gesher Benot Ya'aqov fire studies narrow early thermal processing.

theory.falsification_criteria: Wrangham's early-Homo cooking hypothesis would be falsified if high-resolution pyrogenic biomarkers and heated-sediment records across well-preserved 1.9–1.0 Ma Homo erectus occupation sites systematically show absence of anthropogenic fire while mechanical processing and raw meat alone account for jaw/molar reduction.
theory.stealth_support: Your study shows thermal processing dramatically increases net energy capture and archaeological micro-charcoal/heated-bone evidence pushes habitual fire back past 1.0 Ma.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study falsifies the fixed-BMR gut-vs-brain trade-off across mammals (Navarrete 2011) or shows humans evolved ~400 kcal/day higher total energy budgets than great apes (Pontzer 2016).

episodes.label: Tribes, Markets, and the Stranger's Bargain — Richerson & Boyd's Cultural Group Selection, Soltis's New Guinea Clan Kinetics, Henrich's 15-Society Market & Religion Games, Mathew & Boyd's Turkana Warfare Sanctions, Baumard & Debove's Partner-Choice Markets & Pinker's Individualist Critique
episodes.notes: Why do humans donate blood to anonymous strangers, split windfalls in one-shot economic games, and march into lethal battle alongside hundreds of non-relatives when every other ape restricts costly sacrifice to kin and close grooming partners? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Cultural Group Selection on full empirical trial against individual-level evolutionary rivals led by Partner-Choice Theory, indirect reciprocity, and coalition psychology. Trace how Peter Richerson, Robert Boyd, and Joseph Soltis rescued multi-level selection from George Williams's 1966 genetic critique by showing that conformist social learning and punitive norms drive between-group cultural F_ST more than tenfold above genetic F_ST, while auditing Highland New Guinea clan extinction timescales, Joseph Henrich's landmark fifteen-society market and world-religion behavioral experiments, and Sarah Mathew and Robert Boyd's field investigation of eighty-eight lethal cattle raids among East Africa's decentralized Turkana pastoralists. Then cross-examine the sharpest individualist counterstrikes: Stephane Debove, Nicolas Baumard, and Jean-Baptiste Andre's evolutionary game-theoretic proof that free partner choice and outside options force even dominant actors into fifty-fifty fairness solely to maximize individual fitness, alongside Steven Pinker's dissection of reputational bookkeeping, elite coercion, and folk-group-selection fallacies. Pause twice for Python-verified Price-equation F_ST thresholds, Turkana sanction payoffs, and cluster-randomized cross-cultural statistical power calculations, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a stealth field guide for recognizing multi-level versus partner-choice tests across anthropology, behavioral economics, and historical cliodynamics.

theory.canonical_title: Cultural Group Selection vs. Individual-Selection Explanations of Ultra-Sociality
theory.core_claim: Cultural Group Selection (CGS) holds that because conformist transmission and norm enforcement maintain sharp cultural variance between human groups despite migration, differential group survival, conquest, and prestige-biased institutional copying drove the evolution of large-scale, non-kin human cooperation.
theory.verdict_2026: Whether human ultra-sociality requires Cultural Group Selection or follows from individual-level selection (direct/indirect reciprocity, reputation, and partner choice) remains one of the sharpest fault lines in human evolutionary science. CGS proponents (Richerson, Boyd, Henrich, Turchin) marshal compelling ethnohistorical cases of institutional replacement (e.g., Nuer expansion, Turkana warfare norms) and formal Price-equation models showing cultural F_ST vastly exceeds genetic F_ST. Critics from evolutionary psychology (Pinker, Krasnow, Tooby) and behavioral ecology (West, Baumard) counter that CGS often relabels individual-fitness partner-choice dynamics and struggles to explain why selfish defectors do not invade normative groups from within via payoff-biased learning.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Critics routinely dismiss Cultural Group Selection by invoking George Williams's (1966) refutation of genetic group selection, ignoring that conformist cultural transmission suppresses within-group variation far faster than Mendelian segregation allows. Conversely, CGS advocates often treat any cross-group cultural difference or warfare victory as proof of group-level selection without ruling out individual-level mutualism, coercive elites, or reputation-mediated partner choice.

historical_evolution.milestone: Boyd, Richerson, and Henrich formalize how conformist bias and altruistic punishment create multiple cultural equilibria selectable at the group level.
Mathew & Boyd document Turkana third-party warfare sanctioning, while Pinker ('False Allure of Group Selection') and Baumard et al. (mutualistic partner choice) mount individualist rebuttals.
Richerson et al.'s landmark Behavioral and Brain Sciences target article synthesizes empirical CGS evidence alongside 30+ critical peer commentaries.
Historical-cliodynamics datasets (Turchin) and cross-cultural F_ST benchmarks test intergroup competition against intra-group institutional bargaining and elite coercion models.

pillars.name: High Between-Group Cultural F_ST Exceeds Genetic F_ST
pillars.claim: Conformist transmission and norm enforcement maintain sharp between-group cultural differences despite migration, giving group-level selection genuine traction.

pillars.name: Intergroup Conquest & Institutional Copying Drive Ultra-Sociality
pillars.claim: Differential survival, warfare expansion, and prestige-biased imitation of cooperative institutions drove the rise of non-kin anonymous cooperation.

pillars.name: Individual Reputation & Partner-Choice Sufficiency
pillars.claim: Direct/indirect reciprocity, reputation markets, and mutualistic partner choice explain costly human fairness without invoking between-group selection.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree humans cooperate with unrelated strangers on an unprecedented scale, that conformist cultural inheritance differs fundamentally from Mendelian genetic group selection, and that reputation and norm enforcement matter deeply.
steelman.theory_a_case: Measured cultural F_ST routinely hits 0.1–0.3 (10x higher than genetic F_ST), ethnohistorical records (Nuer expansion, Turkana raid sanctions) show cooperative institutional packages actively displacing rival groups, and individual reciprocity breaks down in 10,000-person anonymous warfare and tax systems.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Within-group payoff-biased social learners should rapidly imitate successful free-riders unless individual-level reputation and coercive policing already make cooperation personally profitable—making it hard to isolate pure group-level causal force.
steelman.rival_b_name: Partner Choice, Indirect Reciprocity & Bargaining Models (Baumard-Pinker-West)
steelman.rival_b_case: Humans evolved exquisite reputational bookkeeping and partner-choice selectivity that turn fairness into an individually optimal long-term investment; many apparent 'group-selected' institutions actually emerge via domestic elite bargaining and mutualistic coordination without intergroup extinction.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Pure partner-choice mutualism struggles to explain self-sacrificial anonymous solidarity in huge multi-ethnic armies, costly religious martyrdom, and third-party sanctioning where the punisher faces severe personal retaliation risk.

episodes.label: Cages of Grain or Councils of Citizens? — Carneiro's Ecological Circumscription, Scott's Mesopotamian Grain Cages, Mayshar, Moav & Pascali's Cereal Appropriability Natural Experiment, Turchin's Afro-Eurasian Cavalry Cliodynamics & Blanton & Fargher's Tlaxcallan Collective-Action Republics
episodes.notes: For over 95 percent of Homo sapiens history, human communities lived without kings, tax collectors, standing armies, or bureaucratic courts—then independently across Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Indus, Northern China, Mesoamerica, and the Andes, monumental states crystallized within a few millennia. Did early states trap farmers inside coercive extraction cages through conquest warfare and confiscated grain, or did citizens and elites bargain to build accountable public infrastructure, courts, and collective defense? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Ecological Circumscription and Coercive Appropriability on full empirical trial against Fiscal Collective-Action and Managerial Governance. Trace how Robert Carneiro's 1970 Science formulation overturned Karl Wittfogel's hydraulic-irrigation determinism by centering exit barriers in circumscribed valleys, reinforced by James C. Scott's Mesopotamian grain-and-corvee synthesis, Peter Turchin's Afro-Eurasian steppe-warfare macrosimulation explaining 65 percent of imperial variance, and Joram Mayshar, Omer Moav, and Luigi Pascali's landmark econometric proof that storable, taxable cereal grains—not sheer caloric land productivity—drove state hierarchy while equally productive root and tuber crops remained stateless. Then cross-examine Richard Blanton and Lane Fargher's 30-polity comparative audit and their excavation of pre-Hispanic Tlaxcallan, a densely populated Mesoamerican urban republic without kings or palaces whose council governance out-resisted the Aztec Empire. Pause twice for Python-verified cereal-versus-tuber tax extraction and fiscal-bargaining calculations, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a field guide for spotting coercive versus collective state-formation tests in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: Ecological Circumscription & Coercive vs. Managerial Theories of State Formation
theory.core_claim: Pristine bureaucratic states emerged when environmentally circumscribed fertile valleys (Carneiro) or taxable, storable cereal surpluses (Scott; Mayshar et al.) trapped populations under coercive extraction and warfare—or alternatively when elites solved collective-action, irrigation, and trade coordination problems (Wittfogel; Service; Blanton & Fargher).
theory.verdict_2026: No single prime mover explains all pristine states in 2026; coercive circumscription, cereal-appropriability models, and collective-action/managerial theories are actively contested across comparative global datasets. Econometric cross-regional tests (Mayshar, Moav & Pascali 2022) strongly support the 'appropriability' thesis—cereals (taxable, storable, easily confiscated) predict early state hierarchy far better than sheer land productivity or root-crop calories. Simultaneously, archaeological excavations at Teotihuacan, Harappa, and Tlaxcallan document large, high-public-goods urban polities lacking autocratic monarchs, proving non-despotic collective-action pathways coexist alongside coercive empires.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely treat 'agricultural surplus' as a sufficient cause of early states, ignoring that high-yield root/tuber societies (e.g., highland New Guinea, Amazonia) generated dense surpluses for millennia without forming tributary bureaucracies because underground tubers resist centralized taxation. Conversely, classical hydraulic-despotism citations ignore that large-scale state irrigation in Mesopotamia and Peru typically followed rather than preceded political centralization.

historical_evolution.milestone: Karl Wittfogel proposes Hydraulic Oriental Despotism (1957); Robert Carneiro counters with Ecological and Social Circumscription (1970 Science) centering warfare and exit barriers.
Elman Service champions managerial redistribution, later modernized into fiscal Collective-Action Theory by Blanton & Fargher (2008) distinguishing autocratic vs. collective polities.
James C. Scott (Against the Grain) and Mayshar, Moav & Pascali (2022 JPE) formalize cereal taxability/appropriability as the decisive lever separating states from stateless farmers.
Multi-pathway syntheses (Turchin Seshat warfare models; Graeber & Wengrow; Feinman) test warfare intensity, fiscal contracts, and ecological traps across 30+ world regions.

pillars.name: Cereal Appropriability & Tax-Legibility State Driver
pillars.claim: Storable, season-synchronized, easily confiscated cereal grains enabled centralized tax extraction and bureaucratic hierarchy far more strongly than underground root/tuber staples.

pillars.name: Ecological Circumscription & Coercive Warfare Monopoly
pillars.claim: Trapped populations in circumscribed valleys facing high exit costs and intense warfare fell under coercive elite extraction (Carneiro).

pillars.name: Non-Despotic Fiscal Collective-Action Urban Pathways
pillars.claim: Large high-public-goods urban states (Teotihuacan, Harappa, Tlaxcallan) also formed through taxpayer bargaining, collective governance, and shared infrastructure without autocratic monarchs.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps reject Wittfogel's rigid hydraulic-despotism determinism (since giant state irrigation usually followed centralization) and agree that sheer agricultural calorie surplus alone does not automatically produce a state.
steelman.theory_a_case: Mayshar, Moav & Pascali (2022 JPE) proved across global archaeological and ethnographic panels that switching from root/tuber calories to easily taxed cereal grains predicts early bureaucratic hierarchy dramatically—showing taxability and exit barriers drove early state extraction.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Monumental cities like Indus Valley Harappa and classic Teotihuacan exhibit standardized urban grids, public drainage, and multi-ethnic housing WITHOUT royal palaces, royal tombs, or despotic iconography—proving states are not solely coercive protection rackets.
steelman.rival_b_name: Fiscal Collective-Action & Managerial Governance (Blanton-Fargher-Feinman)
steelman.rival_b_case: Where states rely on broad internal taxpayer revenue rather than captive external rents (mines, trade chokepoints), rulers must bargain with citizens to supply public goods, courts, and market standards—explaining widespread ancient collective republics alongside autocracies.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Purely voluntary managerial models struggle to explain why early states repeatedly emerged in tandem with fortified walls, mass skeletal war trauma, corvee labor, and coercive grain granaries.

episodes.label: Grooming, Fruit Trees, and the Myth of 150 — Dunbar's 1992 Neocortex-Ratio Regression, Zhou & Sornette's Fractal Social Circles, Lehmann's Grooming Ceiling, Sallet's Macaque MRI Plasticity, DeCasien's 140-Species Frugivory Rebuttal, Muthukrishna & Henrich's Cultural Brain & Lindenfors's 2-to-520 Deconstruction
episodes.notes: Why does the human brain burn twenty percent of our resting metabolic energy while weighing barely two percent of body mass—and can a single neocortex ratio truly cap your personal social circle at one hundred and fifty friends? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Robin Dunbar's Social Brain Hypothesis and 'Dunbar's number' on full comparative, neurobiological, and statistical trial. Trace how Dunbar's landmark 1992 Journal of Human Evolution regression across thirty-six primate genera linked neocortex-to-rest-of-brain volume ratios to mean group size and extrapolated 147.8 humans, reinforced by Wei-Xing Zhou and Didier Sornette's discrete ~3x fractal social layers (5, 15, 50, 150, 500), Julia Lehmann and Amanda Korstjens's twenty-percent primate grooming time-budget ceiling, Jerome Sallet's causal rhesus macaque housing neuroimaging in Science, and Dunbar's 2016 stratified Facebook surveys. Then cross-examine three devastating modern counterstrikes: Alex DeCasien, Scott Williams, and James Higham's phylogenetic generalized least-squares audit across more than 140 primate species proving frugivorous diet—not social group size—predicts brain size once phylogeny and body mass are controlled; Michael Muthukrishna, Michael Doebeli, Maciej Chudek, and Joseph Henrich's formal Cultural Brain Hypothesis unifying adaptive skill learning, group size, and extended juvenile life history; and Patrik Lindenfors, Andreas Wartel, and Johan Lind's 2021 statistical deconstruction proving that phylogenetic prediction intervals around human group size span from 2 to 520 individuals. Pause twice for Python-verified allometric regression, vocal-grooming compression, and out-of-sample log-prediction-interval arithmetic, then leave with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a stealth field guide for spotting brain-evolution and network-ceiling claims across neuroscience, anthropology, and organizational design.

theory.canonical_title: Dunbar's Social Brain Hypothesis & Neocortex-Ratio Group-Size Limits
theory.core_claim: Primate neocortex expansion evolved primarily to track complex social relationships rather than ecological foraging challenges, imposing a cognitive scaling ceiling that predicts an average human personal social network limit of roughly 150 individuals ('Dunbar's number').
theory.verdict_2026: Both halves of Dunbar's framework face fierce empirical contestation in 2026. On the comparative neuroanatomy side, DeCasien et al. (2017) analyzed >140 primate species with phylogenetic controls and found frugivorous diet—not social group size or mating system—was the primary predictor of brain size, reviving ecological-intelligence models (though Shultz & Dunbar counter with pair-bonding and multilevel sociality metrics). On the human group-size side, Lindenfors, Wartel & Lind (2021) demonstrated that phylogenetic extrapolation from non-human primates yields 95 percent prediction intervals spanning 2 to 520 humans, proving that a hard cognitive ceiling of ~150 cannot be derived from neocortex ratios—even if time-budget constraints still produce tiered human social circles around ~5, 15, 50, and 150.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Organizational, network-science, and psychology papers routinely cite '150' as a precise, neuroanatomically proven human cognitive limit, completely overlooking that the 95 percent confidence interval of the primate-to-human neocortex extrapolation spans two orders of magnitude and that empirical human personal-network tiers are equally explainable by finite waking hours (time budgets) rather than neocortical working-memory capacity.

historical_evolution.milestone: Byrne & Whiten ('Machiavellian Intelligence') and Robin Dunbar (1992 JHE) correlate primate neocortex ratio with mean social group size, extrapolating ~150 for humans.
Dunbar formalizes the Social Brain Hypothesis and identifies hierarchical human intimacy layers (~5, 15, 50, 150) across hunter-gatherers, Christmas-card lists, and phone logs.
DeCasien, Williams & Higham (Nature Ecology & Evolution) show diet (frugivory vs. folivory) outpredicts social group size across 140+ primate species.
Lindenfors et al. ('Dunbar's Number Deconstructed') expose massive phylogenetic extrapolation uncertainty, shifting debate toward multi-factor cultural-ecological brain models (Muthukrishna).

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree human personal networks organize into emotionally graded concentric circles (~5 intimate, ~15 close, ~50 friends) constrained strongly by finite time, and that both sociality and diet co-evolved with primate encephalization.
steelman.theory_a_case: Across mammals and birds, pair-bonding and complex multi-level sociality correlate robustly with encephalization, while massive mobile-phone and online-social datasets confirm human active personal ties cluster reliably near ~100–200 despite digital tools removing geographic friction.

steelman.rival_b_name: Ecological Foraging & Cultural Brain / Time-Budget Models (DeCasien-Muthukrishna-Lindenfors)
steelman.rival_b_case: Mapping patchy seasonal fruiting trees (frugivory) and cumulative cultural learning (Cultural Brain Hypothesis) impose fierce spatial-memory and energetic demands that explain primate brain variance cleanly—while empirical ~150 tie counts follow trivially from waking-hour time-budget division without a hard neocortical cap.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Purely dietary foraging models struggle to explain why humans possess specialized dedicated cortical circuits for mentalizing/theory-of-mind (TPJ, mPFC) and why solitary large-brained orangutans vs. hyper-social dolphins show complex social-cognition links.

episodes.label: The Parasite in the Blueprint: Selfish Genetic Elements, Transposon Arms Races, Mutational Hazard, and Molecular Domestication — Why onions carry 5x more DNA than humans; Barbara McClintock's 1950 Ds/Ac maize transposons & the 1980 Nature Selfish DNA revolution (Doolittle & Sapienza; Orgel & Crick); Brennecke & Hannon's germline piRNA ping-pong arms race; Graur's Haldane-Muller mutational-load demolition of ENCODE's 80% functional genome claim; Lynch & Conery's 2*Ne*s Mutational-Hazard drift rival & Chuong, Elde & Feschotte's exaptation of ERVs into placental Syncytins and interferon enhancers; copy-number & drift-barrier math plus spotting intragenomic conflict in disguise
episodes.notes: Why is nearly half of your own human DNA—and over eighty percent of a corn stalk's genome—composed of fractured viral corpses and self-copying genetic hitchhikers? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Selfish Genetic Elements and Intragenomic Conflict on full courtroom trial against organismal-adaptationist genomics and neutral mutational-drift rivals. Journey from Barbara McClintock's 1950 discovery of Dissociation and Activator jumping genes in mosaic maize kernels to the back-to-back 1980 Nature manifestos by W. Ford Doolittle and Carmen Sapienza and by Leslie Orgel and Francis Crick that overturned the phenotype-centric view of the genome and solved the C-value paradox. Audit Julius Brennecke and Gregory Hannon's discovery of germline piRNA genetic-memory clusters ('ping-pong' transposon immunity in Drosophila) alongside Dan Graur and colleagues' devastating Haldane-Muller mutational-load proof that if ENCODE's claimed eighty-percent functional human genome were truly maintained by purifying selection, every human mother would need tens of millions to billions of offspring to survive deleterious mutations. Then cross-examine the two sharpest counter-perspectives: Michael Lynch and John Conery's Science Mutational-Hazard Hypothesis arguing small eukaryotic effective population size passively permits non-coding bloat via genetic drift, and Edward Chuong, Nels Elde, and Cedric Feschotte's synthesis of molecular exaptation from placental Syncytins and RAG1/2 recombinases to primate MER41 interferon enhancers. Pause twice for Python-verified transposition invasion thresholds, Haldane-Muller fertility loads, and Kimura drift-fixation math, then leave with a pre-registered Crucial Experiment protocol and a field guide to intragenomic conflict in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: Selfish Genetic Elements, Transposons & Intragenomic Conflict
theory.core_claim: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic genomes are not harmonious organismal blueprints, but ecosystems hosting autonomous genetic replicators—transposable elements (TEs), meiotic drivers, homing endonucleases, and B chromosomes—that propagate at the expense of host fitness, triggering relentless intragenomic arms races that reshape genome size, chromatin silencing, and speciation.
theory.verdict_2026: Intragenomic conflict and selfish-element dynamics are a dominant, richly substantiated pillar of modern genomics. Roughly 45–50 percent of the human genome (and >80 percent of maize) consists of TE fossils, while KRAB-zinc-finger/KAP1 repressors, piRNA pathways, and rapidly evolving centromeric histones (CenH3 centromere drive) bear unmistakable signatures of host–parasite arms races. Contemporary refinement centers on 'molecular domestication' and exaptation: endogenous retroviruses and transposases have been repeatedly co-opted into indispensable host machinery—including placental Syncytins, adaptive-immune RAG1/2 V(D)J recombinase, neuronal Arc capsids, and interferon enhancers—without overturning their originally selfish parasitic proliferation.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely commit the 'panglossian exaptation fallacy': observing that a handful of TE families were co-opted into enhancers or Syncytin genes and concluding that transposons exist 'for the benefit of the genome' to fuel evolvability, ignoring that millions of TE copies persisted solely via selfish replication despite imposing massive mutational, recombinational, and energetic loads on the host.

historical_evolution.milestone: Barbara McClintock discovers maize 'controlling elements' (transposons); Doolittle & Sapienza and Orgel & Crick (1980 Nature) formalize the 'Selfish DNA' paradigm.
Malik & Henikoff propose Centromere Drive explaining rapid centromeric protein evolution; Burt & Trivers (Genes in Conflict) synthesize meiotic drive, homing genes, and TEs.
piRNA/KRAB-ZNF silencing arms races are decoded; Chuong, Elde & Feschotte document widespread regulatory exaptation of ERVs into innate immunity and pregnancy.
Telomere-to-telomere (T2T) complete genomes illuminate active L1/Alu/SVA dynamics, satellite-repeat meiotic drive, and somatic TE reactivation in aging and cancer.
