pillars.name: Autonomous Selfish Replicators Proliferate Against Host Fitness
pillars.claim: Transposable elements, meiotic drivers, and B chromosomes expand within genomes solely by out-replicating host DNA despite imposing mutational and energetic loads.

pillars.name: Relentless Host-Parasite Intragenomic Arms Races
pillars.claim: Selfish elements trigger ongoing molecular arms races driving rapid positive selection in host silencing machinery (KRAB-ZNFs, piRNA pathways, centromeric CenH3).

pillars.name: Secondary Molecular Domestication & Exaptation (Not Original Purpose)
pillars.claim: Hosts occasionally co-opt parasitic transposons into vital innovations (RAG1/2 immunity, placental Syncytin, neuronal Arc), without overturning their selfish parasitic origins.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree transposons compose huge fractions of eukaryotic genomes, drive costly disease mutations and host silencing arms races, and occasionally get co-opted into extraordinary host innovations like V(D)J recombination and mammalian placentas.
steelman.theory_a_case: Host genomes invest immense metabolic and regulatory effort in KRAB-ZNF repressors, DNA methylation, and piRNAs strictly to muzzle active LINE/ERV parasites—and meiotic drive / centromere drive directly triggers hybrid sterility and speciation through pure intragenomic conflict.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Several active transposon families are surprisingly tightly integrated into normal embryonic stem-cell zygotic genome activation (MERVL/HERVL) and stress-responsive regulatory networks, blurring the boundary between pure parasite and domesticated symbiont.
steelman.rival_b_name: Adaptive Evolvability / Controlling-Element & Neutral Mutational-Hazard Models (McClintock-Lynch)
steelman.rival_b_case: Lynch's Mutational-Hazard model shows massive genome bloating tracks small effective population size (weak purifying selection) rather than aggressive TE hyper-virulence alone, while exaptation advocates highlight TEs as an unparalleled source of ready-made TF binding motifs and viral-like cell-to-cell shuttles.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Claiming transposons exist 'to provide evolvability' fails basic natural-selection logic: millions of freshly inserted TE copies are immediately neutral or deleterious, with <1 percent ever exapted millions of years later.

episodes.label: Everything Talks to Everything? — The Omnigenic Model (Boyle, Liu & Pritchard) vs. Classical Polygenic & Rare-Variant Architecture (Wray, Visscher, Yang, Yao & Wainschtein), the 11% Cis-eQTL Chasm & Genome-Scale Perturb-seq
episodes.notes: When genome-wide association studies scaled to millions of people, disease risk refused to stay parked inside neat textbook pathways — instead spreading across thousands of non-coding variants near housekeeping genes with no obvious link to the illness. This five-act adversarial deep dive stages the fiercest conceptual trial in modern human genetics: Jonathan Pritchard, Evan Boyle, Yang Li, and Xuanyao Liu's Omnigenic Model — proposing that densely wired intracellular networks force at least 70 percent of complex-trait heritability through weak peripheral trans-effects converging onto a compact set of core effector genes — versus Naomi Wray, Peter Visscher, Jian Yang, Alkes Price, and Pierrick Wainschtein's Classical Additive Polygenic and Rare-Variant Architecture. Examine all eight landmark papers spanning 454,787 UK Biobank exomes, 35 biochemical biomarkers, Yengo's 5.4-million-person saturated height map (12,111 SNPs packed into 21 percent of the genome), Yao and Price's shocking MESC discovery that assayed bulk cis-eQTLs mediate only 11 percent of disease heritability, and TOPMed whole-genome sequencing recovering missing heritability in rare low-LD coding variants. Pause twice for explicit mathematical walkthroughs — first deriving how a mere 2 percent directional core co-regulation explodes peripheral trans-heritability past 87 percent, then calculating exact single-cell negative-binomial Perturb-seq cell counts and sequencing budgets required to detect 5 to 10 percent trans-shifts across 2,000 peripheral genes — and leave with a pre-registered Perturb-seq plus core-clamp protocol and a stealth field guide for decoding complex-trait genomics papers.

theory.canonical_title: The Omnigenic Model vs. Polygenic Architecture of Complex Traits
theory.core_claim: The Omnigenic Model (Boyle, Li & Pritchard) posits that cellular gene-regulatory networks are so densely interconnected that virtually every gene expressed in trait-relevant cell types acts as a 'peripheral' modifier exerting tiny trans-regulatory effects on a smaller set of mechanistically direct 'core' genes, accounting for >=70 percent of complex-trait heritability.
theory.verdict_2026: The Omnigenic Model remains vigorously contested against classical infinitesimal/polygenic quantitative genetics in 2026. Ultra-large GWAS (e.g., Yengo et al.'s 5.4-million-person height study identifying 12,111 independent SNPs spanning ~21 percent of the genome) and biochemical-trait dissections (Sinnott-Armstrong 2021) corroborate extreme dispersion of polygenic signal around recognizable biochemical core clusters. Yet critics (Wray, Visscher, Yang 2018; Mostafavi et al. 2023) demonstrate that the core-versus-peripheral boundary resists operational definition for most polygenic diseases, rare whole-genome variants explain substantial missing heritability under classic additive models (Wainschtein 2022), and bulk cis-eQTLs mediate only ~11 percent of disease heritability (Yao & Price 2020), complicating straightforward trans-expression wiring.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Many papers use 'omnigenic' as a trendy buzzword for 'very polygenic,' missing Pritchard's specific mechanistic claim that peripheral heritability must flow quantitatively through trans-regulatory convergence onto core-gene expression levels. Equally overlooked is the systematic ascertainment mismatch (Mostafavi 2023): standard eQTL studies enrich for unconstrained genes with large cis effects, whereas GWAS disease hits disproportionately land in highly constrained, complexly regulated developmental enhancers.

historical_evolution.milestone: R. A. Fisher establishes the infinitesimal polygenic model reconciling continuous phenotypic variation with Mendelian inheritance.
Boyle, Li, Liu, and Pritchard (Cell) launch the Omnigenic Model and its formal cis-plus-trans heritability partition predicting peripheral trans dominance.
Wray, Visscher et al. (Cell) critique 'core vs. peripheral' as a blurry rebranding of polygenicity, while Yao & Price (MESC) reveal a stark cis-eQTL mediation gap.
Biobank exomes (Backman 2021), 5.4M-sample saturated height maps (Yengo 2022), and Perturb-seq trans-eQTL atlases directly test peripheral-to-core regulatory convergence.

theory.falsification_criteria: The Omnigenic Model would be falsified if large-scale Perturb-seq and single-cell trans-eQTL mapping in disease-relevant tissues show that peripheral GWAS risk variants fail to converge on a privileged subset of core genes—or if peripheral variants instead act through dispersed, independent cell-state and physiological effects without core-gene mediation.
theory.stealth_support: Your study finds GWAS heritability spread thinly across thousands of non-coding loci across active tissue chromatin, with weak trans-regulatory convergence onto a small set of causal biochemical or rare-variant genes.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study finds missing heritability concentrates in rare low-LD coding/structural variants, OR shows assayed cis-eQTL transcriptional mediation accounts for only a tiny fraction (~11%) of disease heritability, undermining simple trans-regulatory cascades.

pillars.name: Near-Universal Polygenic Signal Dispersion
pillars.claim: For complex human traits, causal genetic variants are spread across virtually all active chromatin regions expressed in trait-relevant cell types rather than confined to a few discrete pathways.

pillars.name: Sharp Mechanistic Core-vs.-Peripheral Boundary
pillars.claim: Complex diseases possess an operationally definable, small set of direct biochemical 'core' effector genes cleanly separable from thousands of indirect 'peripheral' modifiers.

pillars.name: 70%+ Trans-Regulatory Percolation Through Core Genes
pillars.claim: At least 70 percent of common-variant heritability flows through tiny peripheral trans-eQTL perturbations that converge quantitatively onto core-gene expression levels.

pillars.name: Missing Heritability Beyond Common Additivity
pillars.claim: Common-SNP trans-network convergence explains genetic architecture more fundamentally than uncaptured rare coding/structural variants acting additively.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree that complex traits like height, schizophrenia, and cardiometabolic disease are extraordinarily polygenic (tens of thousands of tiny-effect common loci), that purifying selection flattens common-variant effect sizes, and that rare coding variants point to larger-effect biological pathways.
steelman.theory_a_case: Because transcription factors, chromatin remodelers, and metabolic enzymes form dense cellular networks, small peripheral expression tweaks inevitably ripple in trans onto direct biochemical effectors (clearly seen for blood urate, IGF-1, and testosterone)—explaining why 21 percent of the genome harbors height hits while Mendelian mutations cluster in…
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Mediated expression score regression (Yao & Price 2020) shows assayed cis-eQTLs mediate only ~11 percent of complex disease heritability, and Mostafavi et al. (2023) proved GWAS hits and eQTLs systematically sample different classes of genes, challenging simple steady-state trans-mRNA cascades.
steelman.rival_b_name: Classical Additive Polygenic & Modular Pathway / Rare-Variant Model (Wray-Visscher-Price)
steelman.rival_b_case: For multi-system diseases like schizophrenia, diabetes, or coronary disease, there is no crisp handful of 'core' genes—disease emerges from dozens of parallel cellular, developmental, and physiological modules plus rare low-LD variants (Wainschtein 2022) that close missing heritability under standard Fisherian quantitative genetics without a single…
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Classical additive models describe the infinitesimal statistical variance elegantly but struggle to explain why GWAS signals saturate nearly every active genomic segment in relevant tissues while still showing sharp biochemical pathway enrichment among rare loss-of-function alleles.

flip_scenarios.label: Single-cell Perturb-seq maps >=70% peripheral GWAS variance onto core genes
flip_scenarios.detail: Genome-scale CRISPRi Perturb-seq across 2,500 GWAS peripheral loci in primary disease-relevant cell states proves over 70 percent of phenotypic variance routes through <100 core effector transcripts or proteins.
flip_scenarios.next_experiment: Test whether pharmacological rescue of the identified core effectors neutralizes high polygenic risk scores across ancestry groups.

flip_scenarios.label: Peripheral GWAS knockdowns act independently without converging on core genes
flip_scenarios.detail: Large-scale Perturb-seq and developmental single-cell trans-eQTL atlases show <25 percent of peripheral heritability flows through any identifiable core-gene bottleneck, dispersing instead across independent physiological modules.
flip_scenarios.next_experiment: Decompose heritability across cell-state proportions, developmental timing, and post-translational protein-interaction modules.

flip_scenarios.label: Developmental context-specific eQTLs resolve the 11% mediation gap
flip_scenarios.detail: Time-resolved fetal and stimulated-state single-cell eQTL maps raise mediated disease heritability from 11 percent to >55 percent, showing bulk adult tissues hid the true trans-regulatory wiring.
flip_scenarios.next_experiment: Link developmental cis-eQTLs directly to trans-target gene modules using allele-specific CRISPR enhancer edits.

flip_scenarios.label: Core-peripheral architecture holds for biochemical traits but fails for psychiatric disease
flip_scenarios.detail: Comparative perturbation across 20 traits shows neat core-gene convergence for single-organ biomarkers (urate, LDL) but irreducibly distributed polygenic modules for neuropsychiatric and behavioral traits.
flip_scenarios.next_experiment: Derive quantitative network-modularity thresholds predicting when drug targeting of core genes beats polygenic risk stratification.

episodes.label: Motors on the Genome — Dixon & Ren's Hi-C TAD Discovery, Fudenberg & Mirny's Convergent-CTCF Loop Extrusion, Lupiáñez & Mundlos's Enhancer Hijacking & Ganji/Davidson's Single-Molecule SMC Movies vs. Rao & Aiden's Cohesin-Degron Shock, Bintu & Zhuang's Single-Cell Tracing & Despang's Sox9 Boundary Deletion
episodes.notes: How do two meters of human DNA fold inside a six-micron cell nucleus without tangling into an unreadable knot—and do three-dimensional chromatin loops actually control which genes turn on and off? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Chromatin Loop Extrusion and 3D Topologically Associating Domain (TAD) Theory on full empirical trial. Follow the arc from Jesse Dixon and Bing Ren's landmark 2012 Hi-C discovery of conserved megabase topological domains to Geoffrey Fudenberg and Leonid Mirny's polymer-physics breakthrough showing how ATP-driven cohesin rings extrude DNA loops until stalled exclusively by convergently oriented CTCF motifs, triumphantly validated by Darío Lupiáñez and Stefan Mundlos's congenital limb-malformation CRISPR models and directly filmed at single-molecule resolution by Mahipal Ganji, Cees Dekker, Iain Davidson, and Jan-Michael Peters. Then confront the three shockwaves that forced a profound functional refinement: Suhas Rao and Erez Lieberman Aiden's acute RAD21 auxin-degron experiment wiping out all loop domains while leaving steady-state transcription of most human genes intact, Bogdan Bintu and Xiaowei Zhuang's super-resolution STORM tracing proving TAD boundaries fluctuate stochastically across single cells, and Alexandra Despang's Sox9-Kcnj2 CTCF deletions. Includes two Python-verified polymer-scaling and burst-saturation calculation pauses plus a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment.

theory.canonical_title: Chromatin Loop Extrusion & 3D Topologically Associating Domain (TAD) Theory
theory.core_claim: ATP-driven SMC ring complexes (cohesin in interphase, condensin in mitosis) actively extrude chromatin loops until stalled by convergently oriented CTCF boundary motifs, partitioning metazoan genomes into Topologically Associating Domains (TADs) that constrain enhancer–promoter communication and prevent ectopic gene activation.
theory.verdict_2026: Cohesin/condensin-mediated loop extrusion is decisively proven as the physical mechanism building vertebrate TADs and mitotic chromosomes, directly visualized on single DNA molecules (Davidson 2019; Kim 2019). Yet the functional transcriptional half of TAD theory has undergone dramatic refinement: rapid auxin-inducible cohesin depletion (Rao et al. 2017) wipes out virtually all TADs and CTCF loops while acutely altering expression of surprisingly few genes (<100–200 strongly perturbed), and Micro-C studies (Hsieh 2022) reveal that most short-range enhancer–promoter contacts persist without cohesin. Consequently, 2026 consensus treats loop extrusion as essential primarily for long-range (>100 kb) developmental enhancer scanning, V(D)J recombination, and insulating sensitive developmental loci (e.g., EPHA4/SHH limb enhancers) rather than acting as a universal transcriptional switch.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers frequently describe TADs as rigid, static 'insulated neighborhoods' visible in every single cell and strictly required for all gene transcription, forgetting that Hi-C TAD triangles are ensemble averages over highly dynamic, fleeting cohesin-extruded loops and that acute cohesin loss leaves >95 percent of steady-state transcription intact while leaving A/B chromatin compartments even sharper.

historical_evolution.milestone: Dixon, Bing Ren, and Edith Heard discover Topologically Associating Domains (TADs) conserved across mammalian cell types via Hi-C.
Sanborn/Aiden and Fudenberg/Mirny formulate the Cohesin–CTCF convergent-motif Loop Extrusion polymer model predicting boundary inversions.
Rao et al. (Cell) show cohesin degradation erases TADs with modest acute transcriptional fallout, while single-molecule assays (Davidson, Kim) film cohesin extruding DNA in real time.
Live-cell super-resolution tracking (Gabriele et al. Science 2022) shows loops are surprisingly rare and transient (~10–30 min), while Micro-C decouples short-range E–P contacts from cohesin.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree cohesin physically extrudes DNA loops stalled at convergent CTCF sites, that Hi-C TADs are dynamic population averages rather than frozen static cages, and that acute cohesin degradation erases TADs while sharpening A/B micro-phase compartments.
steelman.theory_a_name: Active Loop Extrusion & 3D TAD Regulation (Mirny-Lieberman Aiden-Dekker)
steelman.theory_a_case: Single-molecule fluorescence movies directly watched cohesin extrude asymmetric loops at ~1 kb/s; inverting a single CTCF motif predictably flips loop direction; and deleting human TAD boundaries causes dramatic congenital limb polydactyly/syndactyly by mis-wiring developmental enhancers.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Rao et al. (2017 Cell) degraded cohesin acutely in human cells, wiping out every TAD corner peak across the genome—yet fewer than ~150 genes changed steady-state transcription >2-fold, and Micro-C showed most short-range enhancer-promoter loops survive without cohesin.
steelman.rival_b_name: Block-Copolymer Compartmentalization & Biochemical Compatibility (Micro-Phase / Affinity Models)
steelman.rival_b_case: A/B chromatin compartmentalization persists (and even strengthens!) without cohesin, short-range enhancer-promoter communication relies primarily on direct TF/Mediator affinity compatibility and local micro-phase attraction, and loop extrusion evolved originally for chromosome compaction/segregation before being co-opted for selected long-range loci.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Passive block-copolymer attraction cannot explain convergent CTCF orientation rules, immune V(D)J locus scanning across megabases, or acute developmental-gene expression failures when cohesin is removed during differentiation transitions rather than steady-state maintenance.

episodes.label: Valleys of Fate and Chaperone Capacitors — Waddington's 1942 Epigenetic Landscape & 1953 Crossveinless Fly Assimilation, Rutherford & Lindquist's Hsp90 Capacitor & Rohner's Blind Cavefish vs. Via's Threshold Genetics, Siegal & Bergman's Network Robustness & Specchia's piRNA Transposon Confound
episodes.notes: How can an organism acquire a brand-new anatomical trait solely in response to an environmental shock—like calluses on an ostrich's chest or eyelessness in pitch-black flooded caves—and within a dozen generations pass that trait down to its offspring even after the environmental trigger is completely removed, without violating a single law of Mendelian genetics? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Conrad Hal Waddington's twin concepts of Developmental Canalization and Genetic Assimilation on full empirical trial. Trace Waddington's 1942 Epigenetic Landscape and his classic 1953 experiment breeding heat-shocked crossveinless Drosophila into constitutive mutants in just fourteen generations, followed by Suzanne Rutherford and Susan Lindquist's 1998 discovery of the Hsp90 molecular chaperone capacitor and Nicolas Rohner's 2013 proof that low-conductivity cave water stresses Hsp90 to unmask cryptic eye-size variation in Mexican cavefish. Then confront four razor-sharp quantitative and molecular critiques: Sara Via and colleagues' proof that assimilation is standard Darwinian polygenic threshold selection rather than Lamarckian heresy, Mark Siegal, Aviv Bergman, and Sasha Levy's demonstration across 300 yeast network hubs that canalization emerges spontaneously from nonlinear gene networks without selection for evolvability, and Valeria Specchia's 2010 bombshell showing Hsp90 inhibition unleashes de novo piRNA-mediated transposon insertions! Pause twice for Python-verified Falconer threshold math and sigmoidal network calculations, and leave with a pre-registered CRISPR Head-to-Head protocol.

theory.canonical_title: Waddington Genetic Assimilation & Evolutionary Canalization
theory.core_claim: Developmental gene networks buffer phenotypes against genetic and environmental noise (canalization), concealing cryptic genetic variation; when severe environmental stress breaches this buffer (e.g., via Hsp90 titration) and reveals an adaptive induced phenotype, selection on standing cryptic variants can convert the plastic trait into a constitutively inherited one (genetic assimilation).
theory.verdict_2026: Waddington's twin concepts of developmental canalization and genetic assimilation are thoroughly validated experimentally—from Waddington's heat-shocked crossveinless flies and Rutherford & Lindquist's Hsp90 chaperone capacitor work to cavefish eye-loss assimilation (Rohner et al. 2013 Science) and yeast prion/chaperone buffering. Contemporary refinement resolves two major debates: (1) mathematical network models (Siegal & Bergman 2002) prove canalization often arises spontaneously as an emergent property of nonlinear regulatory networks without direct selection for robustness, and (2) genetic assimilation is firmly understood as standard polygenic selection on pre-existing cryptic alleles rather than any Lamarckian inheritance of acquired marks—though how often plasticity-first assimilation drives major wild adaptations remains actively quantified.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely misclassify Waddington's genetic assimilation as 'epigenetic/Lamarckian inheritance,' overlooking that Waddington himself explicitly explained assimilation via conventional Mendelian selection shifting polygenic thresholds across standing cryptic genetic variation. Others carelessly equate genetic assimilation (loss of plasticity toward constitutive fixation) with the broader 'Baldwin effect' (selection modifying reaction norms without necessarily eliminating plasticity).

historical_evolution.milestone: C. H. Waddington introduces developmental canalization and demonstrates genetic assimilation of heat-shock-induced crossveinless and ether-induced bithorax phenotypes in Drosophila.
Rutherford & Lindquist (Nature) identify the molecular chaperone Hsp90 as an evolutionary capacitor whose impairment unveils selectable cryptic morphological variation.
Siegal & Bergman show canalization emerges intrinsically from gene-network dynamics; West-Eberhard generalizes assimilation into 'genetic accommodation.'
Rohner et al. (Science) implicate Hsp90/conductivity stress in wild Astyanax cavefish eye-size evolution, while population genomics maps cryptic variation across natural clines.

episodes.label: The One-Way Street Out of Protein — Crick's 1970 Sequence Law, Baltimore & Temin's Reverse Transcriptase, Fire's Catalytic RNAi & Chandramouly's Pol-theta RNA Repair vs. Prusiner's Scrapie Prions, Shapiro's Epigenetic Critique & Koonin's Look-Ahead Assimilation
episodes.notes: Open almost any introductory biology textbook and you will read a notoriously false caricature of Francis Crick's Central Dogma—namely a rigid one-way arrow from DNA to RNA to protein—followed by breathless claims that retroviruses, RNA interference, epigenetic chromatin marks, or misfolded prions have overturned molecular biology's foundational law. This five-act adversarial deep dive restores Crick's actual 1958 and 1970 sequence-information boundary and puts sixty-eight years of challengers on rigorous biochemical trial. Audit what Crick's 1970 Nature diagram explicitly permitted versus strictly forbade: why David Baltimore and Howard Temin and John Coffin's discovery of retroviral reverse transcriptase, Andrew Fire and colleagues' catalytic double-stranded RNA interference in Caenorhabditis elegans, and Gurushankar Chandramouly's discovery of human DNA polymerase theta RNA-templated double-strand break repair all operate cleanly inside Crick's permitted nucleic-acid transfers. Then cross-examine the sharpest adversarial anomalies: Stanley Prusiner's nucleic-acid-free scrapie prions, James Shapiro's twenty-first-century systems-epigenetics critique, and Eugene Koonin's provocative prion-to-genome assimilation argument. Pause twice for Python-verified Shannon codon-degeneracy entropy proofs and ultraviolet target-size versus prion conformational bit-rate math, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment and a field guide for spotting sloppy Central Dogma violation claims in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: Central Dogma of Molecular Biology
theory.core_claim: Residue-by-residue sequence information can pass between nucleic acids (DNA replication, transcription, RNA replication, and reverse transcription) and from nucleic acid to polypeptide (translation), but once sequence information has passed into protein it cannot be reverse-translated back into nucleic acid or protein sequence.
theory.verdict_2026: More than 65 years after Francis Crick's original formulation, the Central Dogma remains one of the most resilient, universally corroborated laws in all of biology—with zero confirmed exceptions to its actual negative prohibition (protein-sequence to nucleic-acid-sequence reverse translation) across every domain of life. Reverse transcription (Temin & Baltimore 1970), RNA-dependent RNA replication, enzymatic RNA editing (ADAR/APOBEC), non-ribosomal peptide synthetases, and prion conformational templating all operate cleanly within or orthogonal to Crick's explicitly drawn 1958/1970 arrow diagram rather than refuting it.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: An extraordinary fraction of textbooks, grant introductions, and peer-reviewed papers falsely state that the Central Dogma is simply 'DNA -> RNA -> Protein' and then claim that retroviruses (reverse transcriptase), epigenetic chromatin marks, alternative splicing, or prions 'violate' or 'overturn' the Central Dogma. Crick (1958, 1970) explicitly allowed RNA -> DNA as a 'special transfer' and strictly banned only sequence-specific flow out of protein.

historical_evolution.milestone: Francis Crick introduces the Sequence Hypothesis and Central Dogma in 'On Protein Synthesis,' strictly prohibiting protein-to-nucleic-acid sequence flow.
Temin & Mizutani and Baltimore independently discover reverse transcriptase; Crick publishes his clarifying Nature diagram showing RNA->DNA was always permitted.
Discovery of catalytic RNAs (Cech, Altman), RNA editing, and Prusiner's protein-only prion folding clarify non-canonical information regulation without breaching sequence directionality.
Discovery of Rqc2 CAT-tailing (template-free Ala/Thr addition) and epitranscriptomic modifications refine translational nuance while Crick's negative law stands completely intact.

pillars.name: Strict Prohibition on Protein-to-Nucleic-Acid Reverse Translation
pillars.claim: Once residue-by-residue sequence information passes into a polypeptide chain, no natural biological machine reads that amino-acid sequence back into DNA or RNA sequence.

pillars.name: Permitted Special Nucleic-Acid Transfers (Reverse Transcription & RNA Replication)
pillars.claim: Crick's 1958/1970 formulation explicitly permitted RNA-to-DNA reverse transcription and RNA-to-RNA replication as valid nucleic-acid sequence transfers.

pillars.claim: Chromatin methylation, alternative splicing, Rqc2 CAT-tailing, and prion conformational templating regulate expression or 3D fold without breaching residue-level sequence directionality.

steelman.settled_ground: All molecular biologists agree that reverse transcription, RNA editing, epigenetic marks, and prions are ubiquitous—and that Crick's actual negative law banning residue-by-residue protein-to-nucleic-acid sequence flow has stood unbroken for 65+ years.
steelman.theory_a_case: Thermodynamic and stereochemical asymmetry makes template-based Watson-Crick base pairing effortless for nucleic acids while rendering a 20-amino-acid folded-protein 'reverse ribosome' biochemically unviable—explaining why zero reverse-translating enzymes evolved across 4 billion years.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Non-ribosomal peptide synthetases, Rqc2 template-free Ala/Thr CAT-tailing, and prion cross-beta conformational templating show proteins CAN convey limited non-nucleic structural or chemical information—even though none translates arbitrary polypeptide sequence back to DNA.
steelman.rival_b_name: Instructive Protein-Template & Reverse-Translation Speculations (Haurowitz-Mekler-Steele)
steelman.rival_b_case: Early 1950s antigen-template antibody theories and later somatic-hypermutation reverse-transcription hypotheses (Steele) asked whether acquired adaptive somatic protein solutions could feed back into germline genes.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Clonal selection completely replaced instructive antibody templates, and zero biological system has ever demonstrated enzyme-catalyzed reading of polypeptide sequence into corresponding nucleotide triplets.

episodes.label: Classical Lamarckian Inheritance of Acquired Somatic Traits — Organisms adaptively modify their somatic organs during life through physiological use and disuse—or direct instructive environmental imprinting—and transmit those specific somatic modifications directly into their offspring's heredity.
episodes.notes: Decisively falsified for eukaryotic multicellular organisms since Weismann's germ-plasm theory, Mendelian genetics, and Luria–Delbruck fluctuation analysis, yet retained as a crucial conceptual anchor because contemporary epigenetics and prokaryotic CRISPR-Cas papers routinely resurrect 'Neo-Lamarckism' as rhetorical clickbait. While microbial CRISPR-Cas spacer acquisition (Koonin & Wolf 2009) and ciliate/nematode RNAi inheritance display genuine instructive environmental capture into heritable sequences or small-RNA pools, they rely on evolved Darwinian molecular machinery and do not vindicate Lamarck's core mechanism of somatic organ use/disuse writing adaptive changes back into animal germlines.

theory.canonical_title: Classical Lamarckian Inheritance of Acquired Somatic Traits
theory.core_claim: Organisms adaptively modify their somatic organs during life through physiological use and disuse—or direct instructive environmental imprinting—and transmit those specific somatic modifications directly into their offspring's heredity.
theory.verdict_2026: Decisively falsified for eukaryotic multicellular organisms since Weismann's germ-plasm theory, Mendelian genetics, and Luria–Delbruck fluctuation analysis, yet retained as a crucial conceptual anchor because contemporary epigenetics and prokaryotic CRISPR-Cas papers routinely resurrect 'Neo-Lamarckism' as rhetorical clickbait. While microbial CRISPR-Cas spacer acquisition (Koonin & Wolf 2009) and ciliate/nematode RNAi inheritance display genuine instructive environmental capture into heritable sequences or small-RNA pools, they rely on evolved Darwinian molecular machinery and do not vindicate Lamarck's core mechanism of somatic organ use/disuse writing adaptive changes back into animal germlines.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Review articles and headlines repeatedly proclaim 'Was Lamarck Right After All?' upon seeing any diet-induced sperm miRNA shift or methylation change—confusing non-adaptive, short-lived stress transmission (which fades in 1–2 generations) with Lamarck's theory that targeted adaptive somatic adjustments (like stretching a neck or strengthening a muscle) drive long-term macroevolutionary design.

historical_evolution.milestone: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck publishes Philosophie Zoologique, formalizing use/disuse and inheritance of acquired traits alongside an innate complexifying drive.
August Weismann formulates the germ-plasm barrier separating somatic modifications from germline inheritance; rediscovery of Mendel seals hard heredity.
Luria and Delbruck's fluctuation test proves bacterial phage-resistance mutations arise randomly prior to exposure rather than being Lamarckianly induced by selection.
Koonin & Wolf identify CRISPR-Cas as a specialized 'quasi-Lamarckian' prokaryotic defense while molecular biology maintains strict rejection of metazoan somatic-to-germline Lamarckism.

steelman.settled_ground: All biologists agree classical Lamarckian inheritance of acquired somatic organ remodeling is dead in animals, while prokaryotic CRISPR-Cas spacer capture represents a genuine—yet strictly Darwinian-evolved—targeted hereditary defense mechanism.
steelman.theory_a_name: Classical Lamarckian Soft Inheritance (Superseded Historical Anchor)
steelman.theory_a_case: Before Mendelian genetics or DNA existed, Lamarck proposed the first coherent naturalistic mechanism of evolutionary transformation, and modern microbial CRISPR-Cas and ciliate genome rearrangements prove directed environmental sequence capture is physically possible when dedicated molecular machinery evolves.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Weismann's germline sequestration, Mendelian independent assortment, Luria-Delbruck fluctuation proofs, and the Central Dogma prohibit somatic organ adaptations from writing corresponding sequence edits into animal germlines.
steelman.rival_b_name: Weismann Barrier & Neo-Darwinian Hard Inheritance
steelman.rival_b_case: Random mutation filtered by selection—augmented by Waddington's Darwinian genetic assimilation and evolved narrow immunity mechanisms like CRISPR—explains adaptation across all domains of life without invoking somatic-to-germline teleology.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Overly rigid 'hard-heredity-only' rhetoric sometimes caused biologists to initially dismiss real non-DNA inheritance channels in plants, C. elegans RNAi, and prokaryotic CRISPR-Cas until molecular mechanisms were proven.

episodes.label: Ghosts Through the Firewall — Mammalian Transgenerational Epigenetic Inheritance (Heard & Martienssen), Two-Wave PGC Erasure (Seisenberger), Sperm tsRNAs (Chen), Olfr151 Fear Memory (Dias & Ressler), 4-Generation Engineered CGIs (Takahashi) & Horsthemke's Human Critique
episodes.notes: Can your grandparents' famine, diet, or traumatic memories pierce the Weismann barrier and write heritable chemical marks onto mammalian sperm and eggs without mutating a single letter of DNA? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Mammalian Transgenerational Epigenetic Inheritance (TEI) on rigorous molecular trial. Trace Heard and Martienssen's foundational F1/F2 intergenerational versus F3+ transgenerational rulebook alongside Seisenberger and Reik's whole-genome bisulfite proof that mammalian primordial germ cells sandblast over 90 percent of DNA methylation clean every generation; examine the three landmark mouse breakthroughs—Dias and Ressler's controversial acetophenone Olfr151 olfactory fear study, Chen and colleagues' Science proof that microinjecting modified sperm tsRNAs into normal zygotes transmits F1 metabolic disease, and Takahashi and Izpisua Belmonte's 2023 Cell demonstration of four-generation engineered CpG-island methylation persisting via post-implantation re-establishment; and cross-examine the entire field through Bernhard Horsthemke's forensic critique of human famine and trauma cohorts plus Giacomo Cavalli and Edith Heard's cross-kingdom synthesis. Pause twice for worked quantitative calculations proving passive reprogramming attrition, 34-billion-fold mitotic dilution of sperm RNAs without RdRP, litter-clustered false-positive inflation, and cryptic cis-mQTL confounding, then walk away with a pre-registered isogenic IVF F3+ experimental protocol and a field guide for spotting sloppy versus rigorous TEI claims in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: Transgenerational Epigenetic Inheritance in Mammals
theory.core_claim: Environmentally induced non-DNA molecular marks—such as DNA methylation, histone modifications, or sperm small non-coding RNAs (tsRNAs/miRNAs)—can survive mammalian germline and zygotic reprogramming to transmit acquired physiological or behavioral phenotypes across three or more generations (F3+ in maternal exposure; F2+ in paternal exposure).
theory.verdict_2026: While transgenerational epigenetic inheritance (TEI) is rock-solid in plants, yeast, and C. elegans (via RNAi/piRNA amplification), its natural prevalence and evolutionary significance in mammals remain fiercely contested in 2026. Proof-of-principle engineered CpG-island methylation at murine Ankrd26 and Ldlr (Takahashi et al. 2023 Cell) proved that specific methylated epialleles CAN escape global reprogramming and transmit metabolic traits across four generations, alongside well-known IAP retrotransposon metastability (Agouti viable yellow, AxinFu). Nonetheless, stringent geneticists (Heard & Martienssen 2014; Horsthemke 2018) emphasize that nearly all dramatic claims of human trauma or murine odor-fear TEI remain confounded by cryptic DNA sequence differences, in utero/germ-cell direct exposure (intergenerational, not transgenerational), maternal behavior, or microbiome transfer.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: A pervasive fatal error in biomedical and social-science papers is calling F1 or F2 effects of a pregnant female's exposure (stress, famine, endocrine disruptors) 'transgenerational epigenetic inheritance'—when the pregnant F0 mother, the F1 fetus, AND the F1 fetus's developing primordial germ cells (which become F2) were all directly exposed in utero; only F3 (maternal) or F2 (paternal) tests genuine transgenerational transmission.

historical_evolution.milestone: Emma Whitelaw's Avy (Agouti) mouse studies demonstrate metastable IAP retrotransposon epialleles, while Anway/Skinner's vinclozolin claims spark decades of replication controversy.

Heard & Martienssen (Cell) establish gold-standard criteria distinguishing intergenerational from true transgenerational inheritance across taxa; Dias & Ressler report controversial murine odor-fear TEI.
Sperm tRNA-derived small RNAs (Chen et al. Science) implicate paternal RNA vectors in diet-induced metabolic shifts, while Horsthemke (2018) critiques human TEI claims as largely unproven.
Takahashi et al. (Cell) demonstrate engineered CpG-island TEI across four mouse generations, refocusing debate from 'can it occur?' to 'how often does natural adaptive TEI occur in humans?'

rivals: Strict Reprogramming Barrier / DNA-Sequence Confounding Null Model (Horsthemke / Heard)
Intergenerational In-Utero / Direct Germ-Cell Exposure Hypothesis
Non-Epigenetic Vertical Transfer (Microbiome, Cultural/Maternal Care, Cryptic Genetic Variants)
theory.falsification_criteria: Any specific mammalian TEI claim is falsified if effects disappear under IVF/embryo transfer into naive surrogates using strictly isogenic inbred lines across F2 (paternal) or F3 (maternal) generations, or if whole-genome sequencing reveals subtle de novo genetic or copy-number mutations explaining the phenotype.
theory.stealth_support: Your study demonstrates an acquired mammalian phenotype persisting into unexposed F3+ generations (paternal line) or F3+ (maternal line) via defined sperm small RNAs or reprogramming-resistant methylation marks.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study shows marks are erased during PGC/zygotic demethylation (>90% reset), phenotypes vanish by F3, or human cohort correlations collapse once shared genetics and socioeconomic continuity are controlled.

episodes.label: The Eighty-Percent Mirage? — The ENCODE 80% Functional Genome Claim (Dunham & Birney 2012; Kellis 2014) vs. Junk DNA, Causal-Role vs. Selected-Effect Function (Doolittle 2013), Graur's Mutational-Load Ceiling (2013, 2017), Rands & Ponting's 8.2% Turnover Constraint & Palazzo–Gregory's Onion Test
episodes.notes: Why does an ordinary kitchen onion pack five times more DNA into every cell than a human being—and why did the 2012 ENCODE Consortium trigger one of the fiercest scientific showdowns in modern biology by assigning biochemical activity to 80.4% of the human genome? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts the ENCODE Functional Genome Claim and the Junk DNA / Onion Test paradigm on complete empirical trial. Unpack the 1,640-dataset biochemical triumph of Dunham, Birney, and the ENCODE Consortium alongside Manolis Kellis and colleagues' candid 2014 PNAS tripartite reconciliation separating biochemical maps, evolutionary conservation, and genetic perturbation phenotypes; then cross-examine the five-paper evolutionary counteroffensive from Dan Graur's 2013 critique and 2017 Haldane–Muller mutational-load fertility ceiling, W. Ford Doolittle's philosophical distinction between causal-role activity and Darwinian selected-effect function, Alexander Palazzo and T. Ryan Gregory's formalization of the Onion Test and RNA stoichiometry audit, and Chris Rands, Chris Ponting, and Gerton Lunter's turnover-corrected mammalian indel analysis pinning active human constraint at 8.2%. Pause twice for Python-verified calculations proving why an 80%-functional human genome demands 434 to 31 billion children per couple under multiplicative load, why random 6-bp transcription-factor motifs occur 1.49 million times purely by chance, and why laboratory mouse knockouts are 5,000x coarser than human natural selection—then walk away with a pre-registered CRISPR plus synthetic-DNA crucial-experiment protocol and a practical stealth field guide for auditing non-coding genomics claims.

theory.canonical_title: ENCODE Functional Genome Claim vs. Junk DNA & the Onion Test
theory.core_claim: The 2012 ENCODE Consortium argued that ~80.4 percent of the human genome exhibits biochemical 'function' (transcription, chromatin marks, TF binding), directly challenging evolutionary genomicists who contend that ~85–90 percent of human DNA is non-functional transposon-derived 'junk' constrained neither by selection nor by organismal necessity (illustrated by the C-value paradox / Onion Test).
theory.verdict_2026: While the semantic battle has clarified into W. Ford Doolittle's distinction between 'causal-role' biochemical activity and 'selected-effect' evolutionary function, the empirical upper bound of truly functional human DNA remains actively contested. Comparative genomics across 240 placental mammals (Zoonomia Consortium 2023 Science) detected evolutionary purifying constraint across ~10.7 percent of the human genome—in close agreement with Rands et al.'s (2014) ~8.2 percent estimate and mutational-load limits (Graur 2017), soundly refuting the 2012 press-release claim that '80 percent of the genome is functional' and 'junk DNA is dead.' Still, lineage-specific turnover of primate enhancers, lncRNAs, and structural/spacer roles keep estimates of selected sequence actively debated between ~10 and ~20–25 percent.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Biomedical papers routinely cite ENCODE (2012) to assert that 'junk DNA was disproven' and that 80 percent of the human genome is biologically necessary, conflating low-level spurious biochemical transcription or transient TF binding with fitness-relevant function. Conversely, strict selectionist critiques sometimes dismiss clade-specific young regulatory elements (invisible to deep 240-mammal phyloP conservation) without testing them via CRISPR deletion or Massively Parallel Reporter Assays.

historical_evolution.milestone: Susumu Ohno coins 'Junk DNA' based on mutational-load mathematics; T. Ryan Gregory formulates the 'Onion Test' (Allium cepa has ~5x more DNA than humans) against pan-functionalism.
ENCODE Consortium (Nature) reports 80.4 percent of the human genome participates in at least one biochemical assay, triggering headlines declaring junk DNA dead.
Dan Graur et al. ('Immortality of Television Sets'), Doolittle (PNAS), and Rands et al. (~8.2 percent constrained) dismantle ENCODE's evolution-free definition of function.
Zoonomia (240 mammals) pins mammalian evolutionary constraint near ~10.7 percent, while high-throughput CRISPRi perturbations quantify functional vs. noisy enhancers and lncRNAs.

rivals: Selected-Effect Evolutionary Constraint Paradigm (Graur, Doolittle, Palazzo & Gregory)
Causal-Role Biochemical Activity Framework (ENCODE Consortium / Kellis)
Lineage-Specific Regulatory Turnover & Structural Nucleoskeletal Hypotheses (Cavalier-Smith)
theory.falsification_criteria: The pan-functionalist (>80 percent) ENCODE claim is already falsified by human mutational-load bounds and megabase-scale viable mammalian gene-desert deletions (Nobrega et al. 2004); the strict <=10 percent functional ceiling would be falsified if systematic primate-specific CRISPR deletions across unconstrained non-coding regions routinely cause measurable fitness defects.
theory.stealth_support: Your study shows deletion of poorly conserved non-coding transcripts or biochemical marks causes reproducible fitness deficits under natural stress (supporting broader functional non-coding genome).
theory.stealth_refute: Your study shows large mega-base deletions of biochemically active non-conserved DNA yield viable, fertile organisms with zero fitness loss, consistent with ~8–15% selected-effect genome constraint.

episodes.label: Drift, Draft, and the Fifty-Year Trial of Neutrality — Motoo Kimura's 1968 Neutral Theory, Tomoko Ohta's Nearly Neutral Paradigm, Eyre-Walker & Keightley's 50% Adaptive Drosophila DFE-alpha, Sella's Genetic Draft, Kern & Hahn's 2018 Obituary & Jensen's Background-Selection Defense
episodes.notes: When molecular biologists first opened up proteins and chromosomes in the 1960s, they stumbled onto a mathematical paradox: species accumulated nucleotide substitutions hundreds of times faster than classical Darwinian natural selection could seemingly sustain without crushing populations under lethal genetic load. This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Motoo Kimura's 1968 Neutral Theory and Tomoko Ohta's 1973 and 1990 Nearly Neutral Paradigm on full empirical trial fifty years into the genomic era. Trace Kimura's stunning rate invariance proof and Ohta's nearly neutral scaling cliff resolving generation-time anomalies across small-population mammals and massive-population microbes; then cross-examine the framework against its sharpest whole-genome challengers—Adam Eyre-Walker and Peter Keightley's DFE-alpha evidence that roughly half of Drosophila amino-acid substitutions are adaptive, Guy Sella, Dmitri Petrov, Molly Przeworski, and Peter Andolfatto's documentation of pervasive linked genetic draft across fruit-fly chromosomes, and Andrew Kern and Matthew Hahn's explosive 2018 fiftieth-anniversary obituary met head-on by Jeffrey Jensen and colleagues' 2019 defense of purifying background selection and demography as the indispensable evolutionary null. Pause twice for worked quantitative calculations reproducing Haldane's extinction load, Ohta's four-order-of-magnitude Ne fixation cliff, and how a simple tenfold population expansion hallucinates nearly thirty percent phantom adaptive evolution in naive McDonald-Kreitman tests, then leave with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a practical stealth field guide for spotting neutral-versus-linked-selection tests across modern genomics.

theory.canonical_title: Neutral & Nearly Neutral Theory of Molecular Evolution (Kimura / Ohta)
theory.core_claim: The vast majority of evolutionary substitutions at the molecular level—and much standing within-species polymorphism—are driven not by positive Darwinian selection, but by random genetic drift acting on selectively neutral (Kimura) or slightly deleterious alleles whose fate depends on effective population size Ne (Ohta's Nearly Neutral Theory).
theory.verdict_2026: Kimura's Neutral Theory as generalized by Tomoko Ohta's Nearly Neutral Theory remains the indispensable mathematical null model and backbone of comparative genomics (dN/dS tests, molecular clocks, McDonald–Kreitman inference). Yet modern whole-genome population datasets have triggered an intense refinement debate: Kern & Hahn (2018) argued that pervasive linked selection—especially background purifying selection against deleterious mutations and recurrent selective sweeps—dramatically shapes neutral diversity across recombining chromosomes, violating naive mutation–drift equilibrium. Jensen et al. (2019) and Charlesworth counter that background selection is itself a direct corollary of Kimura/Ohta's ubiquitous purifying selection rather than a return to pan-selectionist positive adaptation.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Non-specialists routinely caricature Neutral Theory as claiming 'natural selection is unimportant,' completely forgetting that Kimura explicitly invoked pervasive negative (purifying) selection eliminating deleterious mutations as the mechanism leaving neutral variants to drift. Conversely, phylogenetics papers frequently apply naive neutral mutation–drift expectations (theta = 4*Ne*mu) to infer historical population sizes without correcting for linked background selection and biased gene conversion (gBGC).

historical_evolution.milestone: Motoo Kimura (Nature) and King & Jukes ('Non-Darwinian Evolution,' Science) formulate the Neutral Theory to explain rapid molecular clocks and vast allozyme polymorphism.
Tomoko Ohta develops the Nearly Neutral Theory (|Ne*s| ~ 1), explaining why small-Ne lineages accumulate slightly deleterious substitutions and codon-bias relaxation.
McDonald–Kreitman tests and Drosophila genomics reveal unexpectedly high fractions (often 40–50 percent) of adaptive amino-acid substitutions in high-Ne species.
Kern & Hahn (2018) vs. Jensen et al. (2019) debate linked selection's erosion of neutral diversity, embedding background selection and gBGC into modern baseline null models.

rivals: Linked-Selection / Genetic-Draft Paradigm (Gillespie; Kern & Hahn)
Classical Pan-Selectionist / Balancing-Selection School (Dobzhansky / Ford)
Constructive Neutral Evolution (Stoltzfus / Doolittle — complementary extension)
theory.falsification_criteria: Strict neutral mutation–drift equilibrium is falsified across genomes wherever synonymous diversity correlates strongly with local recombination rate and gene density (demonstrating ubiquitous linked selection) or wherever alpha (adaptive substitution fraction) dominates even in small-Ne vertebrates.
theory.stealth_support: Your study shows neutral drift + background purifying selection accurately predicts genome-wide polymorphism patterns and divergence rates scaling inversely with N_e.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study shows pervasive positive selective sweeps and linked genetic draft depress neutral diversity across entire chromosomes (e.g., ~45% adaptive amino-acid substitutions in Drosophila).

episodes.label: Droplets, Hubs, or Kissing Loops? — Hnisz, Sabari & Boija's Super-Enhancer Phase-Separation Model, Cho's Live-Cell Mediator/Pol II Clusters, Chong's Sub-Saturated TF Hubs, Alexander's 300-nm Sox2 Gap & Trojanowski and Weinmann's Locus-Titration Reckoning
episodes.notes: How does a regulatory DNA enhancer sitting a hundred thousand base pairs away—and floating two to three hundred nanometers across the crowded mammalian nucleus—command its target gene promoter to fire explosive bursts of messenger RNA? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts the Transcriptional Phase-Separation Condensate Model on full biophysical trial against both classical direct enhancer-promoter chromatin looping and sub-saturated multivalent transcription-factor hubs. Trace how Denes Hnisz, Phillip Sharp, Richard Young, Benjamin Sabari, and Ann Boija revolutionized gene regulation in 2017 and 2018 by proposing that intrinsically disordered activation domains of transcription factors, MED1, and BRD4 undergo liquid-liquid phase separation at super-enhancers, supported by Won-Ki Cho's live-cell super-resolution imaging of Mediator and RNA Polymerase II clusters and Peiheng Gan's myocardin lineage-switch condensates. Then cross-examine five razor-sharp experimental counterstrikes: Jeffrey Alexander's real-time Sox2 tracking showing transcriptional bursts show zero correlation with tight enhancer proximity, Shasha Chong, Claire Dugast-Darzacq, and Robert Tjian's endogenous single-molecule proof of sub-saturated low-complexity hubs without phase demixing, Derek Le and Alistair Boettiger's multiplexed single-cell super-enhancer community maps, and Jorge Trojanowski and Robin Weinmann's decisive quantitative locus-titration experiments demonstrating that transcription activation peaks via multivalent stoichiometric binding BEFORE crossing the phase-separation threshold—with macroscopic droplets yielding zero extra boost or even dampening output! Pause twice for Python-verified nuclear nanomolar-to-micromolar stoichiometry, 300-nanometer diffusion physics, 3D optical localization error math, and Hill-switch statistical power, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a stealth field guide for auditing condensate claims across genomics, biophysics, and oncology pharmacology.

theory.canonical_title: Transcription Factor / Enhancer Condensate Model vs. Direct Looping
theory.core_claim: The Transcriptional Condensate Model proposes that intrinsically disordered activation domains of transcription factors, coactivators (MED1, BRD4), and RNA Pol II undergo liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) at super-enhancers to bridge enhancers and promoters across hundreds of nanometers without requiring tight direct molecular contact.
theory.verdict_2026: Whether enhancers activate target promoters via phase-separated transcriptional condensates, non-LLPS multivalent binding hubs, or transient direct physical looping remains hotly contested in 2026. Live-cell imaging confirms that enhancers and active promoters often sit 150–300 nm apart during transcriptional bursts (Benabdallah 2019; Heist/Fukaya), seemingly compatible with a diffusing coactivator 'cloud' or condensate bridge. However, direct functional perturbations (Trojanowski et al. 2022 Molecular Cell; Ferrie/Tjian/Darzacq) show that driving TF activation domains across the saturation threshold into true phase-separated droplets frequently fails to enhance—or even reduces—transcription relative to sub-saturated multivalent binding hubs, while single-molecule kinetics often fit transient kiss-and-run or diffusive-gradient models without phase boundaries.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Authors routinely treat any bright fluorescent Mediator or Pol II punctum in a fixed nucleus—or droplet formation at micromolar purified protein concentrations in vitro—as proof that endogenous LLPS drives transcription, without testing whether endogenous nuclear concentrations ever cross the saturation concentration C_sat or whether phase separation actually increases mRNA initiation rate over stoichiometric recruitment.

historical_evolution.milestone: Hnisz, Sharp, and Young (Cell 2017; Sabari Science 2018) propose phase-separated super-enhancer condensates (MED1/BRD4/TF IDRs) as the engine of transcriptional bursting.
Chong/Tjian/Darzacq (Science) document dynamic low-valency TF 'hubs' without clear phase transitions, while Benabdallah et al. observe Shh enhancer–promoter separation during activation.
Trojanowski et al. (Molecular Cell) optogenetically separate multivalent TF binding from droplet formation, finding phase separation is dispensable or inhibitory for transcriptional output.
Single-molecule live imaging of nascent RNA bursts alongside enhancer position tests competing 'tag-and-release,' 'TF diffusive cloud,' and 'micro-condensate' models.

rivals: Sub-Saturated Multivalent TF Binding Hubs (Tjian & Darzacq)
Direct Transient 'Kiss-and-Run' Physical Looping & Tag-and-Release Models
Local Diffusive Concentration-Gradient ('TF Cloud') Models without Phase Boundaries
theory.falsification_criteria: The LLPS enhancer-condensate model is falsified for endogenous transcription if point mutations that abolish macroscopic phase separation while preserving IDR–Mediator binding affinity sustain wild-type transcriptional burst frequency and enhancer–promoter activation across developmental super-enhancers.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree that Mediator, Pol II, and TFs form dynamic high-concentration local clusters at active super-enhancers and that IDRs participate in weak multivalent interactions—disagreeing sharply over whether genuine thermodynamic phase demixing enhances transcription.
steelman.theory_a_case: Super-enhancer-driven genes show exquisite sensitivity to BRD4/MED1 perturbation, purified activation domains form phase-separated droplets concentrating Pol II in vitro, and a ~200 nm condensate bridge neatly explains how an enhancer activates a promoter 200 nm away without touching.

(2022 Molecular Cell) systematically titrated endogenous TF activation domains across the saturation threshold and found transcription rose linearly with site-specific binding—and gained ZERO extra boost (or actually declined!) once true macroscopic phase-separated droplets…
steelman.rival_b_name: Sub-Saturated Multivalent Hubs & Diffusive Tag-and-Release (Tjian-Darzacq-Rippe)
steelman.rival_b_case: Weak multivalent IDR contacts create dynamic sub-saturation micro-clusters (<c_sat) and local diffusive acetylation/phosphorylation clouds that boost Pol II recruitment without paying the kinetic trapping penalty of an interfacial phase boundary.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Pure transient direct-looping ('kiss-and-run') struggles to explain sustained simultaneous co-bursting of two independent promoters sharing one distant super-enhancer separated by 250 nm across live imaging frames.

episodes.label: Before DNA and Protein — Walter Gilbert's RNA World, Ban & Steitz's 2.4-Angstrom Ribozyme Ribosome, Sutherland, Carell & Szostak's Prebiotic Ribonucleotide Syntheses, Martin & Russell's Alkaline Vent Challenge, Bernhardt's Stability Critique & Carter & Wills's RNP Urzyme Coevolution
episodes.notes: Modern cellular life rests on an apparent molecular catch-22: DNA stores genetic blueprints that cannot replicate without protein enzymes, yet protein enzymes cannot be synthesized without nucleic acid blueprints and ribosomes. How did pre-DNA genetics bootstrap itself out of non-living chemistry? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Walter Gilbert's 1986 RNA World Hypothesis on full empirical trial across structural biology, prebiotic systems chemistry, bioenergetics, and ancestral enzyme reconstruction. Follow the crowning structural proof in Nenad Ban, Poul Nissen, Peter Moore, and Thomas Steitz's 2.4-angstrom crystal structure of the 50S ribosomal subunit—demonstrating zero protein atoms within 18 angstroms of peptide-bond catalysis—alongside Matthew Powner, Beatrice Gerland, and John Sutherland's cyanosulfidic 2-aminooxazole ribonucleotide synthesis, Shaun Stairs, Jack Szostak, and Powner's divergent pyrimidine/8-oxopurine pathway, and Sidney Becker and Thomas Carell's unified wet-dry cycle synthesis of all four canonical Watson-Crick nucleosides. Then cross-examine three formidable challenges to a solitary naked-RNA origin: William Martin, John Baross, Deborah Kelley, and Michael Russell's alkaline hydrothermal vent metabolism-first paradigm, Harold Bernhardt's quantitative catalog of 2'-hydroxyl backbone hydrolysis, asphaltization, and chiral cross-inhibition, and Charles Carter and Peter Wills's aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase urzyme evidence for an obligate RNA-Peptide (RNP) coevolutionary origin. Pause twice for Python-verified Eigen quasispecies error-threshold and duplex-melting versus phosphodiester cleavage kinetics, then walk away with a pre-registered Head-to-Head Crucial Experiment protocol and a field guide for spotting RNA World versus RNP and chimeric-backbone tests in disguise.

theory.canonical_title: RNA World Hypothesis of Pre-DNA Genetic Systems
theory.subdiscipline: Prebiotic Molecular Genetics & Origin of Life
theory.core_claim: Prior to the emergence of DNA genomes and genetically encoded protein enzymes, early life relied on RNA polymers serving simultaneously as heritable genetic templates and catalytic ribozymes—leaving molecular fossils such as the ribozyme core of the ribosome and nucleotide cofactors (ATP, NAD, CoA).
theory.verdict_2026: That an RNA-dominated biochemical stage preceded the DNA–protein genetic system is overwhelmingly corroborated by structural biology (the peptidyl-transferase center of every ribosome is an RNA ribozyme) and in vitro directed evolution of RNA polymerase ribozymes capable of copying complex RNAs (including high-fidelity variants such as QT45/tC19Z/38-6). However, the 'RNA-first' origin-of-life claim has undergone deep revision: because pure prebiotic RNA synthesis, homochirality, and non-enzymatic strand separation face severe chemical bottlenecks, leading prebiotic chemists (Sutherland, Krishnamurthy, Szostak, Hud) increasingly favor an 'RNA–peptide coevolution' or 'chimeric RNA–DNA / proto-RNA' systems chemistry rather than a solitary naked-RNA world.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely conflate two distinct claims: (1) the well-established evolutionary conclusion that an RNA–ribozyme stage preceded DNA and modern translation (supported by ribosome architecture), versus (2) the far harder, unresolved prebiotic claim that pure canonical RNA spontaneously polymerized from abiotic soup without prior proto-nucleic acids, peptide cofactors, or mineral/vesicle compartmentalization.

historical_evolution.milestone: Carl Woese, Francis Crick, and Leslie Orgel independently speculate that early RNA acted as both genetic catalyst and template.
Thomas Cech and Sidney Altman discover natural catalytic RNAs (ribozymes); Walter Gilbert coins the term 'The RNA World' (1986 Nature).
Atomic ribosome crystal structures prove peptide bond synthesis is RNA-catalyzed; Powner, Gerland & Sutherland solve activated pyrimidine ribonucleotide synthesis.
Discovery of cross-chiral and high-processivity polymerase ribozymes plus prebiotic cyanosulfidic chemistry shifts consensus toward coupled RNA–peptide/chimeric-backbone emergence.

pillars.name: Historical RNA-Catalyzed Stage Preceded DNA & Encoded Proteins
pillars.claim: An RNA-dominated biochemical era preceded DNA genomes and modern translation, fossilized today in the ribozyme peptidyl-transferase center of every ribosome and nucleotide cofactors.

pillars.name: Self-Sustaining RNA Polymerase Ribozyme Replication
pillars.claim: RNA polymerase ribozymes can catalyze accurate, high-fidelity replication of structured functional RNAs—including copies of themselves.

pillars.name: Solitary 'Naked RNA-First' Prebiotic Abiogenesis
pillars.claim: Pure canonical RNA spontaneously polymerized and replicated from prebiotic mixtures without early peptide cofactors, chimeric RNA-DNA backbones, or mineral/vesicle hosts.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree the ribosome's catalytic core is an RNA ribozyme proving an ancient RNA-centered translation stage existed, while acknowledging that pure canonical RNA faces major prebiotic strand-separation, hydrolysis, and synthesis hurdles.
steelman.theory_a_case: Every cell on Earth makes proteins using an RNA catalyst (the ribosome), uses nucleotide cofactors (ATP, NAD, FAD, CoA) for metabolism, and synthesizes DNA strictly by reducing ribonucleotides—while engineered RNA polymerase ribozymes now copy complex structured RNAs with >95 percent fidelity.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Prebiotic synthesis produces messy mixtures of ribo-, deoxyribo-, and alternative sugars plus amino acids simultaneously, and long RNA duplexes melt only at temperatures that rapidly hydrolyze RNA—making a pristine, peptide-free 'naked RNA' origin chemically fragile.
steelman.rival_b_name: RNP Coevolution & Chimeric Proto-Nucleic Acid World (Carter-Wills-Krishnamurthy-Hud)
steelman.rival_b_case: Because cyanosulfidic chemistry makes RNA precursors, amino acids, and lipids together, short abiotic peptides likely stabilized early RNA folds from Day 1 (RNP World), while heterogeneous RNA-DNA chimeras solve the duplex strand-separation paradox cleanly.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: RNP and proto-RNA alternatives lack direct extant molecular fossils proving non-canonical backbones (TNA/PNA) ever operated inside terrestrial ancestors prior to ribose-phosphate RNA.

episodes.label: Switches, Shadows, and Coding Rebels — King & Wilson's 99% Human-Chimp Paradox, Sean Carroll's Modular Enhancer Theory, Stickleback Pitx1 Pelvic Deletions, Drosophila Wing-Spot Enhancers, Hoekstra & Coyne's Coding-Locus Audit, Frankel's Shadow Enhancers & Lynch-Wagner's Modular Transcription Factors
episodes.notes: If human and chimpanzee proteins share roughly ninety-nine percent of their amino acid sequences—and mouse Pax6 or Hox proteins can functionally substitute for fruit-fly homologs across six hundred million years of evolution—what genetic mutations actually sculpt wings, fins, limbs, and cerebral cortices? This five-act adversarial deep dive places the Cis-Regulatory Evolution Hypothesis of Morphological Divergence on full genomic and developmental trial. Follow the arc from Mary-Claire King and Allan Wilson's classic 1975 Science discovery of the human-chimpanzee protein-anatomy paradox to Sean B. Carroll's foundational 2008 Cell synthesis arguing that modular cis-regulatory enhancers bypass lethal coding pleiotropy, vividized by Benjamin Prud'homme and Nicolas Gompel's convergent courtship wing-spot gains and losses at the Drosophila yellow locus and Yingguang Frank Chan and David Kingsley's recurrent fragile-DNA deletions of the Pitx1 Pel enhancer in pelvic-reduced freshwater sticklebacks. Then cross-examine the three landmark challenges that forced modern evo-devo to mature: Hopi Hoekstra and Jerry Coyne's fierce 2007 Evolution quantitative audit documenting abundant adaptive protein-coding mutations across pigmentation, sensory receptors, and physiology; Nicolas Frankel and David Stern's 2010 Nature discovery that redundant 'shadow enhancers' buffer shavenbaby development against single-enhancer hits except under thermal and genetic stress; and Kathryn Brayer, Vincent Lynch, and Gunter Wagner's ancestral protein resurrection proving mammalian HoxA11 evolved a novel placental Foxo1a protein-protein interaction via intramolecular allostery without catastrophic pleiotropy. Pause twice for Python-verified pleiotropic survival-funnel math, candidate-exon Bayesian ascertainment bias, and shadow-enhancer multiplicative failure rates, then leave with a pre-registered reciprocal CRISPR allele-swap protocol and a practical stealth field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Cis-Regulatory Evolution Hypothesis of Morphological Divergence
theory.core_claim: Macroevolutionary divergence in animal body plans and morphology is driven predominantly by mutations in modular cis-regulatory elements (enhancers and silencers) rather than protein-coding mutations, because modular enhancers alter gene expression in a single tissue or developmental stage without inducing lethal pleiotropy.
theory.verdict_2026: Cis-regulatory modularity is firmly established as a major engine of morphological evolution—exemplified by recurrent Pitx1 pelvic enhancer deletions in sticklebacks, wing-patterning enhancers in Heliconius butterflies and Drosophila, and human-accelerated regulatory elements (HARs) altering corticogenesis. However, the once-dogmatic claim that morphological adaptation proceeds almost exclusively via cis-regulation has been decisively moderated (Hoekstra & Coyne 2007; Stern & Orgogozo 2008): coding mutations in receptors, pigmentation enzymes (Mc1r), ion channels, and even transcription-factor interaction motifs contribute heavily to physiological and microevolutionary adaptation, with cis-regulatory dominance increasing primarily at deeper macroevolutionary timescales where pleiotropic constraints intensify.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely treat 'cis-regulatory evolution minimizes pleiotropy' as an absolute rule, ignoring recent single-cell and transgenic enhancer atlases showing that many developmental enhancers are themselves highly pleiotropic across multiple organs and that shadow-enhancer redundancy buffers many single cis-mutations.

historical_evolution.milestone: Mary-Claire King and Allan Wilson (Science) highlight 99 percent human–chimpanzee protein identity, proposing regulatory mutations drive anatomical divergence.

Stickleback Pitx1 enhancer deletions (Chan 2010), human-specific enhancer knock-ins, and comparative single-cell ATAC-seq quantify cis-vs-coding trade-offs across clades.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree that both cis-regulatory and protein-coding mutations drive real morphological adaptations, and that pleiotropic constraint—NOT raw mutational target size alone—governs which genetic locus fixes in evolution.
steelman.theory_a_case: Across deep macroevolutionary body-plan splits (stickleback pelvic loss via Pitx1 enhancer deletion, Heliconius wing mimicry, human HAR brain enhancers), knocking out conserved developmental TFs in coding regions is embryonic lethal—forcing evolution overwhelmingly onto modular cis-regulatory switches.

steelman.rival_b_name: Balanced Coding-Plus-Regulatory Architecture (Hoekstra-Coyne-Lynch-Wagner)
steelman.rival_b_case: Protein-coding changes in tissue-restricted enzymes, receptors, and modular short linear motifs inside TFs readily alter morphology without lethality—especially over microevolutionary timescales and following gene duplications that free paralogs from pleiotropy.

episodes.label: Leaky Borders on the Tree of Life: The Biological Species Concept, Porous Genomes, and the Genomic-Island Illusion — How one gene pool splits in two when hybrids keep mating; Ernst Mayr's allopatric Biological Species Concept & Coyne & Orr's 119-pair Drosophila isolation clock; Chung-I Wu's porous-genome revolution; Feder, Chilcote & Bush's sympatric Rhagoletis apple-maggot shift, Edelman's 20-genome Heliconius butterfly introgression web & Lamichhaney and the Grants' 3-generation Big Bird hybrid finch; Kevin De Queiroz's Unified Lineage Concept & Cruickshank & Hahn's proof that linked selection creates false F_ST speciation islands with low d_XY; migration-recombination & coalescent island math plus spotting speciation models in disguise
episodes.notes: If a species is defined by Ernst Mayr's textbook Biological Species Concept as a reproductively isolated, hermetically sealed gene pool, why do whole-genome sequences reveal rampant cross-species gene exchange across Heliconius butterflies, oaks, mosquitoes, Darwin's finches, and archaic hominins? This five-act adversarial deep dive places the Biological Species Concept and Speciation-with-Gene-Flow on full empirical trial. Begin with Mayr's allopatric orthodoxy and Jerry Coyne and H. Allen Orr's landmark 1989 comparative audit of 119 Drosophila pairs establishing Haldane's rule and prezygotic reinforcement, then trace Chung-I Wu's 2001 Genic View revolution recasting diverging genomes as selectively semi-permeable sieves rather than sealed vaults. Examine three extraordinary empirical triumphs of porous and non-allopatric speciation: Jeffrey Feder, Charles Chilcote, and Guy Bush's 1988 proof of sympatric host-race divergence in Rhagoletis pomonella apple maggot flies within 150 years, Sangeet Lamichhaney and Rosemary and Peter Grant's real-time genomic tracking of a reproductively isolated homoploid hybrid finch lineage ('Big Bird') arising in just three generations on Daphne Major, and Nathaniel Edelman and colleagues' twenty-genome Science map of recombination-structured introgression across Heliconius butterflies. Then confront two transformative critiques: Kevin De Queiroz's Unified General Lineage Concept dissolving fifty years of species-concept turf wars, and Tami Cruickshank and Matthew Hahn's 2014 Molecular Ecology bombshell proving that celebrated relative F_ST 'genomic islands of speciation' exhibited LOW absolute divergence d_XY—an artifact of linked background selection in allopatry! Pause twice for Python-verified effective-migration and F_ST-versus-d_XY coalescent calculations, plus a pre-registered Crucial Experiment protocol and stealth field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Biological Species Concept & Speciation-with-Gene-Flow
theory.core_claim: Ernst Mayr's Biological Species Concept (BSC) defines sexually reproducing species as reproductively isolated gene pools—classically presumed to diverge strictly in geographic isolation (allopatry)—whereas modern speciation genomics reveals that ecological divergence frequently proceeds with ongoing gene flow and persistent semi-permeable ('porous') genomic boundaries.
theory.verdict_2026: Reproductive isolation via Bateson–Dobzhansky–Muller (BDM) incompatibilities and prezygotic barriers remains the operational cornerstone of eukaryotic speciation biology, yet strict Mayrian allopatric-isolation orthodoxy has been fundamentally rewritten by whole-genome sequencing. Across Heliconius butterflies (Edelman et al. 2019 Science), Anopheles mosquitoes, Darwin's finches, oaks, and hominins, up to 10–40 percent of distinct sister-species genomes show pervasive historical and ongoing introgression, proving species boundaries are selectively semi-permeable rather than hermetically sealed. Meanwhile, early enthusiasm for interpreting 'genomic islands of divergence' as clean footprints of sympatric speciation-with-gene-flow has been tempered by proof that linked selection in low-recombination zones mimics divergence islands even under pure allopatry (Cruickshank & Hahn 2014).
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Genomics papers routinely interpret elevated F_ST 'genomic islands' between sister taxa as automatic proof of localized barrier loci resisting gene flow during parapatric/sympatric speciation, forgetting Cruickshank & Hahn's (2014) demonstration that absolute divergence (d_XY) must be checked because purifying/background selection in low-recombination regions inflates relative F_ST without any differential gene flow. Equally common is forcing the BSC onto asexual microbes, ring species, and fossils where phylogenetic/cohesion criteria apply.

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree reproductive isolation via BDM incompatibilities is fundamental to sexual eukaryotes, that introgression across distinct sister species (butterflies, oaks, finches, hominins) is far more common than Mayr thought, and that F_ST islands require absolute divergence (d_XY) checks to avoid linked-selection artifacts.
steelman.theory_a_case: Whole-genome sequencing of Heliconius butterflies (Edelman 2019 Science), Anopheles mosquitoes, and Darwin's finches reveals 10–40 percent genomic introgression between stable, morphologically distinct species—proving reproductive barriers operate selectively at key barrier loci while neutral or adaptive alleles cross species borders.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Cruickshank & Hahn (2014 Molecular Ecology) showed most headline 'genomic islands of speciation' actually show LOWER absolute divergence (d_XY), exposing linked purifying selection in low-recombination regions under classic allopatry rather than active sympatric barrier-locus resistance.
steelman.rival_b_name: Classical Allopatric BSC vs. Unified Lineage Species Concept (Mayr / de Queiroz)
steelman.rival_b_case: Most porous hybrid zones arise from secondary contact after an initial allopatric divergence phase rather than pure primary sympatric speciation—and de Queiroz's Unified Species Concept cleanly treats reproductive isolation, monophyly, and ecological distinctiveness as staggered operational criteria of one diverging lineage.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Strict Mayrian allopatric BSC cannot even classify asexual prokaryotes, fossil lineages, or ancient ring species—and underestimates how strongly adaptive introgression (such as mimicry wings in Heliconius or EPAS1 altitude genes in humans) fuels adaptive radiation.

episodes.label: Does Evolutionary Theory Need a Rethink? — The Extended Evolutionary Synthesis (Laland, Uller, West-Eberhard, Levis & Pfennig) vs. the Modern Synthesis (Charlesworth, Barton, Futuyma, Wray, Hoekstra & Welch)
episodes.notes: In October 2014, Nature published two competing manifestos under one provocative question: does evolutionary theory need an urgent rethink? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts the Extended Evolutionary Synthesis (EES) on full empirical and philosophical trial against the Updated Modern Synthesis. Walk from Slijper's bipedal goat and Conrad Waddington's heat-shocked fruit flies into Laland, Uller, Feldman, Sterelny, and Muller's four EES pillars — developmental bias, plasticity-first genetic accommodation, inclusive non-genetic inheritance, and reciprocal niche construction — backed by Mary Jane West-Eberhard's landmark synthesis, Levis and Pfennig's four-criterion spadefoot-toad tests, and Uller and Brakefield's regulatory-network bias framework. Then cross-examine every claim against the sharpest population-genetic and philosophical counterattacks: Charlesworth, Barton, and Charlesworth proving mutation-selection-drift math handles plasticity and niche feedbacks without radical revision, Douglas Futuyma highlighting counter-gradient selection against maladaptive ancestral plasticity, and John Welch diagnosing why evolutionary biology generates perennial rethink manifestos. Pause twice for step-by-step calculations — demonstrating how a 0.85 developmental covariance deflects natural selection by 57.9 degrees and flips a trait's evolutionary sign while epigenetic marks decay as f to the n, then proving why typical 5-line experimental evolution studies hold less than 10 percent power and engineering a 52-to-60-line CRISPR plasticity-ablation decisive trial — before concluding with a disciplined 2026 verdict and a stealth field guide for decoding Evo-Devo, plasticity, and epigenetics papers.
