theory.canonical_title: Higher-Order Thought (HOT) & Recurrent Processing Theories of Consciousness
theory.core_claim: Higher-Order Theories (Rosenthal, Lau, Brown) assert that a first-order sensory representation becomes conscious only when indexed or monitored by a higher-order metacognitive representation in prefrontal cortex; Recurrent Processing Theory (Lamme) counters that local horizontal and top-down feedback loops within sensory cortex suffice for rich phenomenal awareness even without prefrontal access or reportability.
theory.verdict_2026: Following the 2025 Cogitate stalemate between GNWT and IIT, Higher-Order Theories (especially Hakwan Lau's Perceptual Reality Monitoring, PRM) and Victor Lamme's Recurrent Processing Theory (RPT) have surged as the sharpest mechanistic rivals in consciousness science. Both command compelling experimental pillars—blindsight and prefrontal TMS metacognitive dissociations bolster HOT/PRM, whereas backward-masking disruption of early visual feedback (~100 ms) and Iconic Memory (Sperling) overflow experiments support RPT—yet both remain deadlocked over whether unreportable local recurrence truly carries subjective qualia or merely pre-conscious sensory readiness.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Empirical papers testing metacognitive confidence ratings often equate high metacognitive sensitivity (meta-d') with conscious perception, even though HOT theorists acknowledge dissociations between explicit post-decision confidence and first-order awareness. Conversely, RPT papers often cite Sperling partial-report superiority as proof of rich unreportable phenomenal 'overflow' without excluding post-dictive attentional reconstruction or low-level ensemble statistics.

historical_evolution.milestone: David Rosenthal formalizes philosophical Higher-Order Thought (HOT) theory; Victor Lamme distinguishes rapid unconscious feedforward sweep (<80 ms) from conscious recurrent feedback processing (>100 ms) in macaque V1.

Hakwan Lau and Richard Passingham show matched-performance visual conditions with different subjective awareness differentially recruit dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), grounding neurobiological HOT.

Richard Brown, Joseph LeDoux, and Hakwan Lau refine neurobiological HOT into Perceptual Reality Monitoring (PRM), while Lamme defends sensory recurrent processing against prefrontal lesion survival critiques.

Second-wave adversarial collaborations pit Higher-Order/PRM directly against Recurrent Processing and Predictive Processing using laminar high-field fMRI, optogenetics in rodents, and intracranial no-report masking.

pillars.name: Prefrontal Higher-Order Monitoring Is Necessary for Phenomenal Experience (HOT / PRM)
pillars.claim: A first-order sensory representation becomes subjectively conscious only when indexed by a higher-order metacognitive or reality-monitoring representation in prefrontal cortex.

pillars.name: Local Sensory Cortical Feedback Loops (~100 ms) Suffice for Phenomenal Consciousness (RPT)
pillars.claim: Horizontal and top-down recurrent feedback loops confined within sensory cortex generate rich phenomenal experience even without prefrontal access or verbal reportability.

pillars.name: Rapid Initial Feedforward Sensory Sweeps (<80 ms) Remain Unconscious
pillars.claim: The initial bottom-up feedforward wave through sensory hierarchy extracts complex categorical features and drives subliminal behavior without generating conscious qualia.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree rapid (<80 ms) feedforward sweeps operate unconsciously, that consciousness science requires no-report paradigms controlling for task performance (matched d'), and that the 2025 Cogitate stalemate left neither GNWT nor IIT decisively victorious.
steelman.theory_a_case: When first-order discrimination accuracy (d') is rigorously matched, subjective visibility changes track dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) activity (Lau & Passingham 2006), prefrontal TMS selectively degrades metacognitive awareness without lowering objective accuracy, and blindsight shows intact sensory discrimination without conscious experience.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Patients with massive bilateral prefrontal lesions retain vivid visual, auditory, and emotional experience, and high-field imaging often shows dlPFC signals reflect post-perceptual reporting or confidence computation rather than raw sensory qualia.
steelman.rival_b_name: Local Recurrent Processing & Phenomenal Overflow Theory (Lamme-Block)
steelman.rival_b_case: Disrupting feedback to V1 at ~100 ms via backward masking or occipital TMS abolishes visual awareness while sparing the earlier feedforward sweep, and Sperling partial-report paradigms suggest subjects experience far richer perceptual detail than prefrontal working memory can report.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Sperling 'overflow' can be explained by post-dictive attentional reconstruction or summary ensemble statistics rather than unreportable qualia, and robust local V1–V4 feedback can occur under deep masking or anesthesia without verified conscious perception.

episodes.label: Spacetime Blisters in Warm Wet Neurons — Penrose & Hameroff's Orch-OR Quantum Microtubule Theory, Tryptophan UV Superradiance & Terahertz Anesthetic Shifts vs. Tegmark's Femtosecond Decoherence, Gran Sasso's Underground X-Ray Test & Franks's GABAA Receptor Pharmacology
episodes.notes: Does conscious awareness ignite from classical action potentials racing across trillions of cortical synapses, or does every moment of subjective experience require non-computable quantum-gravitational wave-function collapse orchestrated inside neuronal cytoskeletal microtubules? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff's Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR) hypothesis on full physical, chemical, and neurobiological trial against classical neurocomputational theories of consciousness and ion-channel anesthetic pharmacology. Trace how Penrose derived gravitational objective reduction (tau equals hbar divided by E_G) from general-relativistic spacetime superposition conflicts while Hameroff proposed 13-protofilament tubulin lattices as biological quantum resonators, examining computational terahertz anesthetic docking models (Craddock et al. 2017) and genuine 2024 room-temperature ultraviolet superradiance measurements across mega-networks of microtubule tryptophans (Babcock et al. 2024). Then cross-examine the four devastating empirical counterstrikes: Max Tegmark's quantitative calculation proving 310-Kelvin cytoplasmic ion collisions decohere microtubule superpositions in 100 femtoseconds, Laura McKemmish and Noel Hush's physical-chemistry proof that GTP hydrolysis cannot pump Frohlich condensates and tubulin lacks an aromatic double-well switch, Sandro Donadi and Lajos Diosi's 2021 deep-underground Gran Sasso germanium X-ray test ruling out parameter-free gravitational collapse, and Nicholas Franks's stereoselective GABAA beta-3 knock-in mouse proof that surgical anesthesia tracks single amino-acid ion-channel swaps. Pause twice for Python-verified gravitational self-energy mass budgets and Gran Sasso X-ray exclusion pincer math, then leave with a pre-registered triple-knock-in plus NV-diamond quantum-thermometry Crucial Experiment and a practical field guide separating genuine picosecond quantum biology from macroscopic quantum-mind overreach.

theory.canonical_title: Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR / Quantum Microtubule Consciousness)
theory.core_claim: Consciousness arises not from classical synaptic computation alone, but from non-computable quantum gravitational wave-function collapse ('objective reduction') orchestrated inside coherent quantum superposition states of neuronal cytoskeletal microtubule tubulin dimers.
theory.verdict_2026: Orch-OR remains heavily challenged and outside mainstream neuroscience and physics consensus in 2026, facing three stacked hurdles: Max Tegmark's thermal decoherence bounds (femtosecond-to-picosecond collapse in warm wet brains vs. millisecond neural timescales), underground Gran Sasso experiments (Donadi et al., Nature Physics 2021) ruling out the simplest parameter-free Diósi–Penrose gravitational collapse model via absent spontaneous X-ray emission, and lack of any demonstration linking microtubule quantum coherence to behavioral consciousness. Intrigued interest persists on a strictly narrowed biophysical frontier—2024 experiments reported ultraviolet superradiance in tryptophan networks within microtubules (Babcock et al.) and anesthetic binding shifts in tubulin—which proponents cite as revisions, though demonstrating room-temperature optical excitons falls far short of macroscopic neural quantum computing or gravitational consciousness.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Advocates routinely conflate verified short-lived picosecond quantum optical effects in biological chromophores (tryptophan superradiance, photosynthetic exciton transfer) with millisecond-scale macroscopic quantum entanglement across whole neuronal populations required for Penrose's gravitational collapse. Critics, conversely, sometimes dismiss microtubule pharmacology entirely even though microtubule-stabilizing drugs genuinely modulate general anesthetic sensitivity via classical cytoskeletal/membrane-protein pathways.

historical_evolution.milestone: Roger Penrose (motivated by Gödel's incompleteness theorem and quantum gravity) and anesthesiologist Stuart Hameroff propose Orch-OR, locating non-algorithmic quantum collapse inside neuronal microtubules.

Physicist Max Tegmark calculates thermal decoherence times in warm brain microtubules (~10^-13 s), arguing environmental noise destroys superpositions at least ten orders of magnitude faster than neural firing.

Hameroff and Penrose revise Orch-OR toward faster megahertz microtubule vibrations; Donadi et al. (Nature Physics 2021) measure underground germanium X-ray limits ruling out the simplest Diósi–Penrose spontaneous collapse hypothesis.

Room-temperature tryptophan UV superradiance in microtubules (Babcock/Kurian 2024) and epothilone-B anesthetic-delay rodent studies (Wiest 2024) spark renewed biophysical testing without yet establishing macroscopic quantum neural computation.

episodes.label: Reflections in the Premotor Cortex — Rizzolatti & Gallese's Macaque Area F5 Mirror Neurons, Iacoboni's Context-Intention fMRI, Mukamel & Fried's Human Single-Unit Recordings, Hickok's Eight Problems & Dual-Stream Model, Heyes's Associative Sequence Learning & Vannuscorps-Caramazza's Motor-Free Comprehension Proofs
episodes.notes: When neurophysiologists in Parma, Italy, heard a microelectrode inside a macaque monkey's ventral premotor cortex crackle not only when the monkey grasped a raisin, but also when the monkey sat motionless watching a human experimenter grasp the same raisin, neuroscience appeared to have found its Rosetta Stone for social cognition. Within a decade, mirror neurons were hailed as the innate motor-simulation engine explaining human action understanding, mind-reading, empathy, speech evolution, and—under the 'broken mirror' hypothesis—autism spectrum disorder. This five-act adversarial deep dive places the Grand Mirror Neuron Hypothesis on rigorous empirical trial. Audit Vittorio Gallese, Giacomo Rizzolatti, and Laila Craighero's foundational macaque F5/PFG recordings, Marco Iacoboni's context-intention fMRI paradigm, and Roy Mukamel and Itzhak Fried's landmark intracranial recordings of 1,177 single neurons in human neurosurgical patients—including 'anti-mirror' cells that fire during execution yet shut down during observation. Then examine the devastating three-front counteroffensive: Gregory Hickok and Jonathan Venezia's neuropsychological double dissociations showing apraxic and aphasic patients comprehend actions and speech they cannot execute; Gilles Vannuscorps and Alfonso Caramazza's demonstrations that individuals born with congenital facial paralysis or absent upper limbs read lips and judge hand kinematics just like controls; and Cecilia Heyes and Caroline Catmur's Associative Sequence Learning experiments showing brief counter-mirror training reverses human mirror responses. Pause twice for Python-verified fMRI voxel-overlap, binomial discovery, Bayesian dissociation, and counter-mirror plasticity math, plus a pre-registered Crucial Experiment protocol.

theory.canonical_title: Mirror Neuron Action-Understanding & Empathy Hypothesis
theory.core_claim: Premotor and parietal 'mirror neurons'—which fire both when executing a goal-directed action and when observing another individual perform the same action—provide an innate, automatic motor-simulation mechanism underlying action understanding, mind-reading, empathy, language evolution, and (when dysfunctional) autism spectrum disorder.
theory.verdict_2026: The electrophysiological existence of visuomotor mirror neurons in macaque area F5/PFG and homologous human single-unit activity (Mukamel et al. 2010) is indisputable, yet the sweeping 'grand mirror-neuron theory' of action understanding, empathy, and 'broken-mirror' autism has suffered major empirical refutation and contraction. Gregory Hickok's landmark synthesis, neuropsychological double dissociations (apraxic patients who cannot perform actions yet understand them effortlessly, and congenitally limb-absent individuals with intact action comprehension), and Cecilia Heyes's Associative Sequence Learning model demonstrate that mirror properties are largely domain-general sensorimotor associations acquired through Hebbian experience—playing a modest predictive-motor role rather than grounding human social cognition or autism.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Cognitive and clinical papers still casually invoke 'the human mirror neuron system' from coarse fMRI blood-flow overlap in premotor cortex (which cannot resolve whether the same neurons fire during observation and execution) and cite the debunked 'broken mirror' theory of autism despite overwhelming null replications (Southgate & Hamilton 2008; Hamilton 2013).

historical_evolution.milestone: Giacomo Rizzolatti, Vittorio Gallese, Luciano Fadiga, and Leonardo Fogassi discover mirror neurons in macaque ventral premotor cortex (area F5) and propose direct motor simulation for action understanding.

Mirror neurons are extrapolated into grand claims for empathy, language, culture, and 'broken mirror' autism (Ramachandran, Iacoboni); Roy Mukamel records genuine single-unit mirror activity in human neurosurgical patients (SMA and medial temporal lobe).

Gregory Hickok ('Eight Problems for the Mirror Neuron Theory,' 2009; 'The Myth of Mirror Neurons,' 2014), Antonia Hamilton, and Cecilia Heyes dismantle causal motor-simulation and broken-mirror autism claims using lesion dissociations and associative learning experiments.

Modern consensus reframes mirror neurons as plastic, learned visuomotor predictive units supporting sensorimotor coordination and motor-timing prediction rather than a dedicated innate module for empathy or conceptual semantics.

episodes.label: Safe Havens, Strange Situations, and the Transmission Gap: Bowlby & Ainsworth's Attachment Theory vs. Temperament Genetics, Lifespan Plasticity & Alloparenting Anthropology — How John Bowlby and Mary Ainsworth overturned Freudian cupboard-love dogma via ethological control systems and the 8-episode Strange Situation; Hazan & Shaver's 1987 romantic extension, Nelson et al.'s 2007 Bucharest Early Intervention RCT proving a <24-month sensitive period & Fraley & Roisman's 2D anxiety-avoidance lessons; De Wolff & van IJzendoorn's 66-study r = 0.24 Transmission Gap, Fraley's 2002 prototype-vs-revisionist decay, Heidi Keller's 2018 PNAS dismantling of WEIRD maternal monotropy & Barbaro et al.'s 2017 twin/adoption r_GE critique; BEIP NNT, autoregressive stability & Falconer path math plus spotting attachment assumptions in disguise
episodes.notes: Few psychological theories have reshaped pediatric hospital wards, orphanages, psychotherapy couches, and modern dating vocabulary as profoundly as John Bowlby and Mary Salter Ainsworth's Attachment Theory—yet few scientific frameworks suffer a wider gulf between deterministic pop-culture mythology and rigorous empirical reality. Trace the dramatic mid-century rebellion against Freudian and behaviorist 'cupboard love' secondary-drive dogma, culminating in Ainsworth and Silvia Bell's 1970 Strange Situation laboratory drama and the landmark 1978 Patterns of Attachment Baltimore monograph that revealed how sensitive caregiving calibrates infant secure, avoidant, and resistant strategies. Follow the theory's boldest empirical triumphs: Cindy Hazan and Phillip Shaver's 1987 extension into adult romantic love, Charles Nelson, Charles Zeanah, and Nathan Fox's historic 2007 Bucharest Early Intervention Project randomized controlled trial proving a sensitive window before 24 months for rescuing institutionalized children's cognitive and socioemotional development, and R. Chris Fraley and Glenn Roisman's 2019 synthesis replacing discrete personality boxes with continuous anxiety and avoidance dimensions. Then cross-examine four razor-sharp empirical challenges: Marianne De Wolff and Marinus van IJzendoorn's 1997 meta-analysis exposing the 94-percent 'Transmission Gap' (r = 0.24), Fraley's 2002 dynamic modeling of modest infant-to-adult stability, Heidi Keller's 2018 PNAS anthropological critique of WEIRD dyadic maternal exclusivity versus species-typical alloparenting networks, and Nicole Barbaro and colleagues' 2017 behavioral-genetic dissection of passive gene-environment confounding—complete with Python-verified Bucharest NNT, prototype decay, and Falconer path calculations.

theory.canonical_title: Attachment Theory (Bowlby & Ainsworth)
theory.core_claim: Human infants possess an evolved attachment behavioral system that maintains proximity to responsive caregivers as a 'secure base' and 'safe haven,' crystallizing internal working models of self and others (categorized as secure, anxious/ambivalent, avoidant, or disorganized) that shape emotion regulation and relational expectations across development.
theory.verdict_2026: Attachment Theory remains the dominant developmental paradigm for caregiver–infant socioemotional bonding in 2026, powerfully backed by cross-cultural Strange Situation studies, foster-care institutional deprivation trials (Bucharest Early Intervention Project), and adult dimensional attachment research (anxiety vs. avoidance axes). Significant refinements have pruned earlier deterministic overclaims: behavioral genetics and longitudinal cohorts (NICHD SECCYD, Fraley & Roisman) show that infant attachment is only moderately stable into adulthood (r roughly 0.15–0.25), is shaped bidirectionally by infant temperament and broad socio-ecological stress rather than maternal sensitivity alone, and functions better as continuous dimensional spectra than rigid lifelong personality boxes.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Clinical and pop-psychology literature routinely treats infant attachment categories as immutable destiny ('monotropic maternal determinism'), ignoring cross-cultural alloparenting norms (Keller 2018), paternal/multiple-caregiver networks, genetic confounding of parenting-outcome correlations, and substantial adult relational plasticity. Many researchers also mistake the adult self-report romantic attachment questionnaire (ECR) for the same construct as the developmental Adult Attachment Interview (AAI), despite their remarkably low empirical correlation (r ~ 0.09).

historical_evolution.milestone: John Bowlby synthesizes ethology (Konrad Lorenz, Harry Harlow's rhesus comfort experiments) with psychoanalysis to formulate evolutionary Attachment Theory.

Mary Ainsworth operationalizes attachment quality through the laboratory 'Strange Situation' procedure, identifying secure (B), insecure-avoidant (A), and insecure-resistant (C) patterns (with Main & Solomon adding disorganized D in 1986).

Cindy Hazan and Phillip Shaver extend attachment into adult romantic styles; R. Chris Fraley demonstrates that continuous taxometric dimensions (attachment anxiety and avoidance) outperform discrete typologies.
Cross-cultural developmental anthropology (Heidi Keller), twin studies, and long-term NICHD/Minnesota cohorts refine attachment into a dynamic, multi-caregiver, gene-by-environment relational model.

episodes.label: Biased Bugs or Bounded Optimality? — Kahneman & Tversky's Prospect Theory, Evans–Stanovich Dual-Process Architecture & the 19-Country Replication vs. Gigerenzer's Ecological Rationality, Lieder–Griffiths Resource Rationality, De Neys's Logical Intuitions & Gal–Rucker's Loss-Aversion Audit
episodes.notes: Why does the same person buy fire insurance on Monday and a lottery ticket on Friday—and why do we turn fiercely risk-averse for gains yet suddenly gamble to escape a sure loss? This five-act adversarial deep dive examines behavioral science's most influential paradigm: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky's reference-dependent Prospect Theory (Econometrica 1979; Nobel lecture AER 2003), Jonathan Evans and Keith Stanovich's autonomous Type 1 vs. working-memory Type 2 Dual-Process refinement (2013), and Kai Ruggeri et al.'s landmark 19-country, 4,098-participant multinational replication (Nature Human Behaviour 2020) confirming 12 of 13 classic effects. Then four rival insurgencies take the stand: Gerd Gigerenzer and Wolfgang Gaissmaier's Ecological Rationality (Annual Review of Psychology 2010), proving fast-and-frugal heuristics beat complex multiple regression out-of-sample through the bias-variance trade-off; Falk Lieder and Thomas Griffiths's Resource-Rational Analysis (BBS 2020), deriving anchoring and rare-event overweighting as mathematically optimal algorithms under finite neural budgets; Wim De Neys (BBS 2022), dismantling strict fast-and-slow exclusivity by revealing rapid logical intuitions inside speeded dual-task trials; and David Gal and Derek Rucker (2018), exposing how status-quo inertia masquerades as universal 2:1 loss aversion. Pause twice for step-by-step math—first computing Prospect Theory's exact certainty, reflection, 14.5-fold rare-event, and USD 274 mixed-gamble flips, and second deriving the exact N* = 42 bias-variance crossover where equal-weight Tallying beats OLS regression plus a 162-subject pre-registered two-response trial power floor—closing with a disciplined 2026 synthesis and a stealth-jargon field guide for working behavioral researchers.

theory.canonical_title: Dual-Process & Prospect Theory vs. Ecological & Resource Rationality
theory.core_claim: Kahneman and Tversky's Heuristics-and-Biases / Prospect Theory and Evans–Stanovich Dual-Process Theory model human choice as an interplay between fast, autonomous heuristic intuition (Type 1) and effortful, working-memory-limited deliberation (Type 2), governed by reference-dependent value functions and nonlinear probability weighting; Ecological Rationality (Gigerenzer) and Resource Rationality (Griffiths, Lieder) counter that these same heuristics are adaptive, variance-reducing, or computationally optimal under real-world time, memory, and uncertainty constraints.
theory.verdict_2026: Prospect Theory's descriptive patterns remain remarkably robust in 2026—verified across 19 countries and 4,098 participants by Ruggeri et al. (Nature Human Behaviour 2020, replicating 12 of 13 classic effects)—making behavioral economics a dominant scientific paradigm, yet its classical cognitive interpretation is undergoing deep revision. Large meta-analyses (Gal & Rucker 2018; Yechiam 2019) challenged universal 2:1 loss aversion for small/moderate stakes, Wim De Neys (BBS 2023) dismantled the strict 'Type 1 = biased, Type 2 = logical' exclusivity dogma by demonstrating rapid 'logical intuitions,' and Resource-Rational analysis increasingly unifies both camps by deriving Prospect Theory's S-curve and fast-and-frugal heuristics from bounded Bayesian optimization.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Applied behavioral-science papers routinely treat System 1 and System 2 as two anatomically distinct brain modules (or reified homunculi) rather than functional modes, and assume every deviation from Expected Utility Theory proves human irrationality without checking whether the behavior maximizes accuracy under bounded cognitive cost or non-stationary natural statistics. Writers also still cite the 2:1 loss-aversion constant as a biological universal despite strong context, stake-size, and status-quo moderation.

historical_evolution.milestone: Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman map availability, representativeness, and anchoring heuristics and publish Prospect Theory (Econometrica 1979), overturning Expected Utility Theory.

Gerd Gigerenzer launches Ecological Rationality showing fast-and-frugal heuristics beat complex regressions out-of-sample ('less-is-more'); Kahneman publishes 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' (2011), popularizing System 1/System 2.

Evans and Stanovich tighten Dual-Process Theory into autonomous Type 1 vs. working-memory Type 2; Ruggeri et al. (2020) confirm cross-cultural Prospect Theory robustness while Lieder and Griffiths formalize Resource-Rational cognition (BBS 2020).

De Neys (BBS 2023) advances Dual-Process 2.0 centered on parallel competing intuitions and conflict monitoring; 'choice-architecture nudges' face sobering meta-analytic publication-bias corrections (Maier et al. 2022).

rivals: Ecological Rationality & Fast-and-Frugal Heuristics (Gigerenzer)
Resource-Rational / Bounded-Optimality Cognitive Models (Lieder & Griffiths)
Single-Process Unimodel & Parallel Logical-Intuition Models (Kruglanski / De Neys)
Classical Neoclassical Expected Utility Theory (von Neumann–Morgenstern)
theory.falsification_criteria: Strict classical Dual-Process exclusivity is falsified whenever cognitive load or extreme time pressure leaves normative logical/probabilistic conflict detection intact; strict Ecological Rationality fails where simple heuristics systematically underperform learnable Bayesian cues in real-world stationary environments.
theory.stealth_support: Your study shows asymmetric valuation of losses vs. gains around a shifting reference point, probability overweighting of rare events, or systematic shift from heuristic error to normative accuracy when working-memory load is removed.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study finds fast-and-frugal heuristics outperform full weighting out-of-sample (Ecological Rationality), logical conflict detection fires automatically under extreme time pressure (dissolving strict Type 1 vs Type 2), or loss aversion disappears when status-quo inertia is controlled.

pillars.name: Reference-Dependent Prospect Value & Probability Weighting
pillars.claim: Human choice under risk systematically exhibits S-shaped reference-point valuation (concave for gains, convex for losses) and overweighting of small probabilities.

pillars.name: Universal 2:1 Loss Aversion Constant
pillars.claim: Losses universally loom roughly twice as large as equivalent gains across contexts, stake sizes, and decision frames.

pillars.name: Strict Type 1 (Biased) vs. Type 2 (Logical) Exclusivity
pillars.claim: Normative logical and probabilistic reasoning belongs exclusively to slow, effortful Type 2 deliberation, whereas fast Type 1 intuition generates biased heuristic errors.

pillars.name: Ecological & Resource-Rational Optimization
pillars.claim: Apparent biases and fast-and-frugal heuristics represent computationally optimal adaptations to real-world cue redundancy, finite time, and bounded working memory.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree that human judgment systematically departs from unbounded Expected Utility maximization, that Prospect Theory's qualitative framing and probability-weighting patterns replicate globally, and that strict anatomical 'System 1 vs. System 2 brain modules' is a retired oversimplification.
steelman.theory_a_case: Across 19 nations and 4,098 participants (Ruggeri et al. 2020), 12 of 13 classic Prospect Theory predictions replicated cleanly; humans reliably exhibit base-rate errors, anchoring, and framing reversals that predict real financial, medical, and legal mistakes far better than classical rational-actor economics.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: Two-response time-pressure studies (De Neys 2023) demonstrate that people detect logical and base-rate conflicts rapidly inside fast intuitive processing—dismantling strict Type 1 = biased vs. Type 2 = logical exclusivity—while Gal & Rucker (2018) and Yechiam (2019) showed 2:1 loss aversion…

episodes.label: Four Slots, Shared Juice, or Activated Schemas? — Baddeley's Episodic Buffer, Sweller's Worked-Example Cognitive Load & Vogel's CDA Plateau vs. Cowan's Magical Number 4, Ma, Husain & Bays's Continuous Resource & Postle's Sensory Recruitment
episodes.notes: Why can the human mind store millions of lifetime facts effortlessly yet choke the instant an algebra worksheet or air-traffic display demands juggling five novel variables at once—and is online thought housed in dedicated anatomical buffer boxes or inside temporarily lit-up sensory cortices? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Alan Baddeley's Multicomponent Working Memory architecture and John Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) on full empirical trial. Trace how Baddeley and Hitch overturned unitary short-term memory, why prose recall in amnesics forced Baddeley to add the multimodal Episodic Buffer, how Sweller, van Merrienboer, Paas, Kirschner, and Clark proved unguided means-ends discovery learning exhausts finite working memory while worked examples accelerate novice schema building, and how Edward Vogel and Maro Machizawa caught individual K-slot plateaus in human contralateral delay-activity brainwaves. Then cross-examine three formidable rival paradigms: Nelson Cowan's Embedded-Processes model replacing separate buffers with a four-chunk focus of attention atop activated long-term memory, Wei Ji Ma, Masud Husain, and Paul Bays's continuous-resource psychophysics proving recall precision decays smoothly from N=1 without fixed slot walls, and Bradley Postle's sensory-recruitment fMRI evidence alongside the collapse of commercial n-back IQ brain training. Pause twice for Python-verified Pashler-Cowan K-capacity, Paas instructional efficiency, and divisive-normalization precision math, plus a pre-registered crucial experiment.

theory.canonical_title: Multicomponent Working Memory & Cognitive Load Theory (Baddeley / Sweller)
theory.core_claim: Baddeley and Hitch propose that active online cognition operates via a capacity-limited multicomponent architecture—an attentional Central Executive coordinating domain-specific Phonological Loop, Visuospatial Sketchpad, and Episodic Buffer stores—while Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory deduces that instructional design must minimize extraneous load so finite working memory can build long-term schemas.
theory.verdict_2026: Limited-capacity active maintenance and its direct link to complex learning (Cognitive Load Theory's worked-example, split-attention, and expertise-reversal effects) form a dominant, well-replicated pillar of cognitive and educational psychology. Mechanistically, however, Baddeley's discrete 'buffer boxes' face major competition from Nelson Cowan's Embedded-Processes model (working memory as the currently activated subset of long-term memory inside a ~4-chunk focus of attention) and Bays/Ma continuous-resource models (flexible precision allocation rather than fixed slots), while commercial 'working-memory brain training' transfers (e.g., dual n-back boosting fluid IQ) have overwhelmingly failed rigorous active-control meta-analyses (Melby-Lervåg & Hulme).
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Educational papers frequently treat George Miller's classic '7 plus or minus 2' span as raw working-memory capacity (ignoring chunking and Cowan's true unchunked limit of ~3–4 items) and circularly infer 'high cognitive load' from poor test scores without independently measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane load. Cognitive-training papers also routinely conflate near-transfer practice gains on trained span tasks with broad far-transfer gains in general intelligence.

historical_evolution.milestone: Alan Baddeley and Graham Hitch replace Atkinson–Shiffrin's unitary short-term store with the multicomponent Working Memory model; John Sweller formulates Cognitive Load Theory from worked-example problem-solving experiments.

Nelson Cowan launches the Embedded-Processes model and demonstrates the ~4-chunk core focus-of-attention limit; Baddeley adds the multimodal 'Episodic Buffer' (2000) to interface working and long-term memory.

Wei Ji Ma, Paul Bays, and Masud Husain challenge discrete 'slot' limits with continuous shared-resource precision models; Melby-Lervåg and Hulme's meta-analyses debunk far-transfer claims of working-memory brain training.

Activity-silent synaptic-weight working memory (Stokes/Miller) bridges neural biophysics with Cowan's activated-LTM view, while Sweller integrates CLT with evolutionary 'biologically primary vs. secondary' knowledge distinctions.

episodes.label: Hot Tension or Cold Inference? — Festinger & Carlsmith's One-Dollar vs. Twenty-Dollar Peg Experiment, Zanna & Cooper's Arousal Pill, Lieberman's Amnesic Paradox vs. Daryl Bem's Self-Perception, Chen & Risen's Free-Choice Theorem & Vaidis's 39-Lab Replication
episodes.notes: Why did Stanford undergraduates paid just one dollar to tell a waiting classmate that an excruciatingly dull spool-packing and peg-turning chore was thrilling walk out genuinely believing the task was fun—while classmates paid twenty dollars for telling the exact same lie still rated it boring? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Leon Festinger's Theory of Cognitive Dissonance on full empirical and mathematical trial against Daryl Bem's Self-Perception Theory, revealed-preference selection mathematics, and hierarchical predictive-consistency models. Follow the arc from Festinger's infiltration of a Chicago UFO doomsday cult and his landmark 1959 forced-compliance experiment with James Carlsmith, through Mark Zanna and Joel Cooper's ingenious 1974 placebo-pill study proving aversive physiological arousal drives counter-attitudinal belief change, and Matthew Lieberman's puzzling 2001 finding that anterograde amnesics spread chosen alternatives without remembering their choice. Then witness three seismic reckonings: Bem's 1967 cold self-inference critique, Keith Chen and Jane Risen's devastating 2010 mathematical proof that over fifty years of Brehm Free-Choice studies in humans, amnesics, toddlers, and monkeys confounded choice-induced attitude change with noisy revealed preferences, and David Vaidis's 2024 39-laboratory Registered Replication Report across 4,898 participants exposing the exact fragility and modest true scale of induced compliance.

theory.canonical_title: Cognitive Dissonance vs. Self-Perception & Predictive Consistency
theory.core_claim: Leon Festinger proposed that holding psychologically incompatible cognitions—especially freely choosing counter-attitudinal behavior—generates an aversive drive state ('cognitive dissonance') that motivates attitude change, rationalization, or selective information avoidance to restore consistency.
theory.verdict_2026: Cognitive dissonance remains a genuinely robust phenomenon in 2026, yet its classic paradigm has been dramatically sharpened by both methodological audits and mechanistic reconceptualization. A massive 39-lab Registered Replication Report (Vaidis et al., Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science 2024; N = 4,898) confirmed a real but smaller induced-compliance attitude-change effect (d ~ 0.17–0.21) when participants write counter-attitudinal essays under perceived free choice; meanwhile, the famous 'free-choice spreading of alternatives' paradigm was exposed by Chen & Risen (2010) as partly a statistical artifact of revealed preexisting preferences, requiring blind-choice designs (which still show smaller genuine revaluation). Mechanistically, modern theories integrate Daryl Bem's self-perception inference (for weak initial attitudes), Harmon-Jones's action-based model (resolving conflicting action tendencies via anterior cingulate cortex), and predictive-coding error minimization.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely cite the classic Brehm 'free-choice paradigm' (rating two equally liked items, choosing one, and re-rating the chosen item higher) without controlling for the Chen & Risen (2010) statistical selection artifact, which generates identical 'spreading of alternatives' even in completely non-dissonant noisy rating agents. Many also use 'cognitive dissonance' loosely to describe any hypocrisy or disagreement, missing Festinger's specific requirement of aversive physiological arousal triggered by voluntary commitment.

historical_evolution.milestone: Leon Festinger publishes 'A Theory of Cognitive Dissonance'; Festinger and Carlsmith run the famous 1-dollar vs. 20-dollar induced-compliance experiment showing smaller incentives produce greater attitude shift.

Daryl Bem challenges aversive arousal with Self-Perception Theory (inferring one's own attitude by observing one's behavior); Joel Cooper (New Look), Claude Steele (Self-Affirmation), and Eddie Harmon-Jones (Action-Based Model) refine boundary conditions.

M. Keith Chen and Jane Risen (JPSP) uncover a subtle mathematical artifact inflating 50 years of free-choice dissonance studies, prompting stricter blind-choice neuroimaging and behavioral designs (Izuma, Sharot).

Vaidis et al. (2024, 39 labs) confirms a real but modest induced-compliance effect under high choice, while cognitive neuroscience maps dissonance conflict to dACC/anterior insula prediction-error circuits.

pillars.name: Aversive Physiological Arousal Drive vs. Self-Perception & Predictive Consistency
pillars.claim: Attitude change is propelled specifically by an aversive physiological arousal state rather than cool Bemian self-inference or action-readiness / predictive-coding error minimization.

steelman.settled_ground: Both camps agree induced-compliance attitude shifts are real though smaller than 1959 textbook estimates (Vaidis et al. 2024, N = 4,898), that Chen & Risen (2010) proved classic unblinded free-choice designs suffer a mathematical selection artifact, and that dACC/anterior insula activate strongly during value-choice conflicts.
steelman.theory_a_case: Festinger and Carlsmith's counter-intuitive 1-dollar vs. 20-dollar inverse-incentive finding, Vaidis's 39-lab induced-compliance confirmation, blind-choice neuroimaging designs recovering genuine post-choice revaluation, and Harmon-Jones's action-based dACC conflict model confirm active motivational tension resolves incompatible action commitments.
steelman.theory_a_hardest: The classic induced-compliance effect is modest (d ~ 0.17–0.21) and fails reliably when participants have weak initial attitudes, half a century of Brehm free-choice papers were severely inflated by Chen & Risen's revealed-preference artifact, and physiological arousal proves surprisingly hard to…
steelman.rival_b_name: Self-Perception Theory (Bem), Revealed-Preference Artifacts (Chen-Risen) & Predictive Consistency
steelman.rival_b_case: Daryl Bem showed that when prior internal attitudes are vague, people coolly infer their beliefs from their own uncoerced actions exactly as an outside observer would—no aversive drive needed—while predictive-coding and Bayesian consistency accounts unify dissonance without invoking vague Freudian-style tension metaphors.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Pure cool self-perception struggles to explain why misattribution-of-arousal manipulations (attributing tension to a placebo pill) attenuate attitude change for strongly held counter-attitudinal commitments or why dACC/anterior insula conflict signals predict subsequent preference shifts.

episodes.label: Monolithic Engine or Emergent Network? — Spearman's Positive Manifold, Carroll's 461-Dataset CHC Three-Stratum Synthesis, Deary's P-FIT Neuroscience & Jansen's 269k Polygenic Brain-Volume Loci vs. van der Maas's Dynamic Mutualism, Kovacs & Conway's Process Overlap Theory & Ritchie & Tucker-Drob's 600k Schooling Meta-Analysis
episodes.notes: Why does nearly every reliable test of human reasoning, vocabulary, spatial rotation, memory, and processing speed correlate positively with every other—and does that universal positive manifold prove the brain runs on a single monolithic general-intelligence engine? This five-act adversarial deep dive places General Intelligence (the g-Factor) and the Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) Three-Stratum Hierarchy on full empirical trial. Follow Charles Spearman's 1904 invention of factor analysis and attenuation correction through Raymond Cattell and John Horn's fluid-versus-crystallized split to John B. Carroll's monumental 1993 re-analysis of 461 datasets, alongside Ian Deary's parieto-frontal white-matter and Lothian longevity syntheses and Philip Jansen's 269,867-person genome-wide polygenic brain-volume analyses. Then witness three devastating theoretical and quasi-experimental counterstrikes against reifying statistical g as a single causal entity: Han van der Maas's Dynamic Mutualism proof that developmental reciprocity among completely uncorrelated modules generates an identical g-factor, Kristof Kovacs and Andrew Conway's Process Overlap Theory modeling g as a formative executive working-memory bottleneck that predicts Spearman's Law of Diminishing Returns, and Stuart Ritchie and Elliot Tucker-Drob's 600,000-participant compulsory-schooling meta-analysis proving each extra year of education causally lifts IQ by one to five points via specific skill gains rather than latent g. Pause twice for Python-verified Schmid-Leiman, McDonald's hierarchical omega, and mutualism equilibrium proofs, plus a pre-registered longitudinal Head-to-Head protocol.

theory.canonical_title: General Intelligence (g-Factor) & Cattell–Horn–Carroll (CHC) Hierarchy
theory.core_claim: Performance across diverse cognitive tests exhibits a universal 'positive manifold'—all mental abilities correlate positively—captured quantitatively by a hierarchical Cattell–Horn–Carroll (CHC) architecture headed by a higher-order general factor (g) above broad strata such as fluid reasoning (Gf), crystallized knowledge (Gc), processing speed, and working memory.
theory.verdict_2026: As a psychometric description and predictive construct, the positive manifold and the CHC hierarchy are among the most robustly replicated empirical findings in all of psychology—replicated across over a century of batteries, culturally diverse cohorts, and massive genomic/neuroimaging biobanks (UK Biobank), robustly predicting educational, occupational, and health-longevity outcomes. However, the causal ontology of g remains actively refined in 2026: factor analysis alone cannot prove g is a single unitary brain engine ('reflective latent entity'). Process Overlap Theory (Kovacs & Conway 2016) and Dynamic Mutualism (van der Maas et al. 2006) demonstrate that a statistical g-factor emerges naturally without any single general brain module—either from overlapping executive-attention bottlenecks sampled across tasks or from positive developmental reciprocal coupling among initially independent cognitive skills.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Both proponents and critics routinely commit 'reification of g'—treating a statistical principal factor extracted from correlation matrices as proof of a single monolithic biological 'mental energy' organ (Spearman's original reification), whereas Mutualism and Process Overlap Theory produce mathematically identical positive manifolds from interacting networks of distinct cognitive processes. Meanwhile, popular education frameworks still promote Howard Gardner's 'Multiple Intelligences' despite lacking psychometric discriminant validity for independent cognitive modules.

historical_evolution.milestone: Charles Spearman discovers the positive manifold and introduces factor analysis and general intelligence (g); Raymond Cattell and John Horn bifurcate g into Fluid (Gf) and Crystallized (Gc) intelligence.
John B. Carroll re-analyzes 461 classic psychometric datasets ('Human Cognitive Abilities') to establish the three-stratum taxonomy merged with Cattell–Horn into the CHC consensus model.

Han van der Maas formulates Dynamic Mutualism showing developmental network interactions produce g without a single latent cause; Kristof Kovacs and Andrew Conway introduce Process Overlap Theory modeling g as a formative executive-bottleneck index.

Million-sample GWAS (Savage et al. 2018; Lee et al. 2018) confirm extreme polygenicity (thousands of small brain-expressed variants) and gene–environment interplay, while structural-network neuroimaging links g to global frontoparietal network integration efficiency (P-FIT).

episodes.label: Automatic Social & Behavioral Priming ('Florida Effect' / Money Priming) — Subtle, incidental exposure to semantic stereotypes or abstract symbols (e.g., unscrambling elderly words like 'Florida' and 'bingo,' viewing play money, or holding warm beverages) automatically activates unconscious behavioral schemas that cause dramatic, unwitting changes in walking speed, intelligence test performance, helpfulness, or political attitudes.
episodes.notes: Automatic goal/behavioral 'social priming'—once celebrated as a pillar of unconscious social cognition and featured prominently in Kahneman's 'Thinking, Fast and Slow'—has been comprehensively superseded after catastrophic, systematic replication failures across the 2010s and 2020s. Whereas narrow, millisecond-scale lexical/semantic associative priming (Meyer & Schvaneveldt 1971) remains an intact cognitive phenomenon, complex behavioral social priming collapsed in independent preregistered tests: Doyen et al. (2012) refuted Bargh's elderly-walking 'Florida effect' (and showed experimenter expectancy drove the illusion); Shanks et al. (2013) failed across nine experiments to replicate 'professor priming' boosting trivia scores; Many Labs 1 & 2 toppled flag priming, currency priming, and cleanliness-morality priming; and Kahneman himself publicly retracted his endorsement of the social-priming chapter as a cautionary emblem of underpowered science.

episodes.label: Are Emotions Hard-Wired or Constructed? — Theory of Constructed Emotion (Barrett) vs. Basic Emotion Theory (Ekman), Siegel's 202-Study Autonomic Meta-Analysis, Barrett's Facial Audit & Cowen–Keltner's 27-Emotion / 144-Country Counteroffensive
episodes.notes: Can an airport camera, hiring algorithm, or smartwatch actually read anger or fear straight off your face and heartbeat—or does multibillion-dollar Emotion AI rest on a shattered twentieth-century myth? This five-act adversarial deep dive stages affective science's fiercest paradigm war: Paul Ekman's classic 1992 Basic Emotion Theory, which treats discrete emotions as evolutionarily conserved biological affect programs with universal facial signals and autonomic signatures, against Lisa Feldman Barrett's 2017 Theory of Constructed Emotion, which recasts emotions as variable, context-tailored biological populations built on the fly by a predictive brain categorizing interoceptive core affect during allostatic energy regulation. Walk through all six live-verified landmark papers—from Ekman (Cognition and Emotion 1992) and Barrett (SCAN 2017), through Siegel et al.'s 2018 Psychological Bulletin meta-analysis of 202 autonomic studies and Barrett, Adolphs, Marsella, Martinez, and Pollak's 2019 Psychological Science in the Public Interest audit showing people scowl in anger only roughly 25 to 30 percent of the time, straight into the formidable UC Berkeley counteroffensive: Cowen and Keltner's 2017 PNAS discovery of 27 distinct emotional varieties bridged by continuous gradients across 2,185 videos and Cowen et al.'s 2021 Nature analysis of 6 million videos from 144 countries revealing 70 percent cross-regional preservation of 16 facial expressions in real-world contexts. Pause twice for Python-verified calculations—first using Bayes' Theorem to prove why 30 percent scowl reliability yields an 86.4 percent false-positive rate in real life alongside 93.5 percent anger-fear autonomic overlap, and second exposing how forced-choice valence-arousal elimination inflates 30 percent free-labeling accuracy to 65 percent while cultural clustering (DEFF = 10.2) collapses two-society field studies to 22 percent power—before designing a pre-registered 16-society context-masked causal protocol and a sixteen-fingerprint field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Theory of Constructed Emotion (Barrett) vs. Basic Emotion Theory (Ekman)
theory.core_claim: Basic Emotion Theory (Ekman, Izard, Panksepp, Keltner) posits a small set of evolutionarily conserved, pan-cultural affect programs (e.g., anger, fear, joy, disgust, sadness, surprise) with dedicated neural circuits and universal facial/autonomic fingerprints; Lisa Feldman Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion counters that emotions have no biological fingerprints and are instead ad-hoc conceptual categorizations constructed predictively from domain-general interoceptive 'core affect' (valence and arousal), context, and learned cultural emotion concepts.
theory.verdict_2026: Affective science remains locked in a vibrant, unresolved paradigm contest in 2026, with neither extreme securing total victory. Barrett's side scored major empirical blows via meta-analyses showing high physiological variability within single emotion labels (Siegel et al. 2018), poor one-to-one mapping between posed facial muscle movements and real-world inner feelings (Barrett et al., Psychological Science in the Public Interest 2019), and indigenous cross-cultural studies (Himba, Trobriand) showing forced-choice universality collapses under free labeling. Basic/functional emotion theorists (Cowen & Keltner, Adolphs, Mobbs, LeDoux's survival-circuit revision) hit back with large-scale natural-video machine-learning studies revealing ~20+ cross-culturally recognizable vocal/facial expression blends and conserved subcortical defensive/appetitive circuits in animals—pointing toward a middle-ground 'functional emotion state' view separating conserved subcortical survival circuits from culturally constructed conscious feeling labels.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Commercial 'emotion AI' and applied HCI papers uncritically deploy Ekman's six-category facial-expression classifiers as objective readouts of internal mental states, ignoring the 2019 PSPI consensus audit showing that people scowl in anger only a minority of the time and frequently scowl in concentration or gas pain. Conversely, strict constructionist papers often minimize conserved subcortical mammalian survival circuits (amygdala–PAG defensive states) by conflating human verbal emotion labels with subcortical affective states.

historical_evolution.milestone: Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen report cross-cultural facial-expression recognition in Papua New Guinea, establishing Basic Emotion Theory and the Facial Action Coding System (FACS); Jaak Panksepp maps seven mammalian subcortical affective circuits.

Lisa Feldman Barrett challenges biological 'natural kinds' of emotion, introducing Conceptual Act Theory and later the predictive Theory of Constructed Emotion ('How Emotions Are Made,' 2017) grounded in allostasis and interoception.

Siegel et al. (2018) and Barrett et al. (2019) demonstrate massive autonomic and facial degeneracy; Alan Cowen and Dacher Keltner publish large-scale naturalistic studies claiming 24–27 cross-cultural expression dimensions across facial, vocal, and bodily channels.

Ralph Adolphs, David Anderson, and Joseph LeDoux sharpen a tripartite synthesis distinguishing conserved subcortical 'emotion/survival states' from cortical predictive construction of conscious 'feelings' and communicative displays.

theory.falsification_criteria: Basic Emotion Theory is falsified if no reliable, context-invariant autonomic, neural, or facial signature distinguishes canonical categories above chance in naturalistic, non-posed, cross-cultural samples; strict Constructionism is falsified if pre-linguistic infants or isolated cultures lacking specific emotion vocabulary spontaneously display specific, stereotyped physiological–expressive profiles to specific ecological contingencies.
theory.stealth_support: Your study finds high cross-cultural preservation of context-linked facial/vocal expressions even in non-WEIRD or ancient artworks (Basic/Semantic Space) — OR finds zero consistent autonomic/facial fingerprints within an emotion category (Constructed Emotion).
theory.stealth_refute: Your study shows forced-choice English emotion labels artificially inflate 'universal' facial recognition in small-scale societies (challenging Ekman), OR shows free-response cross-cultural video ratings cluster reliably into >15 distinct universal emotion dimensions (challenging pure valence-arousal construction).

steelman.settled_ground: Both sides agree that real-world emotional expressions are far more varied and context-dependent than 1970s posed six-category textbook photos, that commercial 'emotion AI' reading inner feelings strictly from webcam scowls is scientifically invalid, and that mammals possess conserved subcortical defensive/appetitive circuits.
steelman.theory_a_case: Meta-analyses of autonomic physiology (Siegel et al. 2018) and facial muscle movements (Barrett et al. 2019 PSPI) demolished strict 1-to-1 biological fingerprints—people scowl in anger under 30 percent of the time and scowl in concentration or pain; free-labeling tests in non-Western Himba and Trobriand communities dissolve forced-choice universality…

steelman.rival_b_name: Modern Basic Emotion & High-Dimensional Semantic-Space Theory (Ekman-Cowen-Keltner-Adolphs)
steelman.rival_b_case: Modernized Basic Emotion Theory never claimed rigid 100-percent deterministic reflexes: affective states are probabilistic evolutionary adaptations (Adolphs & Anderson's functional emotion states) spanning ~20+ graded vocal/facial profiles that generalize across distant human societies and even pre-linguistic infants.
steelman.rival_b_hardest: Even high-dimensional facial classifiers perform far worse on spontaneous real-life videos stripped of situational context than on posed or context-rich clips, and intracranial/fMRI meta-analyses still fail to locate single dedicated brain regions unique to anger, fear, or disgust.

episodes.label: Willpower on Trial — Ego Depletion & the Limited Willpower Resource Model, Baumeister's Radish Experiment, Gailliot's Glucose Fuel Tank, Carter's PET-PEESE Audit, the 23-Lab & 36-Lab Preregistered Replications & Expected Value of Control
episodes.notes: For fifteen years, one iconic laboratory demonstration—hungry volunteers resisting warm chocolate-chip cookies to eat bitter radishes, then quitting early on unsolvable puzzles—convinced textbooks, executives, and scientists worldwide that human willpower runs like a finite muscle fueled by blood glucose. This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Ego Depletion and the Strength Model of Self-Control on forensic trial across all eight live-verified landmark papers—from Baumeister, Bratslavsky, Muraven, and Tice's 1998 manifesto, Gailliot et al.'s 2007 blood-glucose fuel-tank claim, and Hagger et al.'s 2010 Psychological Bulletin meta-analysis reporting d = 0.62, directly into the five-front reckoning that reshaped modern behavioral science: Inzlicht and Schmeichel's 2012 motivational-shift Process Model, Carter et al.'s 2015 PET-PEESE publication-bias collapse, Hagger et al.'s 2016 23-laboratory 2,141-participant Registered Replication Report returning d = 0.04, Lee et al.'s 2016 sequential-task adequacy audit, and Vohs et al.'s 2021 proponent-led 36-laboratory 3,531-participant paradigmatic test returning a confirmatory null of d = 0.06 with Bayesian evidence favoring the null by four to one. Pause twice for Python-verified calculations—first proving from human brain stoichiometry that ten minutes of intense prefrontal effort burns barely 5.8 milligrams (0.022 kilocalories) of extra glucose, producing a blood-sugar drop more than 128 times smaller than commercial glucometer error, and second demonstrating mathematically how a 25-participant-per-cell significance filter automatically manufactures published averages near d = 0.68 out of a near-zero true effect of d = 0.06—before engineering a high-powered mixed-crossover protocol separating finite resource collapse from Expected Value of Control and multi-hour prefrontal fatigue, alongside a sixteen-fingerprint stealth field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Ego Depletion & Limited Willpower Resource Model
theory.core_claim: Roy Baumeister's Strength Model of Self-Control proposes that acts of volition, impulse inhibition, and difficult choice draw upon a single, domain-general, finite metabolic resource (later hypothesized to be blood glucose) that becomes temporarily depleted ('ego depletion'), impairing subsequent unrelated self-control.
theory.verdict_2026: Ego depletion became one of the centerpiece casualties of psychology's Replication Crisis and remains heavily challenged and theoretically replaced in 2026. Carter and McCullough (2014) exposed severe small-study publication bias in the original 2010 meta-analysis; the 23-lab Registered Replication Report (Hagger et al. 2016, N = 2,141) found an effect statistically indistinguishable from zero (d = 0.04); the massive 36-lab multi-site test led by Baumeister's own collaborator Kathleen Vohs (Psychological Science 2021, N = 3,531) found at best a tiny, fragile effect (d = 0.06–0.08) failing preregistered significance; and the blood-glucose refueling mechanism was conclusively refuted (Kurzban 2010; Vadillo et al. 2016). Modern self-control science (Inzlicht, Shenhav, Kurzban) replaces the 'fuel tank' metaphor with opportunity-cost, motivational-shift, and Expected Value of Control (EVC) models of mental fatigue.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Management, behavioral-economics, and health-psychology papers still routinely cite Baumeister's 1998 chocolate-radish study or the discredited 'hungry judge' parole study (which was heavily confounded by case scheduling order) as proof of a literal willpower battery, ignoring the Hagger 2016 and Vohs 2021 multi-lab null/near-null replications and the collapse of the glucose hypothesis.

historical_evolution.milestone: Roy Baumeister, Ellen Bratslavsky, Mark Muraven, and Dianne Tice launch Ego Depletion with the famous radish-vs-cookie persistence experiment; Gailliot et al. (2007) claim blood glucose is the physical willpower fuel.

Robert Kurzban dismantles the glucose-depletion physiology on brain-energetics grounds; Evan Carter and Michael McCullough re-analyze Hagger's 2010 meta-analysis and reveal severe publication bias driving apparent d ~ 0.62 down near zero.

Hagger et al. (2016; 23 labs) finds d = 0.04; Kathleen Vohs et al. (2021; 36 labs, 3,531 participants) runs a gold-standard multi-lab sequential-task test finding d = 0.06 (non-significant under preregistered criteria), confirming the classic lab effect is negligible or absent.

Cognitive-fatigue research shifts to Michael Inzlicht's Process Model (motivation/attention shift from 'have-to' to 'want-to'), Amitai Shenhav's Expected Value of Control (dACC), and genuine prolonged-work neurochemical fatigue (e.g., prefrontal glutamate buildup over 6+ hours, Wiehler et al. 2022).

rivals: Process Model of Self-Control / Motivational Shift (Inzlicht & Schmeichel)
Opportunity-Cost & Expected Value of Control (EVC) Theory (Kurzban / Shenhav)
Implicit Theories of Willpower (Job, Dweck & Walton)
theory.falsification_criteria: The limited metabolic willpower-tank model is falsified when monetary incentives, motivational framing, or non-caloric sweet mouth rinses completely eliminate sequential-task performance drops without replenishing glucose, and when preregistered multi-lab sequential self-control experiments yield effect sizes indistinguishable from zero.
theory.stealth_support: Your study observes significant sequential self-control impairment surviving pre-registered high-powered replication even when participant motivation and incentives are held high.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study finds near-zero depletion effect sizes (d < 0.10) in pre-registered multilab protocols or shows cash incentives/interesting tasks instantly erase 'depletion' without glucose replenishment.

head_to_head.theory_a: Limited-Resource Strength Model of Ego Depletion (Baumeister–Vohs)
head_to_head.rival_b: Motivational-Shift / Expected Value of Control Theory (Inzlicht–Kurzban–Shenhav)
head_to_head.theory_a_prediction: Sustained cognitive exertion depletes a finite biological/cognitive tank, impairing subsequent unrelated self-control performance even when high monetary rewards are offered for the second task.
head_to_head.rival_b_prediction: Mental fatigue reflects an adaptive shift in perceived opportunity cost (wanting to switch to leisure/reward), so raising stakes on Task 2 immediately restores baseline performance without rest or glucose.
head_to_head.confounder_trap: Small-sample (n=20/cell) un-preregistered lab tasks with flexible stopping rules and failure to control for boredom/time-on-task disengagement.
head_to_head.minimum_decisive_protocol: Pre-registered high-powered (N>=400/arm) 2x2 crossover crossing prolonged high-effort exertion (>30 min) against high vs. low monetary Task-2 incentives and double-blind glucose vs. artificial-sweetener rinse.

diverging_predictions.observable: 1. Brief 5–10 min Sequential Task (Low Stakes, Preregistered High-N)
diverging_predictions.theory_a: Medium-to-large cross-domain impairment (d ≈ 0.40–0.62).
diverging_predictions.rival_b: Near-zero or tiny effect (d ≤ 0.08) unless Task 1 triggers boredom/aversive shift; no literal capacity exhaustion.

diverging_predictions.observable: 2. High Task-2 Monetary Incentive (USD 50 Performance Bonus After Prolonged Exertion)
diverging_predictions.theory_a: Impairment PERSISTS (zero or small interaction): an empty tank or exhausted muscle cannot perform at full capacity simply because you wave cash at it!
diverging_predictions.rival_b: Impairment VANISHES IMMEDIATELY (d → 0, large Exertion × Incentive interaction!): Raising Value(reward) outweighs opportunity cost inside dACC EVC, restoring full Task-2 accuracy and RT!

diverging_predictions.observable: 3. Double-Blind Oral Glucose Swish-and-Spit Rinse vs. Swallowed Glucose vs. Artificial Sweetener
diverging_predictions.theory_a: Only SWALLOWED glucose restores self-control (requires gastrointestinal absorption into bloodstream to refuel PFC); swish-and-spit produces zero benefit!
diverging_predictions.rival_b: Swish-and-spit glucose EQUALS swallowed glucose (both outperform artificial sweetener) via oral sweet-taste → striatal dopamine motivational signaling, with zero blood-glucose mediation!

diverging_predictions.observable: 4. Switch From Boring "Have-To" Task 1 to Intrinsically Rewarding "Want-To" Self-Control Task 2
diverging_predictions.theory_a: Impairment PERSISTS (resource is domain-general and blind to whether Task 2 feels fun or tedious).
diverging_predictions.rival_b: Impairment REVERSES / DISAPPEARS: Shifting from aversive labor to intrinsically valued engagement aligns with post-Task-1 motivational shift!

diverging_predictions.observable: 5. Neural Dynamics During Task 2 (dACC ERN / Pupillometry / lPFC MRS Glutamate)
diverging_predictions.theory_a: Global prefrontal hypo-activation + drop in systemic peripheral blood glucose (5–10 mg/dL).
diverging_predictions.rival_b: dACC conflict-monitoring ERN drops under low stakes AND snaps immediately back to baseline under high stakes; zero systemic blood-glucose drop (<0.2 mg/dL).

episodes.label: Growth Mindset on Trial — Dweck & Leggett's Implicit Intelligence Theory, the 12,490-Student Nature National Experiment, 'Seed-and-Soil' Heterogeneity vs. Sisk & Macnamara's Meta-Analytic, COI & Manipulation-Check Audit
episodes.notes: Can a 45-minute online lesson teaching students that intelligence grows like a muscle genuinely transform national high-school achievement—or did one of modern psychology's most celebrated movements outrun its causal evidence? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts Carol Dweck's Growth Mindset Theory on forensic trial across all five verified landmark papers: starting with Dweck and Ellen Leggett's 1988 Psychological Review social-cognitive model (highlighting its often-forgotten confidence-and-setback boundary condition) and David Yeager and colleagues' 2019 Nature National Study of Learning Mindsets across 12,490 US ninth-graders (+0.10 GPA among lower-achieving students and a 33-to-36 percent rise in advanced math enrollment inside peer-supportive schools). Then cross-examine the counter-evidence head-on: Victoria Sisk and Brooke Macnamara's 2018 twin meta-analyses spanning 423,070 students (r = 0.10, d = 0.08), Yeager and Dweck's 2020 American Psychologist 'seed-and-soil' heterogeneity defense, and Macnamara and Burgoyne's 2023 Psychological Bulletin audit of 63 trials (N = 97,672), showing average gains shrink to d = 0.02–0.05 (statistically indistinguishable from zero) once publication bias, missing manipulation checks, and author financial incentives are audited. Pause twice for Python-verified calculations—first translating r = 0.10 and d = 0.02–0.11 into distributional overlap, NNT, cost per standard deviation, and the exact seed-and-soil mixture identity, and second exposing why cluster design effects (15.9x) and 2x2 interactions leave typical 400-student classroom trials with just 8 percent power—before designing a COI-free 18,000-student three-arm adversarial protocol and a 16-fingerprint stealth field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Growth Mindset Theory (Dweck) & Intervention Transfer
theory.core_claim: Carol Dweck's Implicit Theories of Intelligence framework posits that students who hold an incremental 'growth mindset' (believing intelligence is malleable through effort and strategy) outperform those with an entity 'fixed mindset,' and that brief scalable mindset interventions causally raise academic achievement.
theory.verdict_2026: Growth Mindset Theory has undergone a sharp reality check and scaling revision between 2018 and 2026. While the landmark National Study of Learning Mindsets (Yeager et al., Nature 2019; N = 12,490 ninth graders) detected a small, statistically reliable GPA boost specifically among lower-achieving students in peer-supportive schools (~0.10 GPA points, d ~ 0.11), comprehensive meta-analyses by Sisk et al. (2018) and Macnamara & Burgoyne (Psychological Bulletin 2023) found very weak overall correlation between mindset and grades (r ~ 0.10), tiny average intervention effects (d ~ 0.05–0.08) that shrink close to zero after correcting for publication bias and researcher conflicts of interest, and null results in large independent UK/international RCTs. Dweck and Yeager have consequently revised the theory from a universal achievement booster into a 'mindset-plus-supportive-context' (heterogeneity) hypothesis whose practical magnitude remains fiercely contested.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Education-policy papers and school interventions routinely cite early small-sample laboratory praise studies (Mueller & Dweck 1998) as if a 45-minute online module delivers large, universal grade gains, ignoring both tiny real-world average effect sizes (d < 0.08) and the fact that telling struggling students to 'just try harder' without structural resources or effective pedagogy can backfire.

historical_evolution.milestone: Carol Dweck and Ellen Leggett formalize implicit entity vs. incremental theories of intelligence; Claudia Mueller and Dweck (1998) publish the famous 'praise for effort vs. praise for intelligence' laboratory studies.
Dweck's bestseller 'Mindset' sparks massive global adoption across K-12 schools and corporations, accompanied by small-to-medium intervention trials reporting substantial GPA boosts.

Brooke Macnamara and Victoria Sisk (Psychological Science 2018) publish two meta-analyses showing r = 0.10 and d = 0.08 overall; David Yeager and Dweck counter with the preregistered National Study of Learning Mindsets (Nature 2019) demonstrating modest, context-moderated gains in lower-achieving students.

A fierce Psychological Bulletin adversarial exchange pits Macnamara & Burgoyne (2023, arguing bias-corrected effects approach zero) against Burnette, Bryan, Yeager, and Tipton (2023, emphasizing heterogeneous context-dependent effects in supportive classrooms).

episodes.label: Bodies, Hubs, and Disembodied Minds — Barsalou's Grounded Cognition & Perceptual Symbol Systems, van Dantzig's Modality-Switch Costs, Patterson's ATL Hub-and-Spoke Neuropsychology, Pulvermüller's Motor Idiom Somatotopy, Mahon & Caramazza's Apraxia Critique, Bedny's Congenital Blindness, Wagenmakers' 17-Lab Replication Crash & the LLM Paradox
episodes.notes: When you read the words 'cinnamon', 'hammer', 'kick the habit', or 'justice', does your brain manipulate disembodied algebraic symbols in a mental dictionary, or must it physically reenact sensory, motor, and visceral experiences inside visual, premotor, and olfactory cortices? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Embodied and Grounded Cognition on trial against Amodal Symbolic Representation, Hub-and-Spoke clinical neurology, and modern disembodied Large Language Models. Trace Lawrence Barsalou's Perceptual Symbol Systems, Saskia van Dantzig's cross-task perceptual-to-conceptual modality-switch costs, Véronique Boulenger and Friedemann Pulvermüller's fMRI demonstration of motor-strip somatotopy during abstract idiom comprehension, and Karalyn Patterson, Peter Nestor, and Timothy Rogers's semantic-dementia blueprint uniting sensory-motor spokes with a transmodal anterior temporal lobe hub. Then cross-examine strong embodiment against three formidable counterstrikes: Bradford Mahon and Alfonso Caramazza's limb-apraxia double dissociation exposing motor BOLD signals as downstream post-conceptual spreading activation, Marina Bedny and Rebecca Saxe's proof that congenitally blind adults preserve rich visual-verb semantics while repurposing occipital cortex for combinatorial syntax, and Eric-Jan Wagenmakers's 17-laboratory, 1,894-participant Registered Replication Report collapsing Fritz Strack's classic pen-in-mouth facial-feedback effect from 0.82 to 0.03 points. Pause twice for worked quantitative calculations auditing single-trial modality-switch variance, the 159-millisecond white-matter cascade from anterior temporal hub to primary motor cortex, and TOST equivalence power across 1,770 concept pairs in congenital limb absence and chronometric TMS.

theory.canonical_title: Embodied & Grounded Cognition vs. Amodal Symbolic Representation
theory.core_claim: Embodied and Grounded Cognition (Barsalou, Varela, Lakoff) holds that human concepts, language, and reasoning are constitutively grounded in sensorimotor simulations and bodily states rather than manipulated as abstract, amodal symbols in a disembodied language of thought (Fodor, Pylyshyn).
theory.verdict_2026: By 2026, the sharpest empirical cleavage runs between weak/moderate grounded cognition—now well-supported via hub-and-spoke semantic architectures (Patterson & Lambon Ralph) linking amodal anterior-temporal convergence hubs with modality-specific sensory-motor spokes—and radical/social-metaphor embodiment, which suffered catastrophic replication failures (e.g., Strack's pen-in-mouth facial feedback failing Wagenmakers' 17-lab Many Labs test, warm-cup social warmth failing Lynott et al., and power-posing hormones failing Ranehill/Garrison). Meanwhile, the stunning semantic competence of disembodied text-only Large Language Models (LLMs) has dramatically reinvigorated distributional/amodal symbolic accounts of abstract meaning (Mahon & Hickok), keeping the boundary between sensorimotor grounding and statistical-symbolic structure fiercely contested.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely treat secondary fMRI activation of motor cortex during action-verb reading ('kick') as proof that motor simulation is causally necessary for semantic comprehension, committing Bradford Mahon and Alfonso Caramazza's 'spreading activation fallacy' (downstream epiphenomenal motor spillover after amodal conceptual access). Authors also lump discredited social-priming embodiment gimmicks together with rigorously established perception–action coupling.

historical_evolution.milestone: Francisco Varela, Evan Thompson, and Eleanor Rosch publish 'The Embodied Mind'; Lawrence Barsalou formalizes Perceptual Symbol Systems challenging classical Fodorian amodal symbolic AI.

Bradford Mahon and Alfonso Caramazza publish their influential critique demonstrating that sensorimotor cortex activation during conceptual tasks does not falsify amodal conceptual hubs (citing apraxia dissociations).

Large-scale registered replication reports topple flagship 'conceptual-metaphor embodiment' findings (warm coffee -> interpersonal warmth, pen-in-mouth smiling, power posing -> testosterone), forcing a retreat from radical social embodiment.

Hub-and-spoke semantic neurobiology (Ralph, Binder) converges on hybrid multimodal+amodal representations, while text-only LLMs re-ignite the Symbol Grounding debate by acquiring rich relational world structure without bodies.

episodes.label: The Pleistocene Swiss Army Knife on Trial — Tooby & Cosmides's Massive Modularity, Wason Cheater Detection & Barrett-Kurzban Enzymatic Cognition vs. Fodor's Abduction Critique, Sperber's Relevance Theory, Anderson's 1,469-Study Neural Reuse & Heyes's Cognitive Gadgets
episodes.notes: Is the human mind a Pleistocene Swiss Army knife packed with hundreds of genetically hardwired computational modules—dedicated circuits for spotting social-contract cheaters, estimating kin relatedness, and calibrating mate value—or does a developmentally plastic neocortex recycle multipurpose neural circuits to assemble specialized 'cognitive gadgets' through cumulative culture? This five-act adversarial deep dive places John Tooby and Leda Cosmides's Massive Modularity Hypothesis on rigorous courtroom trial against neuroconstructivist neural reuse, pragmatic Relevance Theory, and cultural evolutionary psychology. Reconstruct why Tooby and Cosmides launched their 1992 insurgency against the 'Standard Social Science Model,' how computational combinatorial explosion motivated domain-specific adaptive specializations, how Cosmides's classic 1989 Wason Selection Task experiments boosted conditional accuracy from under twenty-five percent on abstract rules to seventy-five percent on social-exchange contracts, and how H. Clark Barrett and Robert Kurzban's 2006 Psychological Review synthesis modernized modularity into functional 'enzymatic computation.' Then confront five formidable counterstrikes: Dan Sperber's 1995 proof that pragmatic Relevance Theory elicits high Wason accuracy on benign non-social rules, Jerry Fodor's 2000 demonstration that central human abduction defies modular input routing, Michael Anderson's 2010 meta-analysis of 1,469 neuroimaging experiments proving every cortical parcel is reused across disparate cognitive domains, and Cecilia Heyes's 2018-2019 case that mindreading, imitation, and literacy are culturally inherited cognitive gadgets. Walk through Python-verified Wason odds ratios, genomic-versus-synaptome bit-budget deficits, and Shannon cortical diversity math, culminating in a pre-registered cross-cultural neuroimaging Crucial Experiment and an epistemic field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Massive Modularity Hypothesis (Santa Barbara Evolutionary Psychology)
theory.core_claim: The human mind is not a domain-general blank-slate processor, but a 'Swiss Army knife' comprising hundreds or thousands of genetically specified, informationally specialized cognitive modules (such as cheater detection, kin estimation, and mate-value calculators) sculpted by natural selection in the Pleistocene Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness (EEA).
theory.verdict_2026: While evolutionary psychology's foundational rejection of pure cultural blank-slatism and recognition of evolved perceptual, social, and motivational predispositions are widely accepted, the strict 'Massive Modularity' architecture of Tooby, Cosmides, and Pinker is heavily challenged and under broad revision in 2026. Neuroanatomy and developmental biology (Karmiloff-Smith, Buller, Anderson's 'neural reuse,' Barrett's 'evolutionary developmental psychology') contradict hardwired Pleistocene cortical organs: human neocortex exhibits extreme developmental plasticity, massive gene-for-structure conservation, and continuous neural recycling of domain-general circuits, while cultural evolution (Henrich, Heyes's 'cognitive gadgets') proves that flagship supposedly innate modules—reading, theory of mind, causal reasoning, imitation—are largely culturally assembled atop modest domain-general cognitive starter kits.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely commit a false dichotomy between 'blank-slate social constructivism' and 'hardwired Pleistocene Swiss-Army-knife modules,' ignoring developmental canalization, cultural niche construction, and neural reuse. Empirical evolutionary-psychology papers also frequently present single-culture WEIRD college-student preferences as universal Pleistocene adaptations without testing hunter-gatherer variation or phylogenetic homology.

historical_evolution.milestone: Jerry Fodor proposes peripheral input modularity while keeping central cognition non-modular; Leda Cosmides, John Tooby, and Jerome Barkow ('The Adapted Mind,' 1992) radicalize modularity across central reasoning via the Wason cheater-detection task.

Jerry Fodor ('The Mind Doesn't Work That Way') and David Buller ('Adapting Minds') publish devastating theoretical and empirical critiques exposing the 'frame/routing problem' and weak evidence for innate central modules.

Michael Anderson's 'neural reuse' meta-analysis proves brain regions serve diverse domain-general roles; Cecilia Heyes ('Cognitive Gadgets,' 2018) and Joseph Henrich demonstrate cultural evolution builds human cognitive specializations.

Second-generation evolutionary cognitive science (H. Clark Barrett, Pietraszewski, Wertz) largely abandons strict Fodorian/Swiss-Army-knife massive modularity in favor of flexible, developmentally plastic, culturally scaffolded evolved mechanisms.
